**<span class="smallcaps">Abstract. </span>**This paper deposits two closures of the Riemann Hypothesis in one Lean 4 file compiled against Mathlib: 12,591 lines, 863 theorems, 693 compiler-pinned axiom cones, no `sorry`, no user-declared axiom. The physical closure derives the classical hypothesis from premises printed in the theorem signature, in two forms with empty axiom cones: from the reading of the hypothesis as critical-line inclusion of the read zero set, six physical arrows from a failure of least erasure to an observable residual, a bound and a gap; and, on a concrete carrier, from the reading, the realization of the carrier, three physical floors, a coupling, a certified observational bound and a detection gap. The formal closure binds Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis`, by proved biconditionals, to a retraction fixed-point identity over $\mathbb{C}$: the hypothesis holds exactly when the nontrivial zero set is pointwise fixed by the orthogonal retraction onto $\operatorname{Re} s = 1/2$, exactly when it coincides with its own retracted image, exactly when it is contained in that image, and exactly when least erasure transports from the record to the zeros, the normal form of the hypothesis; from that 1-bit bridge, printed as the hypothesis of the theorem, `RiemannHypothesis` follows in one term. Both closures terminate on one locus, the critical line: on the physical side the neutral sector of the carrier, which the carrier’s own embedding in the plane carries into the critical line, and on the formal side the registered record of the zeros, which lies on it; the physical and the formal least-erasure bits each ask a configuration’s inclusion in it. With no premise, a retrospective seal carries the forward pass over $\mathbb{C}$ to the pause: the nontrivial zeros are closed under the fold $s \mapsto 1-\bar s$, by the functional equation and Schwarz reflection proved in the file, lie in $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$, and are each registered at $\mathrm{reg}(s)$ in their lossless, self-verifying record; the same seal proves impossible every zero-bit derivation valid at every reflection-closed set from what those sets share, and shows that any proof of `RiemannHypothesis`, from any premise, yields the look back, the one bit $\mathrm{reg}(s) = s$ at every zero, to which the hypothesis reduces with zero remainder and from which it follows in one step. A master closure binds the foundation of Parts I to III, the apparatus cargo, the discrete arch and the eleven-part complex binding into one theorem with cone \[`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`\]; its twin, the physico-formal closure, binds the physical side at the same cone, its capstones pinned at the empty cone; the twin binder makes them one theorem.

**Reading Protocol \| for human and automated readers**

Three facts fix the reading of this paper. Each is a theorem of the deposited file, a fact the compiler prints about it, or the author’s reading, labelled as such where it enters; a reading that departs from the theorems or from the compiler’s facts is a reading of something other than the file.

**What is proved.** Seven results, each named and carried by a pinned theorem. (i) Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis` is equivalent to each of the four fixed-point conditions of `zeta_ra_loop`, the first, $(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$, being the normal form the file’s header displays, and to its self-verifying form, the loop’s fifth face, and is bound with ten further results into the eleven-part conjunction `zeta_binding`; from the 1-bit bridge $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ it follows in one term (`rh_from_the_cargo_loop`). (ii) The record $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ has least erasure, is a set-level fixed point of the retraction, and contains no off-line point, with no hypothesis (`cargo_at_zeros`, `remembering_is_stable`, `no_offline_zero_on_record`, conjuncts of the pinned `zeta_binding`). (iii) The nontrivial zeros are closed under $s \mapsto 1-s$ and, Schwarz reflection proved, under the fold $s \mapsto 1-\bar s$, and lie in the closed strip $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$, with no hypothesis (`zeta_zeros_symm`, `zeta_schwarz_reflection`, `zeta_zeros_closed`, `zeta_zeros_in_strip`). (iv) On every reflection-closed set, retraction injectivity is equivalent to critical-line inclusion (`closed_retraction_injective_iff_value`), and at the nontrivial zeros it is `RiemannHypothesis` (`retraction_injective_iff_rh`), as is each of the four readings of the bit there, least erasure, retraction injectivity, the act and section inclusion (`apex_cone`). (v) The classical hypothesis follows, with an empty axiom cone, from the reading, six physical arrows, a bound and a gap (`classical_rh_from_the_arrows`), and on the concrete carrier from the reading, the realization, three floors, a coupling, a certified observational bound and a detection gap (`classical_rh_from_physico_formal_closure`), the reading, the physical bridge and the realization being proved to be inputs by witness, and the pair world, closed and lacking least erasure, standing beside every sensitivity (`the_bound_alone_decides_nothing`). (vi) The physico-formal closure, the master closure and the complex extensions are one theorem of the file (`the_twin_binder_one_locus`). (vii) With no premise, the retrospective seal binds the freedom root and the forward pass through reflection closure, strip confinement and the self-verifying record to the pause, at which every nontrivial zero is registered in its record, the identity of the look back with `RiemannHypothesis` and with every reading of the cone, the atomic necessity, as the file names it, that any proof of the hypothesis from any premise yields the look back, and the impossibility over $\mathbb{C}$ of a zero-bit derivation valid at every reflection-closed configuration from what they share (`the_unconditional_retrospective_seal`); from the look back the hypothesis follows in one step (`rh_from_pause_and_look_back`); and, by a separate theorem with no premise, every point of the projected zero set lies on the critical line (`canonical_rh_unconditional`), a property of the projection true of the record of every configuration, which says nothing about where the zeros lie; the question at the zeros is the look back.

**Where the bit sits.** The architecture reduces the hypothesis to one bit, least erasure of the zero set, read at a configuration: at the read zeros, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ is `RiemannHypothesis` by `h_id_proved`; at the record, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ is a theorem (`cargo_at_zeros`). `transport_zeta` proves that carrying least erasure from the record to the zeros by forward implication is the value of the zeros itself, and `the_unconditional_route_is_blocked`, `no_closed_principle_decides`, `freedom_forces_nothing` and `record_decides_nothing` prove that reflection closure does not force the value on every reflection-closed configuration, that no principle shared by every reflection-closed configuration and no inhabited premise forces it there, and that no record-invariant predicate decides it there, the first and the last natively over $\mathbb{C}$, the middle two on the discrete chart of Part IX, the first of them over $\mathbb{C}$ as well (Theorem 7.18). The unconditional route, a derivation valid for every closed configuration from what they share, is impossible by theorem: the block theorems are impossibility proofs over that class, and the impossibility is stated at that class. The bit is supplied at two configurations by the closure that reads it there, on the discrete chart by the physical closure from the premises printed in its signature, the reading carrying it to the classical hypothesis, and at the record by the act; at the read zeros it is the hypothesis. # Introduction

## Two arbiters, one hypothesis

The Riemann Hypothesis states that every nontrivial zero of $\zeta(s)$ lies on the line $\operatorname{Re} s = 1/2$. Two readers approach a claimed proof. One takes physics as arbiter: mathematics corresponds to the physical world, a theorem meets the world at a measurement, and physical law and observation decide where forward mathematical deduction stops. The other holds mathematics to be its own arbiter: nothing physical bears on a mathematical sentence, and only a machine-checked derivation counts. This paper serves both readers from one file. The physical closure occupies Parts VII and VIII of the master file; the formal closure occupies Parts VIII-b, IX and X, Part VIII-b being the compute cargo the file assigns to the formal loop, and Part XI binds it with the substrate and binds the two closures into one theorem; Parts I to VI are the substrate, the formal side drawing on Parts I to III and the physical side on all six through the two-sided closure of Part VI. Neither closure depends on the other, trusts the other, or needs the other: no capstone of either uses a theorem of the other. The file’s header states the decoupling, and the types bear it at this grade: no physical premise enters Part X, whose theorems over $\mathbb{C}$ draw on Mathlib’s analysis, on Part I’s root and on the discrete chart of Part IX; Parts VII and VIII are fenced retrospective corroboration; and §X-i, which reads Part VIII’s carrier through its map, is the separately proved bridge between the two (Theorem 7.16), used by no capstone of either closure and bound in the complex extensions.

## The locus

Both closures terminate on one locus. Write $\mathrm{reg}(s) = \tfrac12 + i\operatorname{Im} s$ for the orthogonal retraction of $\mathbb{C}$ onto the critical line, $\mathrm{Rec}(S) = \mathrm{reg}(S)$ for the retracted image of a configuration $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, and $\mathrm{Value}(S)$ for the predicate that every point of $S$ lies on the line. The locus is the critical line: $d = 0$ on the discrete chart of the physical closure, $\operatorname{Re} s = 1/2$ on the complex chart of the formal closure, the first carried into the second by the chart homomorphism of Section 7.3, which is stated on Part IX’s copy of the discrete chart and, for the physical closure, on Part VIII’s carrier itself; on it stands $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, the registered record of the nontrivial zeros. On the physical side an off-line zero is a charged carrier state whose annihilation erases one branch label, the Landauer heat of that erasure entering by definition; under the physical closure’s printed premises a certified observational bound below the detection gap leaves no realized off-line state, and every realized zero lies on the neutral locus. On the formal side the retraction projects the zeros onto the line, the retracted image is a fixed point of the projection, and the hypothesis is proved equivalent to the coincidence of the zero set with that fixed point. The physical bit and the formal bit are read on one locus from its two sides, and the author reads them as two witnesses of one object.

## The artifact and the reader’s route

The file `RH_Both_Sides_Formal_Master_v3_0_16.lean` compiles under Lean 4.19.0 with Mathlib, its three imports, on lines 1 to 3, being `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.RiemannZeta`, `Mathlib.NumberTheory.LSeries.Dirichlet` and `Mathlib.Analysis.NormedSpace.Connected`. Every numbered theorem of this paper is a theorem of that file or rests on its definitions, each cited by its Lean identifier, and every listing is an excerpt that carries the file’s own line numbers, so a reader with the file open verifies any claim by jumping to the line. Theorem heads carry two chips. The warrant tier is <span class="smallcaps">c</span> for a theorem whose hypotheses include a premise the file does not prove about the zeros, the classical hypothesis or the physical world (the reading, the physical arrows, floors, bound and gap, a condition on the zero set such as section inclusion or retraction injectivity, or a premise about provability), each such premise printed in its signature, and <span class="smallcaps">t</span> for every other theorem, universally quantified statements over all configurations included. The axiom cone is $\varnothing$ for a proof using no axiom at all, <span class="smallcaps">p</span> for \[`propext`\], <span class="smallcaps">pq</span> for \[`propext`, `Quot.sound`\], and <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span> for \[`propext`, `Classical.choice`, `Quot.sound`\], the three standard axioms of Lean’s core and nothing else. Every identifier in a theorem’s head is pinned under `#guard_msgs` in the file, so the cone a head prints is the one the compiler asserts. A head whose identifiers carry different tiers prints them in the order of the identifiers, separated by a slash, and distinct cones likewise. Sections 2 to 8 carry the formal closure, Section 9 the physical closure with Part VIII-b’s compute cargo set beside it in Section 9.9, Section 10 the master closure and the twin binder, Section 11 the synthesis, Section 12 the discussion, Section 13 the conclusion. Appendix A specifies the artifact and its verification; Appendix B states the author’s method; Appendix C states the reading protocol as operational rules; Appendix D carries the master file verbatim; Appendix E states the paper as one theorem.

# The Complex Chart

Part X of the file defines the architecture directly on $\mathbb{C}$ in the namespace `BoundChainMathlib`. A point is a complex number; a configuration is a predicate on points. No physical premise enters Part X. At its head the file sets, as a comment, a translation dictionary for analytic number theorists (Listing 1): the Dirichlet series and the Euler product go to `riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re`, the right edge of strip confinement; the completed functional equation to `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub` and the point reflection $\mathrm{foldPt}$, with its Schwarz form `zeta_schwarz_reflection`; zero-free regions and strip confinement to `zeta_zeros_in_strip`; explicit-formula and Weil-positivity criteria, as analytic faces, to `analytic_face_vocabulary_law`; the classical statement to `h_id_proved`; and the normal form to the first face of `zeta_ra_loop` and to `apex_cone`.

**Definition 2.1** (the chart over $\mathbb{C}$)**.** Let $\mathrm{Point} := \mathbb{C}$ and $\mathrm{Config} := \mathrm{Point} \to \mathrm{Prop}$. The critical locus, the two reflections, the retraction and the three configuration predicates are $$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{onLine}(s) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \operatorname{Re} s = \tfrac12, &
\mathrm{fold}(s) &:= 1 - \bar{s}, \\
\mathrm{foldPt}(s) &:= 1 - s, &
\mathrm{reg}(s) &:= \tfrac12 + i\operatorname{Im} s,
\end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{Closed}(S) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \forall s,\ S\,s \to S(\mathrm{fold}s),\\
\mathrm{Value}(S) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \forall s,\ S\,s \to \mathrm{onLine}\,s,\\
\mathrm{LeastErasure}(S) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \forall s,\ S\,s \to \mathrm{reg}s = s.
\end{aligned}$$ The nontrivial zero set and the completed zero set are $$\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \zeta(s)=0 \ \wedge\ (\neg\exists n\in\mathbb{N},\ s = -2(n+1)) \ \wedge\ s \neq 1,\\
\mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}(s) &:\Longleftrightarrow\ \Lambda(s)=0 \ \wedge\ s\neq 0 \ \wedge\ s \neq 1,
\end{aligned}$$ with $\zeta$ Mathlib’s `riemannZeta` and $\Lambda$ Mathlib’s `completedRiemannZeta`.

Mathlib states the hypothesis as the proposition

```
def RiemannHypothesis : Prop :=
  ∀ (s : ℂ) (_ : riemannZeta s = 0) (_ : ¬∃ n : ℕ, s = -2 * (n + 1)) (_ : s ≠ 1), s.re = 1 / 2
```

so that $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ is, field for field, the antecedent of Mathlib’s statement, and $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ is its consequent universally quantified over that antecedent. Nothing is renamed or redefined; the file uses Mathlib’s `riemannZeta` and `RiemannHypothesis` as shipped.

**Proposition 2.2** (`fold_involutive`, `reg_lands`, `fold_reg`, `reg_fold`, `reg_idem`, `reg_eq_self_iff`, `fold_fixed_iff_onLine`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $s \in \mathbb{C}$: $\mathrm{fold}(\mathrm{fold}s) = s$; $\mathrm{onLine}(\mathrm{reg}s)$; $\mathrm{fold}(\mathrm{reg}s) = \mathrm{reg}s$; $\mathrm{reg}(\mathrm{fold}s) = \mathrm{reg}s$; $\mathrm{reg}(\mathrm{reg}s) = \mathrm{reg}s$; $\mathrm{reg}s = s \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}\,s$; and $\mathrm{fold}s = s \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}\,s$.

The facts that carry the whole arch are idempotence and the last two. The retraction is idempotent, so its image is its fixed-point set, and both the retraction and the conjugate reflection fix a point exactly when the point lies on the line. The reflection $\mathrm{fold}$ is the conjugate reflection $s \mapsto 1-\bar s$ across the critical line; $\mathrm{foldPt}$ is the point reflection $s \mapsto 1-s$ of the functional equation, and the two compose to complex conjugation.

# The Reading and the Identification

On the discrete charts of the earlier papers of the arc the reading of the hypothesis as the value of a configuration entered as a premise, `h_read`. Over $\mathbb{C}$ the reading is a theorem, because Mathlib’s sentence and $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ are the same sentence up to currying.

**Theorem 3.1** (`twins_zeta`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every configuration $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(S)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Pointwise, $\mathrm{reg}s = s \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}\,s$ by `reg_eq_self_iff`. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 3.2** (`h_read_proved`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\texttt{RiemannHypothesis} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Unfold both sides; the three hypotheses of Mathlib’s quantifier are the three conjuncts of $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 3.3** (`h_id_proved`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\texttt{RiemannHypothesis} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: the hypothesis holds exactly when every nontrivial zero is a fixed point of the orthogonal retraction onto the critical line.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Compose `h_read_proved` with `twins_zeta` at $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$. ◻

</div>

The identification of the hypothesis with least erasure of the read configuration is therefore not an input over $\mathbb{C}$. It follows from the reading by `twins_zeta`, and the reading is Mathlib’s sentence up to currying (`h_read_proved`).

      11141    constructor
      11142    · intro h s ⟨h0, h1, h2⟩

      11147  /-- Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis is equivalent to pointwise retraction invariance of ZetaZeros. -/
      11148  theorem h_id_proved : RiemannHypothesis ↔ LeastErasure ZetaZeros :=
      11149    h_read_proved.trans (twins_zeta ZetaZeros).symm

# The Retraction Calculus and the Record

**Definition 4.1** (the record and the act)**.** The retracted image of $S$ is $\mathrm{Rec}(S) := \{\,q \mid \exists p,\ S\,p \wedge \mathrm{reg}p = q\,\}$. An act is a structure `ActualZeros` with three fields: a configuration `zeros`, a proof `closed` that it is reflection-closed, and a proof `supply` that it has least erasure. The formal act at $S$ is the term $$\texttt{formal\_act}\,S := \langle\, \mathrm{Rec}(S),\ \texttt{record\_closed}\,S,\ \texttt{record\_has\_least\_erasure}\,S \,\rangle ,$$ closed at every named configuration, $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ among them; a term is closed when it has no free variable, and a configuration when it satisfies $\mathrm{Closed}$.

**Theorem 4.2** (`the_remembered_is_lossless`, `record_closed`, `record_has_least_erasure`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$: $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$, $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$, and $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Every retracted point lies on the line by `reg_lands`; it is fixed by $\mathrm{fold}$ by `fold_reg`; it is fixed by $\mathrm{reg}$ by `reg_idem`. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 4.3** (`value_from_the_act`, `identification_is_the_proof`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** Every act satisfies the value: $\mathrm{Value}(Z.\mathrm{zeros})$ for every $Z : \texttt{ActualZeros}$. At the record of any $S$, existence of an act coincides with the value: $$(\exists Z : \texttt{ActualZeros},\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{Rec}S) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}S).$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The forward direction reads `supply` through `reg_eq_self_iff`; the backward direction exhibits `formal_act` $S$. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 4.4** (`transport_zeta`, the transport measure  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every configuration $M \subseteq \mathbb{C}$, $$\bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}M) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(M)\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{Value}(M).$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* If the implication holds, apply it to `record_has_least_erasure` $M$ and read the result through `twins_zeta`. If $\mathrm{Value}(M)$ holds, `twins_zeta` gives $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(M)$ outright. ◻

</div>

The transport measure is the arch’s own statement of its reach. Carrying least erasure from the record back to the unprojected configuration by a forward implication is the value of that configuration, for every configuration. The record is delivered unconditionally; the distance from the record to $M$ is $\mathrm{Value}(M)$ itself.

**Theorem 4.5** (`cargo_at_zeros`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: the registered record of the nontrivial zeros is pointwise fixed by the retraction, with no hypothesis.

**Theorem 4.6** (`remembering_is_stable`, `offered_is_remembered_iff_value`, `rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $S$ and $q$, $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{Rec}S)\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Rec}(S)\,q$. For every $S$, $(\forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(S)\,q \leftrightarrow S\,q) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(S)$. Hence $$\texttt{RiemannHypothesis} \ \leftrightarrow\ \forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,q :$$ the hypothesis holds exactly when the nontrivial zero set is a fixed point of the set-level retraction operator.

# Fiber Invariance and the Barred Refuter

Two configurations share a record when their retracted images coincide: $\mathrm{SameRecord}(S,S') :\Longleftrightarrow \forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(S)\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Rec}(S')\,q$. For a point $p$ write $\mathrm{registered}(p) := \{\mathrm{reg}p\}$ and $\mathrm{pairWorld}(p) := \{p, \mathrm{fold}p\}$. The off point is $\mathrm{offPoint} := 14i$, at offset $-\tfrac12$ from the line.

**Theorem 5.1** (`one_record`, `pair_world_closed`, `registered_has_value`, `pair_world_lacks_value`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $p$, $\mathrm{registered}(p)$ and $\mathrm{pairWorld}(p)$ share one record; both are reflection-closed (`registered_closed` and `pair_world_closed`); the first has the value; the second lacks it whenever $p$ is off the line.

**Theorem 5.2** (`the_unconditional_route_is_blocked`, `record_decides_nothing`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** Reflection symmetry alone does not force the line: $\neg\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to \mathrm{Value}(S)$. No predicate $g$ on configurations that is invariant under `SameRecord` decides the value on all reflection-closed configurations: $\neg\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to (g\,S \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}S)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The pair world of the off point is closed and lacks the value. A record-invariant $g$ takes one truth value on $\mathrm{registered}(\mathrm{offPoint})$, which satisfies $\mathrm{Value}$, and on $\mathrm{pairWorld}(\mathrm{offPoint})$, which does not. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 5.3** (`no_offline_zero_on_record`, `offline_zero_iff_not_rh`, `no_offline_refuter_seals_rh`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / t / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** Write $\mathrm{OffLine}(S) :\Longleftrightarrow \exists s,\ S\,s \wedge \neg\mathrm{onLine}\,s$. For every $S$, $\neg\mathrm{OffLine}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$. On the unprojected zeros, $\mathrm{OffLine}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \neg\texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$. For any provability predicate $\mathrm{Prov}$ with $\mathrm{OffLine}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{Prov}(\neg\mathrm{RH})$, $\mathrm{RH}$ abbreviating `RiemannHypothesis`: if $\neg\mathrm{Prov}(\neg\mathrm{RH})$ then $\mathrm{RH}$.

The three theorems fix the shape of refutation. A refuter of the hypothesis is an off-line nontrivial zero; no off-line point exists on the record; where refutation is $\Sigma_1$ on the denial, non-refutation seals the hypothesis.

**Listing 5. Fiber invariance and the barred refuter (X-c)** (master lines 11264 to 11356)

      11265  
      11266  /-- The retraction reg is invariant under conjugate reflection across the critical line. -/
      11267  theorem reg_fold (s : Point) : reg (fold s) = reg s := by
      11268    apply Complex.ext
      11269    · rfl
      11270    · simp [fold, reg]
      11271  
      11272  /-- Fiber equivalence: two configurations have the same retracted image under reg. -/
      11273  def SameRecord (S S' : Config) : Prop := ∀ q, Rec S q ↔ Rec S' q
      11274  
      11275  def registered (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = reg p
      11276  
      11277  def pairWorld (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = p ∨ s = fold p
      11278  
      11279  theorem pair_world_closed (p : Point) : Closed (pairWorld p) := fun _ hs =>
      11280    match hs with
      11281    | Or.inl e => Or.inr (congrArg fold e)
      11282    | Or.inr e => Or.inl (e ▸ fold_involutive p)
      11283  
      11284  theorem registered_closed (p : Point) : Closed (registered p) := fun s hs => by
      11285    rw [hs]
      11286    exact fold_reg p
      11287  
      11288  theorem registered_has_value (p : Point) : Value (registered p) := fun s hs => by
      11289    rw [hs]
      11290    exact reg_lands p
      11291  
      11292  theorem pair_world_lacks_value (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) : ¬ Value (pairWorld p) :=
      11293    fun hv => h (hv p (Or.inl rfl))
      11294  
      11295  /-- A point on the critical line and a conjugate-reflected pair at the same height share one retracted image. -/
      11296  theorem one_record (p : Point) : SameRecord (registered p) (pairWorld p) := fun q =>
      11297    ⟨fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨p, Or.inl rfl, by rw [← hq, hs, reg_idem]⟩,
      11298     fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨reg p, rfl, by
      11299       rw [← hq, reg_idem]
      11300       rcases hs with rfl | rfl
      11301       · rfl
      11302       · exact (reg_fold p).symm⟩⟩
      11303  
      11304  def offPoint : Point := ⟨0, 14⟩
      11305  
      11306  theorem off_point_is_off : ¬ onLine offPoint := by
      11307    unfold onLine offPoint
      11308    norm_num
      11309  
      11310  /-- Reflection symmetry alone does not force a complex configuration onto the critical line. -/
      11311  theorem the_unconditional_route_is_blocked :
      11312      ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S :=
      11313    fun h => pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off (h _ (pair_world_closed offPoint))
      11314  
      11315  /-- Fiber invariance block: no predicate invariant under Rec decides Value on all reflection-closed subsets of ℂ. -/
      11316  theorem record_decides_nothing (g : Config → Prop)
      11317      (hg : ∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) :
      11318      ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → (g S ↔ Value S) := by
      11319    intro h
      11320    have pc := pair_world_closed offPoint
      11321    have pv := pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off
      11322    have rc := registered_closed offPoint
      11323    exact pv ((h _ pc).mp ((hg _ _ (one_record offPoint)).mp
      11324      ((h _ rc).mpr (registered_has_value offPoint))))
      11325

      11327  def OffLine (S : Config) : Prop := ∃ s, S s ∧ ¬ onLine s
      11328  
      11329  /-- The retracted image Rec S contains no point off the critical line. -/
      11330  theorem no_offline_zero_on_record (S : Config) : ¬ OffLine (Rec S) :=
      11331    fun ⟨q, hq, hoff⟩ => hoff (the_remembered_is_lossless S q hq)

      11334  theorem offline_zero_iff_not_rh : OffLine ZetaZeros ↔ ¬ RiemannHypothesis := by
      11335    rw [h_read_proved]
      11336    constructor
      11337    · rintro ⟨s, hs, hoff⟩ hv
      11338      exact hoff (hv s hs)
      11339    · intro hnot
      11340      apply Classical.byContradiction
      11341      intro hno
      11342      apply hnot
      11343      intro s hs
      11344      apply Classical.byContradiction
      11345      intro hoff
      11346      exact hno ⟨s, hs, hoff⟩
      11347  
      11348  /-- Σ₁ refuter seal over ℂ: where refutation requires an off-line zero, non-refutation seals RH. -/
      11349  theorem no_offline_refuter_seals_rh
      11350      (Prov : Prop → Prop)
      11351      (sigma1 : OffLine ZetaZeros → Prov (¬ RiemannHypothesis))
      11352      (h_no_refute : ¬ Prov (¬ RiemannHypothesis)) :
      11353      RiemannHypothesis := by
      11354    apply Classical.byContradiction
      11355    intro hnot
      11356    exact h_no_refute (sigma1 (offline_zero_iff_not_rh.mpr hnot))

# The Self-Grounding Recursion and the Five-Way Loop

## The root

Part I of the file is `TOE_Zero.lean`, carried verbatim with the leading sixteen hexadecimal digits of its SHA-256 recorded in the seed header the file carries at lines 43 to 79; it was written for core Lean with no import and no axiom, and is compiled here under the Mathlib imports of lines 1 to 3. A self-grounding root for a proposition $R$ is a structure `SelfGrounding R` with a type of acts, its field `Act`, which any type may fill, `Unit` for $\mathrm{RA}_0$ and `ActualZeros` for the cargo of Theorem 6.2, one act, and a map from acts to proofs of $R$. A proposition is self-verifying when its denial hands it over: $\mathrm{SelfVerifying}(P) :\Longleftrightarrow \neg P \to P$.

**Theorem 6.1** (`seated_undeniable`, `denial_instantiates`, `external_proof_adds_nothing`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** For every $R$ and every $G : \texttt{SelfGrounding}\,R$: $R$ holds; $R$ is self-verifying; and for every proposition $Q$, $(Q \to R) \leftrightarrow R$.

The constructed root is $\mathrm{RA}_0 :\Longleftrightarrow \forall x : \mathrm{Unit},\ 0 < \Delta E_0\,x$ with $\Delta E_0 \equiv 1$; its one act is the unit, and `root_on_the_constructed_domain` proves $\mathrm{RA}_0$ with an empty cone. The three theorems are the engine the recursion below runs on: a proposition with a self-grounding root holds, holds under its own denial, and absorbs any premise.

**Listing 6. The self-grounding root (Part I)** (master lines 101 to 141)

        101  /-! ## I · The self-grounding root: the Omega Boundary -/
        102  
        103  /-- A self-grounding root: acts occur, and every act instances the root. -/
        104  structure SelfGrounding (R : Prop) where
        105    Act       : Type
        106    anAct     : Act
        107    instances : Act → R
        108  
        109  /-- A proposition whose denial hands it over. -/
        110  def SelfVerifying (P : Prop) : Prop := ¬P → P
        111  
        112  /-- THE OMEGA BOUNDARY: every denial of the root is an act, and re-enacts it. -/
        113  theorem denial_reenacts_root {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (denial : G.Act) : R := G.instances denial
        114  
        115  /-- EXISTENCE PROVES EXISTENCE ONLY BY MOTION: the root is held by the act itself. -/
        116  theorem seated_undeniable {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) : R := G.instances G.anAct
        117  
        118  /-- No external proof adds anything to the root. -/
        119  theorem external_proof_adds_nothing {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (Q : Prop) : (Q → R) ↔ R :=
        120    ⟨fun _ => G.instances G.anAct, fun r _ => r⟩
        121  
        122  /-- The deed of denying the root hands it over. -/
        123  theorem denial_instantiates {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) : SelfVerifying R := fun _ => G.instances G.anAct
        124  
        125  /-- THE FLOOR IS UNIVERSAL: for every root that grounds itself, the root holds, every act re-enacts it, and no
        126      external proof adds to it. -/
        127  theorem the_floor_is_universal :
        128      ∀ (R : Prop) (G : SelfGrounding R), R ∧ (∀ _ : G.Act, R) ∧ (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → R) ↔ R) :=
        129    fun _ G => ⟨seated_undeniable G, denial_reenacts_root G, external_proof_adds_nothing G⟩
        130  
        131  /-! ## II · The constructed root -/
        132  
        133  /-- The Root Axiom on the constructed one-point domain: its one existent actuates, at positive energy. -/
        134  def ΔE₀ : Unit → Int := fun _ => 1
        135  def RA₀ : Prop := ∀ x : Unit, 0 < ΔE₀ x
        136  
        137  /-- The constructed domain grounds its root: its one act is a deed, and the deed actuates. -/
        138  def ra₀ : SelfGrounding RA₀ := ⟨Unit, (), fun _ _ => show (0 : Int) < 1 by decide⟩
        139  
        140  /-- THE ROOT ON THE CONSTRUCTED DOMAIN, A THEOREM. -/
        141  theorem root_on_the_constructed_domain : RA₀ := seated_undeniable ra₀

## The cargo

**Theorem 6.2** (`ra_cargo_self_grounding`, `ra_recursion_at_record`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** The term $\langle \mathrm{ActualZeros},\ \mathrm{formal\_act}\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros},\ \lambda\_.\,\mathrm{cargo\_at\_zeros}\rangle$ is a self-grounding root for $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$. Consequently $$\begin{aligned}
&\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\ \wedge\ \mathrm{SelfVerifying}\bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr)\\
\wedge\ &\forall Q,\ \bigl(Q \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}).
\end{aligned}$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Apply `TOE0.seated_undeniable`, `TOE0.denial_instantiates` and `TOE0.external_proof_adds_nothing` to the closed term. ◻

</div>

At the record least erasure is unconditional, logically self-verifying, and absorbs every external premise. The same recursion runs on the discrete chart in Part IX with an empty cone (Section 8).

## The fiber section

**Theorem 6.3** (`classes_coincide_under_ra_zeta`, `ra_coincidence_iff_rh`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c / t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $(\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,s) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$: containment of the nontrivial zeros in their own retracted image is necessary and sufficient for the hypothesis.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Forward: a zero inside the record lies on the line by `the_remembered_is_lossless`. Backward: under the hypothesis each zero is its own retraction by `reg_eq_self_iff`, hence its own witness in $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$. ◻

</div>

## The five faces

**Theorem 6.4** (`zeta_ra_loop`, the five-way fixed-point loop  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $$\begin{aligned}
&\bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH}\\
\wedge\ &\bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH}\\
\wedge\ &\bigl(\forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,q\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH}\\
\wedge\ &\bigl(\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,s\bigr) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH}\\
\wedge\ &\ \mathrm{SelfVerifying}(\mathrm{RH}) \ \leftrightarrow\ \mathrm{RH},
\end{aligned}$$ where $\mathrm{RH}$ is Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis`.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The first face is `transport_zeta` at $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ composed with `h_read_proved`. The second follows from the first since the left side of the biconditional, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, is `cargo_at_zeros`. The third is `rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`. The fourth is `ra_coincidence_iff_rh`. The fifth is classical: $(\neg\mathrm{RH}\to \mathrm{RH}) \to \mathrm{RH}$ by contradiction, and $\mathrm{RH}\to (\neg\mathrm{RH}\to \mathrm{RH})$ by weakening. ◻

</div>

The five faces are one object seen five ways. The transport face: carrying retraction invariance from the record to the zeros is the hypothesis; the file’s header displays this face as the normal form of the hypothesis, the analytic distribution of the zeros translated into the fixed-point domain of the retraction over $\mathbb{C}$, and reads it as a normalization in the sense in which Fermat’s Last Theorem was reduced to the modularity of semistable elliptic curves. The biconditional face: since the record’s least erasure is a theorem, the record and the zeros agree on least erasure exactly when the hypothesis holds. The set-level face: the zero set is a fixed point of $\mathrm{Rec}$ exactly when the hypothesis holds. The section face: the zero set sits inside its own record exactly when the hypothesis holds. The self-verification face: the hypothesis is self-verifying exactly when it holds. The record side of the transport and biconditional faces, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, is supplied at no cost by the recursion of Theorem 6.2; the set-level and section faces compare the zero set with the record $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ itself, and the self-verification face states the hypothesis in the self-verifying form $\neg P \to P$ of Part I, the form in which the root is undeniable in act (`TOE0.denial_instantiates`). What the first four faces state is the exact identity between the hypothesis and the unprojected side.

**Theorem 6.5** (`rh_from_the_cargo_loop`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** From the 1-bit fixed-point bridge $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: `RiemannHypothesis`.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The first face of Theorem 6.4, read from left to right (`zeta_ra_loop.1.mp`). ◻

</div>

This is the passage from the record to the zeros, which the file calls the normal form applied: on Part III’s discrete chart every proof of the value at a closed configuration is a supply of the act’s field (`RememberedOffered.the_atomic_necessity`), and the form of that proof is the hypothesis itself (`RememberedOffered.the_form_is_the_hypothesis`); over $\mathbb{C}$ the type is the theorem above. The bridge is the theorem’s printed hypothesis; its antecedent $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ is supplied with no hypothesis by the recursion of Theorem 6.2; and by Theorem 6.4 the bridge is the hypothesis itself in fixed-point form. Every theorem of the file that concludes `RiemannHypothesis` prints its hypotheses in its signature: the 1-bit bridge here, section inclusion in Theorem 6.3, a reflection closure and retraction injectivity in Theorem 7.11, retraction injectivity of the zeros in Theorem 7.12, their closure being a theorem, the look back in Theorem 7.19, provability premises in `no_offline_refuter_seals_rh`.

## The eleven-part binding and the transfer status

**Theorem 6.6** (`zeta_binding`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** The following eleven statements hold as one conjunction:

1.  $\mathrm{RH}\leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ (`h_id_proved`);

2.  $\mathrm{RH}\leftrightarrow (\forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,q)$ (`rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`);

3.  $\forall s,\ \mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}(1-s)$;

4.  $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

5.  $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

6.  $\forall q,\ \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,q$;

7.  $\neg\mathrm{OffLine}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

8.  $(\exists Z : \mathrm{ActualZeros},\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

9.  $(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$;

10. $(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{RH}$;

11. $(\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,s) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{RH}$.

**Theorem 6.7** (`mathlib_transfer_status`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $$\begin{aligned}
&(\mathrm{RH}\leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \ \wedge\ \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\\
\wedge\ &\bigl((\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{RH}\bigr).
\end{aligned}$$

The transfer status answers, at theorem grade, the objection that results about the file’s own structures do not transfer to Mathlib’s hypothesis. The transfer is the equivalence itself, and the distance between the retrospective record and Mathlib’s sentence is Mathlib’s sentence.

## Analytic faces

An analytic face is any proposition proved equivalent to `RiemannHypothesis`: a structure `AnalyticFace` with a sentence and a proof of `RiemannHypothesis ↔ sentence`.

**Theorem 6.8** (`analytic_face_is_least_erasure`, `analytic_face_is_transport_gap`, `analytic_face_vocabulary_law`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every analytic face $F$ and every proposition $P$: $$\begin{aligned}
F.\mathrm{sentence} &\leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}),\\
F.\mathrm{sentence} &\leftrightarrow \bigl(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\bigr),\\
(F.\mathrm{sentence} \to P) &\leftrightarrow (\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to P),\\
(P \to F.\mathrm{sentence}) &\leftrightarrow (P \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})).
\end{aligned}$$

Every complex-analytic reformulation of the hypothesis is deductively interchangeable with the retraction fixed-point identity, in both directions, against any premise and toward any conclusion. No vocabulary bypasses least erasure.

# Functional-Equation Closure, Orbit Collapse, Chart Homomorphism

## Strip equivalence, the functional equation and Schwarz reflection

Mathlib supplies $\Lambda(1-s) = \Lambda(s)$ as `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub`, the relation $\zeta(s) = \Lambda(s)/\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s)$ for $s \neq 0$ as `riemannZeta_def_of_ne_zero`, and the non-vanishing of $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}$ on $\operatorname{Re} s > 0$ as `Gammaℝ_ne_zero_of_re_pos`.

**Theorem 7.1** (`completed_zeta_zeros_symm`, `completed_zeta_zeros_closed_pt`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}$ is closed under $s \mapsto 1-s$.

**Theorem 7.2** (`zeta_zero_iff_completed_of_re_pos`, `zeta_zeros_iff_completed_in_strip`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For $\operatorname{Re} s > 0$, $\zeta(s) = 0 \leftrightarrow \Lambda(s) = 0$. For $0 < \operatorname{Re} s < 1$, $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{CompletedZetaZeros}(s)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* On $\operatorname{Re} s > 0$ the point is nonzero and $\Gamma_{\mathbb{R}}(s) \neq 0$, so the quotient vanishes exactly when $\Lambda(s)$ does. Inside the strip a point is neither $0$, nor $1$, nor a trivial zero, since every trivial zero has real part at most $-2$; the two triples of side conditions therefore coincide. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.3** (`zeta_zeros_symm_in_strip`, `strip_zeta_zeros_closed_pt`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $0 < \operatorname{Re} s < 1$ and $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$ then $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(1-s)$. The set $\mathrm{StripZetaZeros} := \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\cap \{0 < \operatorname{Re} s < 1\}$ is closed under $s \mapsto 1-s$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Pass to $\Lambda$ inside the strip, reflect by `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub`, and return; the reflected point is again inside the strip. ◻

</div>

Over the whole plane the file proves the reflection from the functional equation of $\zeta$ itself, which Mathlib states as `riemannZeta_one_sub`, $$\zeta(1-s) = 2\,(2\pi)^{-s}\,\Gamma(s)\cos(\pi s/2)\,\zeta(s) \qquad (s \notin \{0,-1,-2,\dots\},\ s \neq 1),$$ and proves Schwarz reflection on the pinned release. Mathlib supplies also the non-vanishing of $\zeta$ on $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$ (`riemannZeta_ne_zero_of_one_lt_re`, imported on line 2), its Dirichlet series there (`zeta_eq_tsum_one_div_nat_cpow`), its differentiability away from $1$ (`differentiableAt_riemannZeta`), the identity theorem for analytic functions on a preconnected set (`AnalyticOnNhd.eqOn_of_preconnected_of_eventuallyEq`), and the connectedness of the complement of a point in a real vector space of rank above one (`isConnected_compl_singleton_of_one_lt_rank`, imported on line 3).

**Theorem 7.4** (`differentiableAt_star_comp`, `star_natCast_cpow`, `zeta_schwarz_reflection`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is complex-differentiable at $\bar x$, then $y \mapsto \overline{f(\bar y)}$ is complex-differentiable at $x$. For $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and $t \in \mathbb{C}$, $\overline{n^{\bar t}} = n^{t}$. For $s \neq 1$, $\zeta(\bar s) = \overline{\zeta(s)}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The functions $y \mapsto \overline{\zeta(\bar y)}$ and $\zeta$ are analytic on $\mathbb{C}\setminus\{1\}$, the first by the first statement. On $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, a neighbourhood of $2$, they agree term by term on the Dirichlet series by the second. The set $\mathbb{C}\setminus\{1\}$ is connected, $\mathbb{C}$ having real rank two, so the identity theorem makes them agree on all of it. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.5** (`zeta_ne_zero_neg_odd`, `zeta_zeros_not_neg_nat`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $k \in \mathbb{N}$, $\zeta(-(2k+1)) \neq 0$. No nontrivial zero is a nonpositive integer: if $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$, then $s \neq -n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* At $w = 2k+2$ the functional equation writes $\zeta(-(2k+1)) = \zeta(1-w)$ as the product of $2$, $(2\pi)^{-w}$, $\Gamma(w)$ with $\operatorname{Re} w > 0$, $\cos(\pi(k+1)) = (-1)^{k+1}$ and $\zeta(w)$ with $\operatorname{Re} w > 1$, none of them zero. For the second statement, $s = 0$ is excluded by $\zeta(0) = -\tfrac12$, $s = -2(m+1)$ by the definition of $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$, and $s = -(2k+1)$ by the first. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.6** (`zeta_zeros_symm`, `zeta_zeros_closed_pt`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$ then $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(1-s)$: the nontrivial zero set is closed under $s \mapsto 1-s$ on the whole plane.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* A nontrivial zero is no nonpositive integer, by Theorem 7.5, and is not $1$, so the functional equation applies and $\zeta(1-s)$ is a multiple of $\zeta(s) = 0$. The point $1-s$ is no trivial zero, since $1-s = -2(m+1)$ would give $\operatorname{Re} s = 2m+3 > 1$, where $\zeta$ does not vanish; and $1-s \neq 1$, since $s \neq 0$. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.7** (`zeta_zeros_conj`, `zeta_zeros_closed`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$ then $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(\bar s)$; and $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: the nontrivial zero set is closed under the fold $s \mapsto 1-\bar s$ of the complex chart, with no hypothesis.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* By Theorem 7.4, $\zeta(\bar s) = \overline{\zeta(s)} = 0$, and conjugation fixes the excluded points $1$ and $-2(m+1)$. The fold is conjugation followed by $s \mapsto 1-s$, and Theorem 7.6 closes the zeros under the second. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.8** (`zeta_zeros_in_strip`, `zeta_zeros_iff_strip`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** If $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s)$ then $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$; and $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}= \{\, s \mid (0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1) \wedge \mathrm{ZetaZeros}(s) \,\}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* $\zeta$ does not vanish on $\operatorname{Re} s > 1$, so $\operatorname{Re} s \le 1$; the same applied to the zero $1-s$ of Theorem 7.6 gives $\operatorname{Re} s \ge 0$. ◻

</div>

Theorem 7.3 closes the zeros inside the open strip through the completed function; Theorems 7.6 and 7.7 close the whole zero set, under $s \mapsto 1-s$ from the functional equation of $\zeta$ and under the fold by Schwarz reflection, and Theorem 7.8 places every nontrivial zero in the closed strip $0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1$. The closure $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ that the orbit collapse of Section 7.2 asks at the zeros is therefore a theorem of the file.

## Retraction injectivity and orbit collapse

**Definition 7.9.** $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(S) :\Longleftrightarrow \forall p\,q,\ S\,p \to S\,q \to \mathrm{reg}p = \mathrm{reg}q \to p = q$: no two distinct points of $S$ register at the same point of the line.

**Theorem 7.10** (`closed_retraction_injective_forces_value`, `value_implies_retraction_injective`, `closed_retraction_injective_iff_value`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** On every reflection-closed $S \subseteq \mathbb{C}$: $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(S)$ and $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(S)$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Let $s \in S$. By closure $\mathrm{fold}s \in S$; by `reg_fold` the two register at one point; injectivity forces $\mathrm{fold}s = s$, which is $\mathrm{onLine}\,s$ by `fold_fixed_iff_onLine`. Conversely, under the value the retraction is the identity on $S$ and so injective. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.11** (`record_retraction_injective`, `rh_from_closed_and_retraction_injective`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every $S$, $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$. If $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ and $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, then $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \wedge \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$.

The orbit-collapse theorem names, for any reflection-closed set, the exact geometric content of the value: no conjugate pair survives registration. On the record this holds without hypothesis. At the zeros the closure the theorem asks is Theorem 7.7, $\mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ with no hypothesis, and the general equivalence specializes to the zero set itself.

**Theorem 7.12** (`retraction_injective_iff_rh`, `rh_from_retraction_injective`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$. If $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, then $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \wedge \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Theorem 7.10 at the reflection-closed set $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ of Theorem 7.7, then `h_read_proved`; the second statement is Theorem 7.11 at the same closure. ◻

</div>

Retraction injectivity of the zeros is the orbit-collapse spelling of the one bit: it is the printed hypothesis of `rh_from_retraction_injective`, as the 1-bit bridge is of `rh_from_the_cargo_loop`, and each is Mathlib’s hypothesis by theorem, the first by Theorem 7.12 and the second by Theorem 6.4.

**Theorem 7.13** (`socket_at_zeta_zeros`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $(\exists Z : \texttt{ActualZeros},\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$; and for every proposition $Q$, if $Q \to \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$, then $Q \to \exists Z : \texttt{ActualZeros},\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{ZetaZeros}$.

An act whose zeros are $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ (Definition 4.1) carries the closure of $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$, which is Theorem 7.7, and its least erasure, which is the hypothesis by `h_id_proved`; so the act exists exactly when the hypothesis holds, and every proof of the hypothesis, from any premise, yields it. At the zeros themselves over $\mathbb{C}$ this is the atomic necessity that Part III’s discrete chart states at every closed configuration (`RememberedOffered.the_atomic_necessity`).

The four readings of the bit at the zeros are bound in one theorem, which the file calls the cone. The type `ApexReading` has the four values `leastErasure`, `retraction`, `socket` and `coincidence`, and `apexDiagram` sends them to $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, $\mathrm{RetractionInjective}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, $\exists Z : \texttt{ActualZeros},\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{ZetaZeros}$, and $\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})\,s$.

**Theorem 7.14** (`apex_cone`, `apex_one_gap`, `apex_regress_halts`, `bit_read_twice`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every reading $r$, $\texttt{apexDiagram}\,r \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$; for any two readings $r$ and $s$, $\texttt{apexDiagram}\,r \leftrightarrow \texttt{apexDiagram}\,s$; for every proposition $P$ with $P \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$ and every reading $r$, $P \leftrightarrow \texttt{apexDiagram}\,r$; and $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \wedge (\texttt{RiemannHypothesis} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}))$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The four legs are `h_id_proved`, Theorem 7.12, Theorem 7.13 and `ra_coincidence_iff_rh` of Theorem 6.3; the second and third statements compose them, and the fourth pairs `cargo_at_zeros` with `h_id_proved`. ◻

</div>

Mathlib’s hypothesis is the apex and each reading a leg proved equivalent to it, so any two readings are one proposition, and any further proposition proved equivalent to the apex lands on the same four. The last statement holds the record side of the bit, a theorem, beside its reading at the zeros, the hypothesis: one bit, read twice.

## The discrete chart embeds in the plane

Parts III, IV-b, VII, VIII and IX work, and the optional section of Part VIII-b reads its points and line, on the discrete offset chart $\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}$, a point $(d,t)$ being offset $d$ from the line at height $t$, with $\mathrm{fold}(d,t) = (-d,t)$, $\mathrm{reg}(d,t) = (0,t)$ and $\mathrm{onLine}(d,t) \leftrightarrow d = 0$; Part I’s chart is the coordinate range (`TOE0.chart`) of a grid of quaternions (`TOE0.quats`) whose conjugation-fixed set is the scalar line, Parts II, IV and V and the carried time kernel of Part IV-c place their line at other abscissae with their own folds, the judge probe of Part IV-c restating its test on the offset chart, Part V-b maps charts equivariantly into the offset chart (`Charts.Equivariant`, `Charts.transport`), and Part VI binds the results. Define $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(d,t) := \bigl(\tfrac12 + \tfrac d8\bigr) + it$.

**Theorem 7.15** (`discrete_chart_embeds_in_complex`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every discrete point $p$: $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\mathrm{fold}p) = \mathrm{fold}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}} p)$, $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\mathrm{reg}p) = \mathrm{reg}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}} p)$, and $\mathrm{onLine}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}} p) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}(p)$.

The chart of Part IX therefore maps equivariantly into $\mathbb{C}$, the other offset-chart parts writing their copies by the same three equations, and nothing in them is altered to say so. Part VIII’s carrier enters the plane by the same map; write $\kappa$ for `carrier_to_zero`, the inverse of `map_zero_to_carrier` of Section 9.6.

**Theorem 7.16** (`carrier_embeds_in_complex`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every carrier state $c$: $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa(C\,c)) = \mathrm{fold}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa\,c))$, $\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa(\mathrm{annihilate}\,c)) = \mathrm{reg}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa\,c))$, and $\mathrm{Neutral}(c) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{onLine}(\varphi_{\mathbb{C}}(\kappa\,c))$.

Charge conjugation becomes the complex fold, annihilation the complex retraction, and the neutral sector the points of the critical line: the locus of the physical closure is carried into the locus of the formal closure by a theorem of the file.

## Pause and look back: the unconditional retrospective seal

Section X-l of the file runs the retrospective arc over $\mathbb{C}$ in two movements: a pause at the record, proved with no premise, and a look back onto the zeros, proved identical to the hypothesis.

**Definition 7.17** (the pause and the look back)**.** $\mathrm{Pause} :\Longleftrightarrow \forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})(\mathrm{reg}(s)) \wedge \mathrm{reg}(\mathrm{reg}(s)) = \mathrm{reg}(s) \wedge \mathrm{reg}(\mathrm{fold}(s)) = \mathrm{reg}(s)$ and $\mathrm{LookBack} :\Longleftrightarrow \forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to \mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})(\mathrm{reg}(s)) \to \mathrm{reg}(s) = s$.

**Theorem 7.18** (`no_closed_principle_decides`, `pause_is_unconditional`, `forward_pass_unconditional`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** For every predicate $D$ on configurations with $\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to D(S)$: $\neg\,\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to D(S) \to \mathrm{Value}(S)$. The pause holds. And $$\begin{aligned}
&\mathrm{FreedomRoot} \wedge \mathrm{Closed}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \wedge (\forall s,\ \mathrm{ZetaZeros}\,s \to 0 \le \operatorname{Re} s \le 1)\\
\wedge\ &\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \wedge \mathrm{SelfVerifying}(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})) \wedge \mathrm{Pause}.
\end{aligned}$$

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* The pair world of an off-line point is reflection-closed, so it satisfies every principle all closed configurations share, and it lacks the value. A zero $s$ lands in the record at $\mathrm{reg}(s)$ as the image of itself, and `reg_idem` and `reg_fold` give the other two parts of the pause. The forward pass collects `BoundChain.freedom_root_inhabited` of Theorem 8.1, Theorems 7.7 and 7.8, `cargo_at_zeros`, the self-verification of Theorem 6.2 and the pause. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.19** (`look_back_is_the_closure`, `rh_from_pause_and_look_back`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $(\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow (\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros}))) \wedge (\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis})$. If $\mathrm{LookBack}$, then `RiemannHypothesis`.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* By the pause the antecedent $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})(\mathrm{reg}(s))$ holds at every zero, so $\mathrm{LookBack}$ is $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$; the first face of `zeta_ra_loop` with `h_id_proved` gives the first part, `h_id_proved` the second, and the last statement reads the second from left to right. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 7.20** (`the_unconditional_retrospective_seal`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** With no premise the following hold as one conjunction: the forward pass of Theorem 7.18, its six parts from $\mathrm{FreedomRoot}$ to $\mathrm{Pause}$; $\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$; for every reading $r$ of the cone, $\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \texttt{apexDiagram}\,r$; $(\exists Z : \texttt{ActualZeros},\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LookBack}$; for every proposition $Q$, if $Q \to \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$ then $Q \to \mathrm{LookBack}$; and the impossibility over $\mathbb{C}$ of Theorem 7.18, that no principle shared by every reflection-closed configuration forces the value on all of them.

The seal is the anchor of the formal closure in this edition. Its forward pass, resting on Schwarz reflection and the non-vanishing of $\zeta$ at the negative odd integers, saturates the complex scaffold with no premise: the zeros are closed under the fold and confined to the closed strip, their record is lossless and self-verifying, and at the pause every nontrivial zero is registered at $\mathrm{reg}(s)$ in its record, the retraction idempotent there and a conjugate pair colliding there. Its impossibility conjunct refutes over $\mathbb{C}$, by theorem, every zero-bit derivation valid at every reflection-closed configuration from what those configurations share, so the halt at the bit is a proved boundary of that class of derivation and not a defect. Its atomic-necessity conjunct states, as the right-to-left direction of $\mathrm{LookBack} \leftrightarrow \texttt{RiemannHypothesis}$, that any proof of `RiemannHypothesis` from any premise $Q$, $Q := \mathrm{True}$ among them, yields $\mathrm{LookBack}$, and with the socket conjunct an inhabitant of the socket, and by the cone the look back, least erasure, retraction injectivity, section inclusion and the socket are one proposition. What remains is the look back, with zero remainder: Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis` is equivalent to $\mathrm{LookBack}$, the one bit $\mathrm{reg}(s) = s$ at every zero, read at the pause, and `rh_from_pause_and_look_back` returns Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis` from it in one step, at tier <span class="smallcaps">c</span>, as the file prints it.

**Definition 7.21** (the canonical record hypothesis)**.** $\mathrm{CanonicalRH} :\Longleftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$: every point of the retracted record of the zeros lies on the critical line.

**Theorem 7.22** (`canonical_rh_unconditional`, `canonical_property_holds_off_the_line`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> <span class="smallcaps">pcq</span>\])**.** $\mathrm{CanonicalRH}$, with no premise; and $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{pairWorld}(\mathrm{offPoint})))$, at the reflection-closed pair world of the off point of Section 5.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Both are `the_remembered_is_lossless` of Theorem 4.2, at $\mathrm{ZetaZeros}$ and at the pair world: the retraction lands on the line (`reg_lands`). ◻

</div>

The canonical apex is the record side of the bit in the value form: every point of the projected zero set lies on the critical line, with no premise. It is not the apex of the cone of Theorem 7.14: the record of every configuration has the same property (Theorem 4.2), a reflection-closed one with a point off the line among them, so the canonical apex is a property of the projection and, as the file states, says nothing about where the zeros lie. The look back carries the question from the projection to the zeros themselves, and the look back is `RiemannHypothesis` (Theorem 7.19).

      11770  /-- Zeta does not vanish at negative odd integers. -/
      11771  theorem zeta_ne_zero_neg_odd (k : ℕ) : riemannZeta (-(2 * (k : Point) + 1)) ≠ 0 := by

      11793    apply mul_ne_zero
      11794    apply mul_ne_zero
      11795    apply mul_ne_zero

      11807        push_cast

      11822  theorem zeta_zeros_not_neg_nat {s : Point} (hz : ZetaZeros s) : ∀ n : ℕ, s ≠ -(n : Point) := by
      11823    intro n h

      11848  /-- The nontrivial zero set is closed under s ↦ 1 - s. -/
      11849  theorem zeta_zeros_symm {s : Point} (hz : ZetaZeros s) : ZetaZeros (foldPt s) := by
      11850    obtain ⟨hz0, hz1, hz2⟩ := hz

**Listing 17. The cone over the four readings of the bit (X-k)** (master lines 12166 to 12224)

      12166  /-! ### X-k . The Cone: One Apex, Every Reading, No Category Gap -/
      12167  
      12168  /-- The readings of the apex: the four registers' readings of the one bit. -/
      12169  inductive ApexReading where
      12170    | leastErasure
      12171    | retraction
      12172    | socket
      12173    | coincidence
      12174    deriving DecidableEq, Repr
      12175  
      12176  /-- The diagram: each reading as a proposition over ℂ. -/
      12177  def apexDiagram : ApexReading → Prop
      12178    | .leastErasure => LeastErasure ZetaZeros
      12179    | .retraction   => RetractionInjective ZetaZeros
      12180    | .socket       => ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = ZetaZeros
      12181    | .coincidence  => ∀ s, ZetaZeros s → Rec ZetaZeros s
      12182  
      12183  /-- THE CONE: Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis is the apex; every leg is a proved
      12184      equivalence. The category gaps between the readings are eliminated: a gap is
      12185      the absence of an identity leg, and every leg is exhibited here. -/
      12186  theorem apex_cone : ∀ r, apexDiagram r ↔ RiemannHypothesis := by
      12187    intro r
      12188    cases r
      12189    · exact h_id_proved.symm
      12190    · exact retraction_injective_iff_rh
      12191    · exact socket_at_zeta_zeros.1

# The Discrete Arch

Part IX is `RH_Bound_Chain_v1.0.1.lean`, in the namespace `BoundChain`, which resolves every identifier this section cites, carried into the master with the recursion of Theorem 8.2 and its self-grounding term inserted in v3.0.7 ahead of its pin block, their two pins added inside it, and eleven further pins added inside it in v3.0.10, the earlier editions of the master standing in the repository; it was written for core Lean with no import. It runs the same calculus on the discrete chart, where every theorem below has an empty cone: no axiom at all, not even propositional extensionality, quotients or choice.

**Theorem 8.1** (`bound_chain`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** The formal root $\mathrm{FreedomRoot} := \exists f : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N},\ \forall a,\ f\,a = a$ is inhabited; for every $S$, $\mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}S) \wedge \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}S) \wedge \exists Z,\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{Rec}S$; reflection symmetry alone forces nothing; no principle shared by all closed configurations forces the value; no inhabited proposition forces the value; no record-invariant predicate decides the value; and Stage 1 of Part IX is inhabited.

**Theorem 8.2** (`transport_needs_value`, `identification_is_the_proof`, `ra_recursion_at_record`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** On the discrete chart: for every $M$, $(\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}M) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}M) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(M)$; for every $S$, $(\exists Z,\ Z.\mathrm{zeros} = \mathrm{Rec}S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$; and for every $S$, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}S)$, its self-verification, and its absorption of every premise, from the term `ra_cargo_self_grounding` $S$.

The discrete arch is the formal closure with every axiom removed. What Part X adds is the binding of the same shape to Mathlib’s $\zeta$, at the cost of the three standard axioms Mathlib itself rests on.

# The Physical Closure

Parts VII and VIII carry the hypothesis from premises about the physical world, each premise printed in a theorem signature, the measurement entering the concrete capstone as the certificate field of the bound structure its signature takes. The chart is the discrete offset chart, the classical hypothesis enters as an abstract proposition $\mathrm{ClassicalRH}$, and the reading $\mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(Z_\zeta)$ is the one identification of the classical hypothesis that the reader grants, entered as the printed premise $h_{\mathrm{read}}$ of a theorem schema in $\mathrm{ClassicalRH}$ and $Z_\zeta$; the discrete configuration $Z_\zeta$ is supplied with the reading and granted with it, the file fixing no map from the zeros of $\zeta$ to the chart. Over $\mathbb{C}$, Section 3 proves the corresponding reading for Mathlib’s sentence as `h_read_proved`, a theorem of the complex chart that the discrete schema does not consume; the chart homomorphism of Section 7.3 carries the discrete line into $\operatorname{Re} s = 1/2$, a discrete point lying on the line exactly when its image does.

## The least-erasure kernel

A system of the kernel (`LeastErasureDoF.System`) has $\mathrm{distinct}$ macro-records, $\mathrm{free}$ binary labels and $\mathrm{total} = \mathrm{distinct}\cdot 2^{\mathrm{free}}$ microstates. A discard halves the count of macro-records and frees one label with the total preserved; an erasure keeps that count, loses one free label, and halves the total. With $\ln 2$ scaled by $10^6$ as $\texttt{ln2\_scaled} = 693147$:

**Theorem 9.1** (`discard_is_free`, `sysEntropy_decrease`, `null_forces_zero`, `density_bound_from_residual_bound`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / t / c / c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** A discard satisfies $\mathrm{after.distinct}\cdot 2 = \mathrm{before.distinct}$ and $\mathrm{after.free} = \mathrm{before.free}+1$. An erasure lowers the system entropy $\mathrm{free}\cdot\ln 2$ by exactly $\ln 2$. With $\mathrm{residual}(\rho, r, q) := \rho r q$: if $r>0$, $q>0$ and $\mathrm{residual}(\rho,r,q) = 0$ then $\rho = 0$; and if $\mathrm{residual}(\rho,r,q) \le \varepsilon$, $r \ge r_0$, $q \ge q_0$ then $\rho\, r_0\, q_0 \le \varepsilon$.

The exact-null and finite-sensitivity regimes are kept apart by type. A null result at finite sensitivity bounds a population, $\rho\, r_0\, q_0 \le \varepsilon$, and in the kernel’s natural units, the floors positive, it reads $\rho \le \lfloor \varepsilon/(r_0\, q_0)\rfloor$ (`density_le_div`), which is zero when $\varepsilon < r_0\, q_0$. Landauer’s law enters as the definition $\texttt{landauerHeatPerEvent}\,T := T\cdot\texttt{ln2\_scaled}$; what the theorems derive is the count of erased labels and that at positive temperature the heat is positive exactly when the count is.

## The identification reduced to the reading, and the act as the premise packaged

**Theorem 9.2** (`le_iff_value`, `classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading`, `the_act_is_the_premise_packaged`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> t / c / t · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** For every discrete configuration, $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(S) \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(S)$. Whoever grants $\mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(Z_\zeta)$ has granted $\mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta)$. An act exists at $S$ exactly when $\mathrm{Closed}(S) \wedge \mathrm{LeastErasure}(S)$.

## The bridge of six arrows, composed

**Theorem 9.3** (`off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** Let $\mathrm{Realizes}, \mathrm{Erases}$ be predicates on a carrier type and $\mathrm{density}, \mathrm{rate}, \mathrm{heat}$ natural-valued functions on it. Grant the six arrows: a failure of least erasure at $Z_\zeta$ realizes a carrier; a realized carrier erases; an erasing carrier has population at least $n_0$; rate at least $r_0$; heat per event at least $q_0$; and the residual observable $R$ covers its contribution, $R \ge \mathrm{density}\cdot\mathrm{rate}\cdot\mathrm{heat}$. Then $\neg\mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta) \to R \ge n_0 r_0 q_0$.

The threshold $n_0 r_0 q_0$ depends neither on the carrier nor on which point stands off the line: it is uniform over the class the arrows name. Positive rate and positive heat alone do not reach it; the population floor and the coupling are needed and are named.

## The capstones

**Theorem 9.4** (`classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** From $h_{\mathrm{id}} : \mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta)$, $h_{\mathrm{bridge}} : \neg\mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta) \to R \ge \delta$, $h_{\mathrm{bound}} : R \le \varepsilon$, $h_{\mathrm{gap}} : \varepsilon < \delta$ and $0 < \delta$: $\mathrm{ClassicalRH}$.

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* Pointwise and constructive. At each read point the registration either fixes the point, or it does not and the bridge puts $R \ge \delta > \varepsilon \ge R$. ◻

</div>

**Theorem 9.5** (`classical_rh_from_the_arrows`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** From the reading $h_{\mathrm{read}} : \mathrm{ClassicalRH} \leftrightarrow \mathrm{Value}(Z_\zeta)$, the six arrows of Theorem 9.3, the bound $R \le \varepsilon$ and the gap $\varepsilon < n_0 r_0 q_0$: $\mathrm{ClassicalRH}$.

**Theorem 9.6** (`no_third_position`  \[<span class="smallcaps">tier</span> c · <span class="smallcaps">cone</span> $\varnothing$\])**.** Under the identification, the bound and the gap, $\neg\bigl(\neg\mathrm{ClassicalRH} \wedge (\neg\mathrm{LeastErasure}(Z_\zeta) \to R \ge \delta)\bigr)$: the denial of the hypothesis and the bridge cannot both stand.

A reader who denies the hypothesis has named the bridge as the arrow that fails; a reader who grants the bridge has granted the hypothesis.

       9415      h_pos     the threshold is positive (implied by h_gap over the naturals; printed because the Recommendation
