        219    ((List.range 4).flatMap fun i => (List.range 4).map fun j => (i, j)).countP
        220      fun (i, j) => i < j && p.getD j 0 < p.getD i 0
        221  
        222  /-- The twelve gates as the even permutations. -/
        223  def gates : List (List Nat) := perms4.filter fun p => inversions p % 2 == 0
        224  
        225  def compose (p q : List Nat) : List Nat := q.map fun i => p.getD i 0
        226  def inverse (p : List Nat) : List Nat := [0, 1, 2, 3].map fun i => p.idxOf i
        227  
        228  def conjClass (g : List Nat) : List (List Nat) := (gates.map fun h => compose (compose h g) (inverse h)).eraseDups
        229  
        230  def insertSorted (n : Nat) : List Nat → List Nat
        231    | [] => [n]
        232    | m :: ms => if n ≤ m then n :: m :: ms else m :: insertSorted n ms
        233  
        234  def sortNat (l : List Nat) : List Nat := l.foldr insertSorted []
        235  
        236  /-- The class equation from the sorted class size of each element: a class of size s contributes s elements. -/
        237  def collapse : Nat → List Nat → List Nat
        238    | 0, _ => []
        239    | _ + 1, [] => []
        240    | fuel + 1, s :: rest => s :: collapse fuel (rest.drop (s - 1))
        241  
        242  set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
        243  /-- SECOND WAY: the twelve gates, with class equation 1, 3, 4, 4. -/
        244  theorem the_class_equation :
        245      gates.length = 12 ∧ collapse 12 (sortNat (gates.map fun g => (conjClass g).length)) = [1, 3, 4, 4] := by
        246    decide
        247  
        248  /-! ## V · The regress terminated -/
        249  
        250  /-- THE REGRESS ENDS AT THE ROOT: any proposition offered as a further ground of the root is idle; the root needs
        251      no level above it. -/
        252  theorem no_level_above {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) : ∀ Q : Prop, (Q → R) → R := fun _ _ => G.instances G.anAct
        253  
        254  /-! ## VI · The master seal -/
        255  
        256  /-- THE MASTER SEAL: the floor is universal; the root is a theorem on the constructed domain; the Return closes;
        257      the line is the fixed set; and the twelve gates are recovered three ways. -/
        258  theorem the_master_seal :
        259      (∀ (R : Prop) (G : SelfGrounding R), R ∧ (∀ _ : G.Act, R) ∧ (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → R) ↔ R)) ∧
        260      RA₀ ∧ (qi.mul qj).mul qk = qneg ∧
        261      quats.all (fun q => (q.conj == q) == (q.b == 0 && q.c == 0 && q.d == 0)) = true ∧
        262      (units.filter upToSign).length = 12 ∧ gates.length = 12 ∧ (shell.filter upToSign).length = 12 ∧
        263      collapse 12 (sortNat (gates.map fun g => (conjClass g).length)) = [1, 3, 4, 4] :=
        264    ⟨the_floor_is_universal, root_on_the_constructed_domain, the_return, the_line_is_the_fixed_set,
        265     twenty_four_units_twelve_gates.2, the_class_equation.1, the_shell_splits_twelve_and_twelve.2.1, the_class_equation.2⟩
        266  
        267  end TOE0
        268  
        269  /-! ## The zero law, pinned: every cone is empty -/
        270  /-- info: 'TOE0.denial_reenacts_root' does not depend on any axioms -/
        271  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.denial_reenacts_root
        272  /-- info: 'TOE0.seated_undeniable' does not depend on any axioms -/
        273  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.seated_undeniable
        274  /-- info: 'TOE0.external_proof_adds_nothing' does not depend on any axioms -/
        275  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.external_proof_adds_nothing
        276  /-- info: 'TOE0.denial_instantiates' does not depend on any axioms -/
        277  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.denial_instantiates
        278  /-- info: 'TOE0.the_floor_is_universal' does not depend on any axioms -/
        279  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.the_floor_is_universal
        280  /-- info: 'TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain' does not depend on any axioms -/
        281  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.root_on_the_constructed_domain
        282  /-- info: 'TOE0.the_return' does not depend on any axioms -/
        283  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.the_return
        284  /-- info: 'TOE0.units_square_to_minus_one' does not depend on any axioms -/
        285  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.units_square_to_minus_one
        286  /-- info: 'TOE0.conj_involutive_on_the_chart' does not depend on any axioms -/
        287  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.conj_involutive_on_the_chart
        288  /-- info: 'TOE0.the_line_is_the_fixed_set' does not depend on any axioms -/
        289  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.the_line_is_the_fixed_set
        290  /-- info: 'TOE0.twenty_four_units_twelve_gates' does not depend on any axioms -/
        291  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.twenty_four_units_twelve_gates
        292  /-- info: 'TOE0.the_shell_splits_twelve_and_twelve' does not depend on any axioms -/
        293  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.the_shell_splits_twelve_and_twelve
        294  /-- info: 'TOE0.the_class_equation' does not depend on any axioms -/
        295  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.the_class_equation
        296  /-- info: 'TOE0.no_level_above' does not depend on any axioms -/
        297  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.no_level_above
        298  /-- info: 'TOE0.the_master_seal' does not depend on any axioms -/
        299  #guard_msgs in #print axioms TOE0.the_master_seal
        300  
        301  end PartI
        302  
        303  /-! # PART II · Every_Prime_3_2_0.lean, verbatim -/
        304  section PartII
        305  /-
        306    EVERY PRIME · 3.2.0
        307    Core Lean 4.19.0, standalone: no library, no import, no axiom declared, no sorry.
        308    Every theorem prints its axiom cone at the foot of the file; 237 cones are pinned under
        309    #guard_msgs, so a compile in which any pinned cone changes fails.
        310  
        311    The file proves, on one chart, what a formal system can prove about the Riemann Hypothesis
        312    and locates the one thing it cannot: a single bit, which is the hypothesis itself, and which
        313    every proof of the hypothesis supplies rather than derives.
        314  
        315    THE CHART. A point is (x, t) with x the doubled real part and t the height; the critical line
        316    is x = 1. The fold (x, t) ↦ (2 − x, t) is s ↦ 1 − s̄. Registration (x, t) ↦ (1, t) lands
        317    every point on the line and keeps the height. A world is a set of points, a zero set. The
        318    record of a world is its image under registration. Two worlds with the same record are
        319    twins of one record. A world is fold-closed when the fold maps it into itself.
        320  
        321    TERMS USED IN THIS FILE.
        322    seat            the fixed set of an involution: the line under the fold; 1 under multiplication.
        323    orbit           the two points a fold-closed world carries off the line, exchanged by the fold;
        324                    at a prime p, the two ordered factorizations (1, p) and (p, 1).
        325    reading of the record   a predicate on worlds that takes one value on all twins of one record.
        326    keyless, keyed  a predicate on worlds true on every world; true on some world and false on another.
        327    admissible      keyless, or a reading of the record.
        328    coalition       a Boolean combination of premises, of any depth.
        329    forces          a premise forces the line when every fold-closed world satisfying it satisfies RH.
        330    least erasure   a world every twin of which has a point off the line whenever it has one.
        331    posit, act      an assumption written as the field of a structure; an inhabitant of a
        332                    self-grounding structure, whose existence is equivalent to the proposition.
        333                    The one posit of the file is least erasure at the actual zero set; a classical
        334                    theorem written as a field (the functional equation, the explicit formula, the
        335                    faces) is cited there, not posited.
        336    supply, spend   to provide the posit. The supplied bit is the sign of the posit.
        337    arrow           a sign function: the identity on a type, or λ(n) = (−1)^Ω(n).
        338    displacement, side   for a point, x − 1; for a point off the line, the sign of x − 1.
        339    setting         a hypothesis with a provability predicate, Σ₁-complete and sound on the denial.
        340    resolution n    the chart with the line at x = n: the fold x ↦ 2n − x, registration (x, t) ↦ (n, t), and
        341                    the open strip 0 < x < 2n; the chart above is resolution one.
        342    seeded witness  for a world in time: one locus at every instant, the same truth value of the
        343                    hypothesis at every instant, and the hypothesis at instant 0, the seed.
        344    computation     a finite list of reported points; it reads an act when every point it reports
        345                    is a zero of the act's zero set.
        346  
        347    SECTIONS AND THEIR MAIN THEOREMS.
        348    I      the identity arrow; a bit is two distinct values (aperture_one_bit_wide)
        349    II     every prime is one fibre of exactly two (prime_fibre, freedom_is_exactly_two)
        350    III    completely additive functions are determined at the primes (determined_by_primes)
        351    IV     the p-adic valuation as a free assignment; Euclid's lemma from first principles
        352           (euclid_lemma, prime_freedom_independent, primes_base_of_freedom)
        353    V      the sign arrow of an additive count is completely multiplicative (arrow_multiplicative);
        354           no finite stage decides a universal (finite_never_forces)
        355    VI     the chart: no registered point lies off the line; no reading of the record decides
        356           the hypothesis; keyless premises force nothing (unicorn_never_registered,
        357           record_decides_nothing, keyless_forces_nothing)
        358    VII    least erasure is the hypothesis (least_erasure_is_the_value)
        359    VII-bis the fold never crosses the line; a second symmetry; the record blind at every scale
        360    VIII   a self-grounding supply exists exactly when the proposition holds (supply_iff);
        361           the five faces of the hypothesis (faces_are_one)
        362    IX     primes, the free basis and the identity arrow are keyless and force nothing
        363    X      the explicit formula as a structure; least erasure is Weil positivity
        364           (least_erasure_is_positivity); positivity is keyed (positivity_is_keyed)
        365    XI     the posit as a structure field (rh_from_the_act, acts_are_one)
        366    XII    the block with no axiom (record_decides_nothing_free)
        367    XIII   the hypothesis on the supplied bit (prime_arc_sealed)
        368    XIV    the hypothesis is the weakest forcing premise (rh_is_the_weakest_forcing_premise);
        369           the Li and de Bruijn–Newman coordinates (li_prefix_never_forces, rh_iff_the_sign)
        370    XV     four faces in time, exactly one keyed (exactly_one_face_is_keyed)
        371    XVI    the eigenstructure of the fold; the side bit and its calibration
        372           (record_never_reads_the_side, colocation_is_a_calibration)
        373    XVII   admissible coalitions force nothing; no certified height forces; the heat flow on
        374           polynomials; the Liouville arrow computed; five readings agree; no reader index
        375    XVIII  a theory placed on three strata; the root crosses no keyed sentence; the two can'ts;
        376           the round trip; the ladder blocked (the_road)
        377    XIX    the vocabulary law; the even coalition; the triaxial cut; the ladder's proof; the
        378           route ledger (the_front)
        379    XX     least erasure affirmed: the record, the ledger, the price, the one form, the act
        380           (least_erasure_affirmed)
        381    XXI    every assignment realized; the arrow for every n; the closure on any carrier; the
        382           closure, whole (the_closure_on_any_carrier, the_closure)
        383    XXII   the socket: every route to the value lands in the one field (socket_is_the_value)
        384    XXII.c two denials, one form: the denial of the root refuted by its own act, the denial of the
        385           hypothesis denying the self-grounding assertion of the line and every seed; the witness
        386           forced by the act (two_denials, the_witness_forced_by_the_act)
        387    XXIII  double security: the two channels of the line (double_security)
        388    XXIV   the root undeniable in act; the root read at the zeros; the lock (the_lock)
        389    XXV    admissible forcing is vacuous; the closure at resolution n, where the open strip does not
        390           supply the bit; the readings of the root joined; the rejection computed by a search; the
        391           posit as an act; no reading of the record returns any chart reading; the primes a free
        392           basis; least erasure as self-verification; every route carries its theorem; the tenth
        393           falsifier barred by the act (admissible_forcing_is_vacuous, rh_from_the_act_at,
        394           strip_does_not_supply_at, root_readings_joined, rejection_is_computed,
        395           every_route_carries_its_theorem, the_tenth_is_barred_by_the_act, the_kinetic_bar)
        396    XXVI   the closure bound whole: the two-part reading, the lock, the socket, the irreducible cut, the
        397           two denials, the witness and the bar, in one theorem (the_capstone)
        398  
        399    TWO THINGS ARE PROVED AT ONCE. Least erasure is equivalent to the hypothesis on every world
        400    (least_erasure_is_the_value), so the hypothesis follows from the posit. No reading of the
        401    record, and no Boolean combination of readings and keyless premises, agrees with the
        402    hypothesis on every fold-closed world (no_coalition_decides), so nothing in the file supplies
        403    the posit.
        404  -/
        405  namespace PrimeFreedom
        406  
        407  /-! ## I · The identity arrow, and a bit as two distinct values -/
        408  
        409  /-- The identity arrow on a type. -/
        410  def arrow (α : Type) : α → α := id
        411  
        412  theorem arrow_exists (α : Type) : ∃ f : α → α, ∀ a, f a = a := ⟨id, fun _ => rfl⟩
        413  
        414  /-- A Boolean takes one of two values. -/
        415  theorem orientation_two_valued : ∀ b : Bool, b = true ∨ b = false := by
        416    intro b
        417    cases b
        418    · exact Or.inr rfl
        419    · exact Or.inl rfl
        420  
        421  /-- The two orientations are distinct. -/
        422  theorem orientations_distinct : (true : Bool) ≠ false := fun h => Bool.noConfusion h
        423  
        424  /-- A bit is two values, and they differ. -/
        425  theorem aperture_one_bit_wide : (∀ b : Bool, b = true ∨ b = false) ∧ (true : Bool) ≠ false :=
        426    ⟨orientation_two_valued, orientations_distinct⟩
        427  
        428  /-! ## II · Every prime is one fibre of exactly two -/
        429  
        430  def isPrime (p : Nat) : Prop := 2 ≤ p ∧ ∀ d, d ∣ p → d = 1 ∨ d = p
        431  
        432  /-- The fixed point of multiplication. -/
        433  def mul_seat : Nat := 1
        434  
        435  /-- The multiplicative orbit over n: the pairs that multiply to n. -/
        436  def mul_orbit (n : Nat) (a b : Nat) : Prop := a * b = n
        437  
        438  theorem seat_is_one : mul_seat = 1 := rfl
        439  
        440  /-- The fibre of multiplication over a prime is the pair (1, p), (p, 1). -/
        441  theorem prime_fibre (p : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) (a b : Nat) :
        442      mul_orbit p a b ↔ (a = 1 ∧ b = p) ∨ (a = p ∧ b = 1) := by
        443    constructor
        444    · intro h
        445      have hdvd : a ∣ p := ⟨b, h.symm⟩
        446      cases hp.2 a hdvd with
        447      | inl h1 =>
        448        subst h1
        449        have h' : 1 * b = p := h
        450        rw [Nat.one_mul] at h'
        451        exact Or.inl ⟨rfl, h'⟩
        452      | inr hp_eq =>
        453        subst hp_eq
        454        have h2a : 2 ≤ a := hp.1
        455        have hb : b = 1 := by
        456          have h_pos : 0 < a := by omega
        457          exact Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_left h_pos (by rw [show a * b = a from h, Nat.mul_one])
        458        exact Or.inr ⟨rfl, hb⟩
        459    · rintro (⟨ha1, hbp⟩ | ⟨hap, hb1⟩)
        460      · rw [ha1, hbp]
        461        exact Nat.one_mul p
        462      · rw [hap, hb1]
        463        exact Nat.mul_one p
        464  
        465  /-- No a satisfies a · a = p for a prime p. -/
        466  theorem prime_off_seat (p : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) : ¬ ∃ a, mul_orbit p a a := by
        467    rintro ⟨a, ha⟩
        468    have h2p : 2 ≤ p := hp.1
        469    cases (prime_fibre p hp a a).mp ha with
        470    | inl h1 => omega
        471    | inr h2 => omega
        472  
        473  /-- The fibre over a prime is exactly the ordered pair and its reverse, and the two are distinct. -/
        474  theorem freedom_is_exactly_two (p : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) :
        475      (∀ a b, mul_orbit p a b ↔ (a = 1 ∧ b = p) ∨ (a = p ∧ b = 1)) ∧ (1 : Nat) ≠ p :=
        476    ⟨prime_fibre p hp, by intro h; have := hp.1; omega⟩
        477  
        478  /-! ## III · Completely additive functions are determined at the primes -/
        479  
        480  /-- A completely additive measure on the multiplicative monoid of the positive integers. -/
        481  def CompletelyAdditive (f : Nat → Int) : Prop :=
        482    ∀ a b, a > 0 → b > 0 → f (a * b) = f a + f b
        483  
        484  /-- A completely additive function vanishes at 1. -/
        485  theorem seat_is_zero (f : Nat → Int) (hf : CompletelyAdditive f) : f 1 = 0 := by
        486    have h := hf 1 1 (by decide) (by decide)
        487    rw [Nat.mul_one] at h
        488    omega
        489  
        490  /-- Least witness search, with fuel. -/
        491  def findLeastFrom (P : Nat → Prop) [DecidablePred P] (start : Nat) : Nat → Nat
        492    | 0 => start
        493    | fuel + 1 => if P start then start else findLeastFrom P (start + 1) fuel
        494  
        495  theorem findLeastFrom_correct (P : Nat → Prop) [DecidablePred P] (start fuel m : Nat)
        496      (hlo : start ≤ m) (hhi : m ≤ start + fuel) (hm : P m) :
        497      P (findLeastFrom P start fuel) ∧ findLeastFrom P start fuel ≤ m := by
        498    induction fuel generalizing start with
        499    | zero =>
        500      have h : m = start := by omega
        501      subst h
        502      exact ⟨hm, Nat.le_refl m⟩
        503    | succ fuel ih =>
        504      show P (if P start then start else findLeastFrom P (start + 1) fuel) ∧
        505        (if P start then start else findLeastFrom P (start + 1) fuel) ≤ m
        506      rcases Decidable.em (P start) with h | h
        507      · rw [if_pos h]
        508        exact ⟨h, hlo⟩
        509      · rw [if_neg h]
        510        have hne : m ≠ start := fun he => h (he ▸ hm)
        511        exact ih (start + 1) (by omega) (by omega)
        512  
        513  
        514  /-- The least divisor of n at least 2, found by bounded search from 2 with fuel n. -/
        515  def leastDivisor (n : Nat) : Nat := findLeastFrom (fun d => 2 ≤ d ∧ d ∣ n) 2 n
        516  
        517  theorem leastDivisor_spec (n : Nat) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
        518      (2 ≤ leastDivisor n ∧ leastDivisor n ∣ n) ∧ leastDivisor n ≤ n ∧
        519        (∀ m, 2 ≤ m → m ∣ n → leastDivisor n ≤ m) := by
        520    have hbase := findLeastFrom_correct (fun d => 2 ≤ d ∧ d ∣ n) 2 n n hn (by omega)
        521      ⟨hn, Nat.dvd_refl n⟩
        522    refine ⟨hbase.1, hbase.2, fun m hm2 hm => ?_⟩
        523    have hmn : m ≤ n := Nat.le_of_dvd (by omega) hm
        524    exact (findLeastFrom_correct (fun d => 2 ≤ d ∧ d ∣ n) 2 n m hm2 (by omega) ⟨hm2, hm⟩).2
        525  
        526  /-- The least divisor at least 2 is prime: any divisor of it divides n, and the search's
        527      minimality bounds it from below. -/
        528  theorem leastDivisor_prime (n : Nat) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : isPrime (leastDivisor n) := by
        529    obtain ⟨⟨hd2, hdvd⟩, hdle, hmin⟩ := leastDivisor_spec n hn
        530    refine ⟨hd2, fun m hm => ?_⟩
        531    have hdpos : 0 < leastDivisor n := by omega
        532    have hmle : m ≤ leastDivisor n := Nat.le_of_dvd hdpos hm
        533    rcases Decidable.em (m = 1) with h1 | h1
        534    · exact Or.inl h1
        535    · right
        536      have hmne0 : m ≠ 0 := by
        537        intro h0
        538        rw [h0] at hm
        539        obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hm
        540        rw [Nat.zero_mul] at hc
        541        omega
        542      have hm2 : 2 ≤ m := by omega
        543      have hle := hmin m hm2 (Nat.dvd_trans hm hdvd)
        544      omega
        545  
        546  /-- Every integer greater than one has a prime divisor: the least divisor at least 2, found by
        547      bounded search. No classical axiom. -/
        548  theorem exists_prime_dvd (n : Nat) (h0 : 0 < n) (h1 : n ≠ 1) : ∃ p, isPrime p ∧ p ∣ n := by
        549    have hn : 2 ≤ n := by omega
        550    exact ⟨leastDivisor n, leastDivisor_prime n hn, (leastDivisor_spec n hn).1.2⟩
        551  
        552  /-- Two completely additive functions that agree at every prime agree everywhere, by bounded
        553      induction peeling one prime divisor at each step. -/
        554  theorem determined_by_primes (f g : Nat → Int) (hf : CompletelyAdditive f)
        555      (hg : CompletelyAdditive g) (h_agree : ∀ p, isPrime p → f p = g p) :
        556      ∀ n, 0 < n → f n = g n := by
        557    suffices h : ∀ fuel n, n ≤ fuel → 0 < n → f n = g n from fun n hn => h n n (Nat.le_refl n) hn
        558    intro fuel
        559    induction fuel with
        560    | zero => intro n hle h0; omega
        561    | succ fuel ih =>
        562      intro n hle h0
        563      if h1 : n = 1 then
        564        subst h1
        565        rw [seat_is_zero f hf, seat_is_zero g hg]
        566      else
        567        obtain ⟨p, hp, hpd⟩ := exists_prime_dvd n h0 h1
        568        obtain ⟨k, hk⟩ := hpd
        569        have hk0 : 0 < k := by
        570          rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos k with hkc | hkc
        571          · exfalso
        572            rw [hkc, Nat.mul_zero] at hk
        573            omega
        574          · exact hkc
        575        have hp2 : 2 ≤ p := hp.1
        576        have hlt : k < n := by
        577          obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hp2
        578          rw [hk, hd, Nat.add_mul]
        579          omega
        580        have hpf : f (p * k) = f p + f k := hf p k (by omega) hk0
        581        have hpg : g (p * k) = g p + g k := hg p k (by omega) hk0
        582        rw [hk, hpf, hpg, h_agree p hp, ih k (by omega) hk0]
        583  
        584  /-! ## IV · The p-adic valuation as a free assignment; Euclid's lemma from first principles -/
        585  
        586  /-- Remainder descent: if p divides m * b and x * b, with x = m * q + r, then p divides r * b. -/
        587  theorem dvd_remainder_mul (p b m q r x : Nat) (hpm : p ∣ m * b) (hx : p ∣ x * b)
        588      (hqr : m * q + r = x) : p ∣ r * b := by
        589    have h2 : p ∣ (m * q) * b := by
        590      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hpm
        591      exact ⟨c * q, by
        592        calc (m * q) * b = (m * b) * q := Nat.mul_right_comm m q b
        593          _ = (p * c) * q := by rw [hc]
        594          _ = p * (c * q) := Nat.mul_assoc p c q⟩
        595    have h3 : (m * q) * b + r * b = x * b := by rw [← Nat.add_mul, hqr]
        596    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := hx
        597    obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := h2
        598    have hY : r * b = x * b - (m * q) * b := by
        599      calc r * b = (m * q) * b + r * b - (m * q) * b := (Nat.add_sub_cancel_left _ _).symm
        600        _ = x * b - (m * q) * b := by rw [h3]
        601    exact ⟨u - v, by rw [Nat.mul_sub, ← hu, ← hv]; exact hY⟩
        602  
        603  /-- The least positive m with p ∣ m * b, found by search from 0 with fuel p. -/
        604  def leastMulDvd (p b : Nat) : Nat := findLeastFrom (fun m => 0 < m ∧ p ∣ m * b) 0 p
        605  
        606  theorem leastMulDvd_spec (p b : Nat) (hwit : 0 < p ∧ p ∣ p * b) :
        607      (0 < leastMulDvd p b ∧ p ∣ leastMulDvd p b * b) ∧ leastMulDvd p b ≤ p ∧
        608        (∀ k, k ≤ p → 0 < k ∧ p ∣ k * b → leastMulDvd p b ≤ k) :=
        609    ⟨(findLeastFrom_correct (fun m => 0 < m ∧ p ∣ m * b) 0 p p (Nat.zero_le p) (by omega)
        610        hwit).1,
        611     (findLeastFrom_correct (fun m => 0 < m ∧ p ∣ m * b) 0 p p (Nat.zero_le p) (by omega)
        612        hwit).2,
        613     fun k hk hPk =>
        614       (findLeastFrom_correct (fun m => 0 < m ∧ p ∣ m * b) 0 p k (Nat.zero_le k) (by omega)
        615         hPk).2⟩
        616  
        617  /-- Euclid's lemma: a prime dividing a product divides one of the factors. Proved by least-witness
        618      search, the division algorithm and descent on the remainder. -/
        619  theorem euclid_lemma (p a b : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) (hab : p ∣ a * b) : p ∣ a ∨ p ∣ b := by
        620    rcases Decidable.em (p ∣ a) with hpa | hpa
        621    · exact Or.inl hpa
        622    · right
        623      have hp0 : 0 < p := by have := hp.1; omega
        624      obtain ⟨⟨hm0, hmdvd⟩, hmle, hmin'⟩ :=
        625        leastMulDvd_spec p b ⟨hp0, Nat.dvd_mul_right p b⟩
        626      have hmp : leastMulDvd p b ∣ p := by
        627        apply Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero
        628        have hc : p % leastMulDvd p b = 0 ∨ 0 < p % leastMulDvd p b := by omega
        629        rcases hc with h0 | hpos
        630        · exact h0
        631        · have hlt : p % leastMulDvd p b < leastMulDvd p b := Nat.mod_lt p hm0
        632          have hdvd' : p ∣ (p % leastMulDvd p b) * b :=
        633            dvd_remainder_mul p b (leastMulDvd p b) (p / leastMulDvd p b)
        634              (p % leastMulDvd p b) p hmdvd (Nat.dvd_mul_right p b)
        635              (Nat.div_add_mod p (leastMulDvd p b))
        636          have hle := hmin' (p % leastMulDvd p b) (by omega) ⟨hpos, hdvd'⟩
        637          omega
        638      have hma : leastMulDvd p b ∣ a := by
        639        apply Nat.dvd_of_mod_eq_zero
        640        have hc : a % leastMulDvd p b = 0 ∨ 0 < a % leastMulDvd p b := by omega
        641        rcases hc with h0 | hpos
        642        · exact h0
        643        · have hlt : a % leastMulDvd p b < leastMulDvd p b := Nat.mod_lt a hm0
        644          have hdvd' : p ∣ (a % leastMulDvd p b) * b :=
        645            dvd_remainder_mul p b (leastMulDvd p b) (a / leastMulDvd p b)
        646              (a % leastMulDvd p b) a hmdvd hab (Nat.div_add_mod a (leastMulDvd p b))
        647          have hle := hmin' (a % leastMulDvd p b) (by omega) ⟨hpos, hdvd'⟩
        648          omega
        649      rcases hp.2 _ hmp with h | h
        650      · rw [h] at hmdvd
        651        rwa [Nat.one_mul] at hmdvd
        652      · rw [h] at hma
        653        exact absurd hma hpa
        654  
        655  /-- Greatest witness at or below the bound, by downward search; P 0 always holds here. -/
        656  def findGt (P : Nat → Prop) [DecidablePred P] : Nat → Nat
        657    | 0 => 0
        658    | n + 1 => if P (n + 1) then n + 1 else findGt P n
        659  
        660  theorem findGt_spec (P : Nat → Prop) [DecidablePred P] (n : Nat) (h0 : P 0) :
        661      P (findGt P n) := by
        662    induction n with
        663    | zero => exact h0
        664    | succ n ih =>
        665      show P (if P (n + 1) then n + 1 else findGt P n)
        666      rcases Decidable.em (P (n + 1)) with h | h
        667      · rw [if_pos h]; exact h
        668      · rw [if_neg h]; exact ih
        669  
        670  theorem findGt_max (P : Nat → Prop) [DecidablePred P] (n k : Nat) (hk : k ≤ n) (hPk : P k) :
        671      k ≤ findGt P n := by
        672    induction n with
        673    | zero =>
        674      have h : k = 0 := by omega
        675      subst h
        676      exact Nat.le_refl _
        677    | succ n ih =>
        678      show k ≤ (if P (n + 1) then n + 1 else findGt P n)
        679      rcases Decidable.em (P (n + 1)) with h | h
        680      · rw [if_pos h]; exact hk
        681      · rw [if_neg h]
        682        have hne : k ≠ n + 1 := fun hkk => h (hkk ▸ hPk)
        683        have hkn : k ≤ n := by omega
        684        exact ih hkn
        685  
        686  /-- The p-adic valuation: the exponent of p in n, as the greatest k with p ^ k ∣ n. -/
        687  def pExp (p n : Nat) : Nat := findGt (fun k => p ^ k ∣ n) n
        688  
        689  theorem pExp_dvd (p n : Nat) : p ^ pExp p n ∣ n :=
        690    findGt_spec (fun k => p ^ k ∣ n) n (by
        691      show p ^ 0 ∣ n
        692      rw [Nat.pow_zero]
        693      exact Nat.one_dvd n)
        694  
        695  /-- Exponents of two outrun their index. -/
        696  theorem two_pow_ge (k : Nat) : k + 1 ≤ 2 ^ k := by
        697    induction k with
        698    | zero => decide
        699    | succ k ih => rw [Nat.pow_succ]; omega
        700  
        701  /-- A power of p ≥ 2 dividing a positive n is bounded by n. -/
        702  theorem pow_dvd_bound (p n k : Nat) (hp : 2 ≤ p) (hn : 0 < n) (h : p ^ k ∣ n) : k ≤ n := by
        703    have h1 : p ^ k ≤ n := Nat.le_of_dvd hn h
        704    have h2 : k + 1 ≤ 2 ^ k := two_pow_ge k
        705    have h3 : 2 ^ k ≤ p ^ k := Nat.pow_le_pow_left hp k
        706    omega
        707  
        708  theorem pExp_le_of_dvd (p n k : Nat) (hk : k ≤ n) (h : p ^ k ∣ n) : k ≤ pExp p n :=
        709    findGt_max (fun k => p ^ k ∣ n) n k hk h
        710  
        711  /-- Four factors rearranged. -/
        712  theorem mul_mul_mul_comm_nat (a b c d : Nat) : (a * b) * (c * d) = (a * c) * (b * d) := by
        713    calc (a * b) * (c * d) = a * (b * c) * d := by
        714          rw [Nat.mul_assoc, ← Nat.mul_assoc b c d, Nat.mul_assoc a (b * c) d]
        715      _ = a * (c * b) * d := by rw [Nat.mul_comm b c]
        716      _ = (a * c) * (b * d) := by
        717          rw [Nat.mul_assoc, Nat.mul_assoc c b d, Nat.mul_assoc a c (b * d)]
        718  
        719  /-- The p-adic valuation is additive over products. -/
        720  theorem pExp_mul (p a b : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 < b) :
        721      pExp p (a * b) = pExp p a + pExp p b := by
        722    have hp2 : 2 ≤ p := hp.1
        723    have hp0 : 0 < p := by omega
        724    have hia : p ^ pExp p a ∣ a := pExp_dvd p a
        725    have hjb : p ^ pExp p b ∣ b := pExp_dvd p b
        726    obtain ⟨a', ha'⟩ := hia
        727    obtain ⟨b', hb'⟩ := hjb
        728    have hpa' : ¬ p ∣ a' := by
        729      intro hdiv
        730      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hdiv
        731      have hbig : p ^ (pExp p a + 1) ∣ a :=
        732        ⟨c, by
        733          calc a = p ^ pExp p a * a' := ha'
        734            _ = p ^ pExp p a * (p * c) := by rw [hc]
        735            _ = p ^ (pExp p a + 1) * c := by rw [Nat.pow_add, Nat.pow_one, Nat.mul_assoc]⟩
        736      have hle := pExp_le_of_dvd p a (pExp p a + 1)
        737        (pow_dvd_bound p a _ hp2 ha hbig) hbig
        738      omega
        739    have hpb' : ¬ p ∣ b' := by
        740      intro hdiv
        741      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hdiv
        742      have hbig : p ^ (pExp p b + 1) ∣ b :=
        743        ⟨c, by
        744          calc b = p ^ pExp p b * b' := hb'
        745            _ = p ^ pExp p b * (p * c) := by rw [hc]
        746            _ = p ^ (pExp p b + 1) * c := by rw [Nat.pow_add, Nat.pow_one, Nat.mul_assoc]⟩
        747      have hle := pExp_le_of_dvd p b (pExp p b + 1)
        748        (pow_dvd_bound p b _ hp2 hb hbig) hbig
        749      omega
        750    have hprodeq : a * b = p ^ (pExp p a + pExp p b) * (a' * b') := by
        751      have e1 : a * b = (p ^ pExp p a * a') * b := congrArg (fun x => x * b) ha'
        752      have e2 : (p ^ pExp p a * a') * b = (p ^ pExp p a * a') * (p ^ pExp p b * b') :=
        753        congrArg (fun x => (p ^ pExp p a * a') * x) hb'
        754      have e3 : (p ^ pExp p a * a') * (p ^ pExp p b * b') =
        755          (p ^ pExp p a * p ^ pExp p b) * (a' * b') := mul_mul_mul_comm_nat _ _ _ _
        756      have e4 : (p ^ pExp p a * p ^ pExp p b) * (a' * b') =
        757          p ^ (pExp p a + pExp p b) * (a' * b') :=
        758        congrArg (fun x => x * (a' * b')) (Nat.pow_add p _ _).symm
        759      exact e1.trans (e2.trans (e3.trans e4))
        760    have hup : p ^ (pExp p a + pExp p b) ∣ a * b := ⟨a' * b', hprodeq⟩
        761    have hdown : ¬ p ^ (pExp p a + pExp p b + 1) ∣ a * b := by
        762      intro hbig
        763      have hdecomp : p ^ (pExp p a + pExp p b + 1) = p ^ (pExp p a + pExp p b) * p := by
        764        rw [Nat.pow_add, Nat.pow_one]
        765      have hdiv : p ∣ a' * b' := by
        766        have h' : p ^ (pExp p a + pExp p b) * p ∣ p ^ (pExp p a + pExp p b) * (a' * b') := by
        767          rw [← hprodeq, ← hdecomp]
        768          exact hbig
        769        exact Nat.dvd_of_mul_dvd_mul_left (Nat.pow_pos hp0) h'
        770      rcases euclid_lemma p a' b' hp hdiv with h | h
        771      · exact hpa' h
        772      · exact hpb' h
        773    have hle1 : pExp p a + pExp p b ≤ pExp p (a * b) :=
        774      pExp_le_of_dvd p (a * b) _ (pow_dvd_bound p (a * b) _ hp2 (Nat.mul_pos ha hb) hup) hup
        775    have hle2 : pExp p (a * b) ≤ pExp p a + pExp p b := by
        776      have hK : p ^ pExp p (a * b) ∣ a * b := pExp_dvd p (a * b)
        777      rcases Decidable.em (pExp p a + pExp p b + 1 ≤ pExp p (a * b)) with hgt | hgt
        778      · exact absurd (Nat.dvd_trans (Nat.pow_dvd_pow p hgt) hK) hdown
        779      · omega
        780    omega
        781  
        782  /-- The valuation of p at itself is one. -/
        783  theorem pExp_self (p : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) : pExp p p = 1 := by
        784    have hp2 : 2 ≤ p := hp.1
        785    have hp0 : 0 < p := by omega
        786    have h1 : p ^ (1 : Nat) ∣ p := by rw [Nat.pow_one]
        787    have h1le : 1 ≤ pExp p p := pExp_le_of_dvd p p 1 (by omega) h1
        788    have hnot2 : ¬ p ^ (1 + 1 : Nat) ∣ p := by
        789      intro h
        790      have hle : p ^ (1 + 1) ≤ p := Nat.le_of_dvd hp0 h
        791      rw [Nat.pow_add, Nat.pow_one] at hle
        792      have hge : 2 * p ≤ p * p := by
        793        obtain ⟨d, hd⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_add_of_le hp2
        794        rw [hd, Nat.add_mul]
        795        exact Nat.le_add_right _ _
        796      omega
        797    rcases Decidable.em (2 ≤ pExp p p) with h | h
        798    · exact absurd (Nat.dvd_trans (Nat.pow_dvd_pow p h) (pExp_dvd p p)) hnot2
        799    · omega
        800  
        801  /-- The valuation vanishes where p does not divide. -/
        802  theorem pExp_eq_zero_of_not_dvd (p n : Nat) (h : ¬ p ∣ n) : pExp p n = 0 := by
        803    rcases Decidable.em (1 ≤ pExp p n) with hpos | hneg
        804    · have hpow : p ^ (1 : Nat) ∣ p ^ pExp p n := Nat.pow_dvd_pow p hpos
        805      rw [Nat.pow_one] at hpow
        806      exact absurd (Nat.dvd_trans hpow (pExp_dvd p n)) h
        807    · omega
        808  
        809  /-- The valuation at one is zero. -/
        810  theorem pExp_one (p : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) : pExp p 1 = 0 := by
        811    apply pExp_eq_zero_of_not_dvd
        812    intro hd
        813    have h1 := Nat.le_of_dvd (by decide) hd
        814    have h2 := hp.1
        815    omega
        816  
        817  /-- The valuation at a different prime is zero. -/
        818  theorem pExp_other (p q : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) (hq : isPrime q) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
        819      pExp p q = 0 := by
        820    apply pExp_eq_zero_of_not_dvd
        821    intro hd
        822    rcases hq.2 p hd with h | h
        823    · have := hp.1; omega
        824    · exact hpq h
        825  
        826  /-- The p-adic valuation as an integer-valued function. -/
        827  def padicMeasure (p : Nat) (n : Nat) : Int := (pExp p n : Int)
        828  
        829  theorem padicMeasure_additive (p : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) :
        830      CompletelyAdditive (padicMeasure p) := by
        831    intro a b ha hb
        832    show ((pExp p (a * b) : Nat) : Int) = (pExp p a : Int) + (pExp p b : Int)
        833    rw [pExp_mul p a b hp ha hb, Int.natCast_add]
        834  
        835  /-- For distinct primes p and q there is a completely additive function equal to 1 at p and 0 at q:
        836      the p-adic valuation. -/
        837  theorem prime_freedom_independent (p q : Nat) (hp : isPrime p) (hq : isPrime q) (hpq : p ≠ q) :
        838      ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0 :=
        839    ⟨padicMeasure p, padicMeasure_additive p hp,
        840     by show ((pExp p p : Nat) : Int) = 1; rw [pExp_self p hp]; rfl,
        841     by show ((pExp p q : Nat) : Int) = 0; rw [pExp_other p q hp hq hpq]; rfl,
        842     by show ((pExp p 1 : Nat) : Int) = 0; rw [pExp_one p hp]; rfl⟩
        843  
        844  /-- Uniqueness and independence together: a completely additive function is determined by its
        845      values at the primes, and those values are freely assignable. -/
        846  theorem primes_base_of_freedom :
        847      (∀ f g : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f → CompletelyAdditive g →
        848        (∀ p, isPrime p → f p = g p) → ∀ n, 0 < n → f n = g n) ∧
        849      (∀ p q : Nat, isPrime p → isPrime q → p ≠ q →
        850        ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0) :=
        851    ⟨determined_by_primes, prime_freedom_independent⟩
        852  
        853  /-! ## V · The sign arrow of an additive count -/
        854  
        855  /-- An additive count: Ω(ab) = Ω(a) + Ω(b) for positive a and b. -/
        856  def AdditiveCount (Om : Nat → Nat) : Prop := ∀ a b, a > 0 → b > 0 → Om (a * b) = Om a + Om b
        857  
        858  /-- The sign arrow of a count: +1 on an even count, −1 on an odd one. -/
        859  def signArrow (k : Nat) : Int := if k % 2 = 0 then 1 else -1
        860  
        861  /-- The sign of a sum is the product of the signs. -/
        862  theorem signArrow_add (m n : Nat) :
        863      signArrow (m + n) = signArrow m * signArrow n := by
        864    unfold signArrow
        865    rw [Nat.add_mod]
        866    rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one m with hm | hm <;>
        867      rcases Nat.mod_two_eq_zero_or_one n with hn | hn <;>
        868      rw [hm, hn] <;> decide
        869  
        870  /-- The sign arrow of an additive count is completely multiplicative, as λ(n) = (−1)^Ω(n) is. -/
        871  theorem arrow_multiplicative (Om : Nat → Nat) (hOm : AdditiveCount Om)
        872      (a b : Nat) (ha : a > 0) (hb : 0 < b) :
        873      signArrow (Om (a * b)) = signArrow (Om a) * signArrow (Om b) := by
        874    rw [hOm a b ha hb, signArrow_add]
        875  
        876  /-- At a prime the count is one and the sign is −1. -/
        877  theorem arrow_at_prime (Om : Nat → Nat) (p : Nat) (_hp : isPrime p) (hOm : Om p = 1) :
        878      signArrow (Om p) = -1 := by
        879    rw [hOm]
        880    decide
        881  
        882  /-! ## V-bis · No finite stage decides a universal -/
        883  
        884  /-- For every N there is a property true below N and false at N. -/
        885  theorem finite_never_forces (N : Nat) :
        886      ∃ P : Nat → Prop, (∀ n, n < N → P n) ∧ ¬ ∀ n, P n :=
        887    ⟨fun n => n < N, fun _ h => h, fun h => Nat.lt_irrefl N (h N)⟩
        888  
        889  /-- A property with counterexamples past every stage is not universal:
        890      no finite census decides the limit. -/
        891  theorem limit_not_forced (P : Nat → Prop) (h_finite : ∀ N, ∃ n > N, ¬ P n) : ¬ (∀ n, P n) := by
        892    intro h
        893    obtain ⟨n, _, hn_not⟩ := h_finite 0
        894    exact hn_not (h n)
        895  
        896  /-! ## VI · The chart: the fold, registration, the record -/
        897  
        898  /-- A point of the chart: the doubled real part x and the height t.
        899      The critical line is x = 1; the fold s ↦ 1 − s̄ sends x to 2 − x;
        900      registration keeps the height and lands on the line. -/
        901  structure Pt where
        902    x : Int
        903    t : Nat
        904    deriving DecidableEq
        905  
        906  def onLine (z : Pt) : Prop := z.x = 1
        907  instance (z : Pt) : Decidable (onLine z) := inferInstanceAs (Decidable (z.x = 1))
        908  def fold (z : Pt) : Pt := ⟨2 - z.x, z.t⟩
        909  def reg (z : Pt) : Pt := ⟨1, z.t⟩
        910  
        911  theorem fold_fixed_iff (z : Pt) : fold z = z ↔ onLine z := by
        912    cases z with
        913    | mk x t =>
        914      show Pt.mk (2 - x) t = Pt.mk x t ↔ x = 1
        915      constructor
        916      · intro h
        917        have hx := congrArg Pt.x h
        918        change 2 - x = x at hx
        919        omega
        920      · intro h
        921        subst h
        922        rfl
        923  
        924  theorem reg_fixes_line (z : Pt) (h : onLine z) : reg z = z := by
        925    cases z with
        926    | mk x t =>
        927      have hx : x = 1 := h
        928      subst hx
        929      rfl
        930  
        931  /-- No registered point lies off the line. -/
        932  theorem unicorn_never_registered (z : Pt) (h : ¬ onLine z) : ∀ w, reg w ≠ z := by
        933    intro w hw
        934    apply h
        935    rw [← hw]
        936    exact rfl
        937  
        938  /-- Every point is on the line, fixed by the fold and by registration, or off the line, moved by
        939      the fold, sharing its record with its partner, and registered by no point. -/
        940  theorem nothing_escapes_one_cut (z : Pt) :
        941      (onLine z ∧ fold z = z ∧ reg z = z) ∨
        942      (¬ onLine z ∧ fold z ≠ z ∧ reg (fold z) = reg z ∧ ∀ w, reg w ≠ z) :=
        943    if h : z.x = 1 then Or.inl ⟨h, (fold_fixed_iff z).mpr h, reg_fixes_line z h⟩
        944    else Or.inr ⟨h, fun hf => h ((fold_fixed_iff z).mp hf), rfl, unicorn_never_registered z h⟩
        945  
        946  /-- A world is a zero set on the chart. -/
        947  abbrev World := Pt → Prop
        948  def FoldClosed (Z : World) : Prop := ∀ z, Z z → Z (fold z)
        949  /-- The hypothesis, on the chart: every zero lies on the line. -/
        950  def RH (Z : World) : Prop := ∀ z, Z z → onLine z
        951  def Left (Z : World) : Prop := ∃ z, Z z ∧ z.x < 1
        952  def Right (Z : World) : Prop := ∃ z, Z z ∧ 1 < z.x
        953  
        954  /-- On a fold-closed world some zero lies left of the line exactly when some zero lies right of it. -/
        955  theorem sides_together (Z : World) (hZ : FoldClosed Z) : Left Z ↔ Right Z :=
        956    ⟨fun ⟨z, hz, hx⟩ => ⟨fold z, hZ z hz, show 1 < 2 - z.x by omega⟩,
        957     fun ⟨z, hz, hx⟩ => ⟨fold z, hZ z hz, show 2 - z.x < 1 by omega⟩⟩
        958  
        959  /-- On a fold-closed world the hypothesis holds exactly when no zero lies left of the line. -/
        960  theorem rh_iff_no_left (Z : World) (hZ : FoldClosed Z) : RH Z ↔ ¬ Left Z := by
        961    constructor
        962    · intro h ⟨z, hz, hx⟩
        963      have e : z.x = 1 := h z hz
        964      omega
        965    · intro h z hz
        966      if hx : z.x = 1 then exact hx
        967      else
        968        exfalso
        969        apply h
        970        if hl : z.x < 1 then exact ⟨z, hz, hl⟩
        971        else exact ⟨fold z, hZ z hz, show 2 - z.x < 1 by omega⟩
        972  
        973  /-- The record of a world: its zeros registered. -/
        974  def recordOf (Z : World) : World := fun r => ∃ s, Z s ∧ reg s = r
        975  def SameRecord (Z Z' : World) : Prop := ∀ r, recordOf Z r ↔ recordOf Z' r
        976  /-- A reading respects the record when two worlds of one record read alike. -/
        977  def RespectsRecord (g : World → Prop) : Prop := ∀ Z Z', SameRecord Z Z' → (g Z ↔ g Z')
        978  
        979  /-- The on-line world at height 14, and the off-line pair at offset k about the same height. -/
        980  abbrev W1 : World := fun z => z = ⟨1, 14⟩
        981  abbrev pairAt (k : Int) : World := fun z => z = ⟨1 - k, 14⟩ ∨ z = ⟨1 + k, 14⟩
        982  abbrev W2 : World := pairAt 1
        983  
        984  theorem W1_closed : FoldClosed W1 := by
        985    intro z hz
        986    have h : z = ⟨1, 14⟩ := hz
        987    subst h
        988    show fold ⟨1, 14⟩ = ⟨1, 14⟩
        989    decide
        990  
        991  theorem W1_rh : RH W1 := by
        992    intro z hz
        993    have h : z = ⟨1, 14⟩ := hz
        994    subst h
        995    exact rfl
        996  
        997  theorem pair_closed (k : Int) : FoldClosed (pairAt k) := by
        998    intro z hz
        999    rcases hz with h | h
       1000    · subst h
       1001      apply Or.inr
       1002      show Pt.mk (2 - (1 - k)) 14 = Pt.mk (1 + k) 14
       1003      congr 1
       1004      omega
       1005    · subst h
       1006      apply Or.inl
       1007      show Pt.mk (2 - (1 + k)) 14 = Pt.mk (1 - k) 14
       1008      congr 1
       1009      omega
       1010  
       1011  theorem pair_not_rh (k : Int) (hk : k ≠ 0) : ¬ RH (pairAt k) := by
       1012    intro h
       1013    have e : (1 : Int) - k = 1 := h ⟨1 - k, 14⟩ (Or.inl rfl)
       1014    omega
       1015  
       1016  theorem pair_same_record (k : Int) : SameRecord W1 (pairAt k) := by
       1017    intro r
       1018    constructor
       1019    · intro ⟨s, hs, hr⟩
       1020      have h : s = ⟨1, 14⟩ := hs
       1021      subst h
       1022      exact ⟨⟨1 - k, 14⟩, Or.inl rfl, hr⟩
       1023    · intro ⟨s, hs, hr⟩
       1024      rcases hs with h | h <;> subst h <;> exact ⟨⟨1, 14⟩, rfl, hr⟩
       1025  
       1026  theorem W2_closed : FoldClosed W2 := pair_closed 1
       1027  theorem W2_not_rh : ¬ RH W2 := pair_not_rh 1 (by decide)
       1028  theorem same_record_12 : SameRecord W1 W2 := pair_same_record 1
       1029  
       1030  /-- Distinct positive offsets give distinct fold-closed worlds with the record of W1, none
       1031      satisfying the hypothesis. -/
       1032  theorem fibre_is_infinite (k k' : Int) (hk : 0 < k) (hk' : 0 < k') (hne : k ≠ k') :
       1033      SameRecord W1 (pairAt k) ∧ ¬ RH (pairAt k) ∧ pairAt k ⟨1 - k, 14⟩ ∧ ¬ pairAt k' ⟨1 - k, 14⟩ := by
       1034    refine ⟨pair_same_record k, pair_not_rh k (by omega), Or.inl rfl, ?_⟩
       1035    intro h
       1036    rcases h with h | h
       1037    · have e : (1 : Int) - k = 1 - k' := congrArg Pt.x h
       1038      omega
       1039    · have e : (1 : Int) - k = 1 + k' := congrArg Pt.x h
       1040      omega
       1041  
       1042  /-- Two worlds with the same record that both satisfy the hypothesis are equal. -/
       1043  theorem lossless_unique (Z Z' : World) (h : SameRecord Z Z') (hZ : RH Z) (hZ' : RH Z') :
       1044      ∀ z, Z z ↔ Z' z := by
       1045    intro z
       1046    constructor
       1047    · intro hz
       1048      obtain ⟨s, hs, hsr⟩ := (h z).mp ⟨z, hz, reg_fixes_line z (hZ z hz)⟩
       1049      have e : reg s = s := reg_fixes_line s (hZ' s hs)
       1050      rw [← hsr, e]
       1051      exact hs
       1052    · intro hz
       1053      obtain ⟨s, hs, hsr⟩ := (h z).mpr ⟨z, hz, reg_fixes_line z (hZ' z hz)⟩
       1054      have e : reg s = s := reg_fixes_line s (hZ s hs)
       1055      rw [← hsr, e]
       1056      exact hs
       1057  
       1058  /-- No reading of the record agrees with the hypothesis on every fold-closed world. -/
       1059  theorem record_decides_nothing (g : World → Prop) (hg : RespectsRecord g) :
       1060      ¬ ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → (g Z ↔ RH Z) := fun h =>
       1061    W2_not_rh ((h W2 W2_closed).mp ((hg W1 W2 same_record_12).mp ((h W1 W1_closed).mpr W1_rh)))
       1062  
       1063  /-- record_decides_nothing, under a second name. -/
       1064  theorem unicorn_block (g : World → Prop) (hg : RespectsRecord g) :
       1065      ¬ ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → (g Z ↔ RH Z) := record_decides_nothing g hg
       1066  
       1067  /-- A premise is keyless when it holds on every world. -/
       1068  def Keyless (A : World → Prop) : Prop := ∀ Z, A Z
       1069  /-- A premise forces the line when every fold-closed world it holds on satisfies the hypothesis. -/
       1070  def Forces (A : World → Prop) : Prop := ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → A Z → RH Z
       1071  
       1072  /-- A keyless premise forces nothing: it holds on W2, which is fold-closed and fails the
       1073      hypothesis. -/
       1074  theorem keyless_forces_nothing (A : World → Prop) (hA : Keyless A) : ¬ Forces A :=
       1075    fun h => W2_not_rh (h W2 W2_closed (hA W2))
       1076  
       1077  /-- The hypothesis separates W1 from W2, which share one record. -/
       1078  theorem sentence_separates_record_does_not : (RH W1 ∧ ¬ RH W2) ∧ SameRecord W1 W2 :=
       1079    ⟨⟨W1_rh, W2_not_rh⟩, same_record_12⟩
       1080  
       1081  /-! ## VII · Least erasure is the value -/
       1082  
       1083  def OffLine (Z : World) : Prop := ∃ z, Z z ∧ ¬ onLine z
       1084  /-- Least erasure in the fibre: if the world erases, every world of its record erases. -/
       1085  def LeastErasure (Z : World) : Prop := ∀ Z', SameRecord Z Z' → OffLine Z → OffLine Z'
       1086  
       1087  theorem record_is_lossless (Z : World) : ¬ OffLine (recordOf Z) := by
       1088    intro ⟨r, ⟨s, _, hsr⟩, hoff⟩
       1089    apply hoff
       1090    rw [← hsr]
       1091    exact rfl
       1092  
       1093  theorem record_same (Z : World) : SameRecord Z (recordOf Z) := by
       1094    intro r
       1095    constructor
       1096    · intro ⟨s, hs, hsr⟩
       1097      exact ⟨reg s, ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩, hsr⟩
       1098    · intro ⟨s', ⟨s, hs, hss'⟩, hs'r⟩
       1099      subst hss'
       1100      exact ⟨s, hs, hs'r⟩
       1101  
       1102  /-- Least erasure holds on a world exactly when the hypothesis does. -/
       1103  theorem least_erasure_is_the_value (Z : World) : LeastErasure Z ↔ RH Z := by
       1104    constructor
       1105    · intro hle z hz
       1106      if h : z.x = 1 then exact h
       1107      else exact absurd (hle (recordOf Z) (record_same Z) ⟨z, hz, h⟩) (record_is_lossless Z)
       1108    · intro hrh _ _ ⟨z, hz, hoff⟩
       1109      exact absurd (hrh z hz) hoff
       1110  
       1111  /-- Least erasure is not a reading of the record: it holds on W1 and fails on W2, which share one
       1112      record. -/
       1113  theorem least_erasure_reads_past_the_record : ¬ RespectsRecord LeastErasure := fun h =>
       1114    W2_not_rh ((least_erasure_is_the_value W2).mp
       1115      ((h W1 W2 same_record_12).mp ((least_erasure_is_the_value W1).mpr W1_rh)))
       1116  
       1117  /-- Any premise that forces the line and is forced by it is the line, on every fold-closed
       1118      world. -/
       1119  theorem posit_is_the_value (A : World → Prop) (h : Forces A)
       1120      (h' : ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → RH Z → A Z) : ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → (A Z ↔ RH Z) :=
       1121    fun Z hZ => ⟨h Z hZ, h' Z hZ⟩
       1122  
       1123  /-! ## VII-bis · The fold never crosses the line; a second symmetry; the record blind at every scale -/
       1124  
       1125  /-- The fold lands on the line exactly where the point already was: folding never crosses. -/
       1126  theorem fold_onLine_iff (z : Pt) : onLine (fold z) ↔ onLine z := by
       1127    show (2 - z.x = 1) ↔ (z.x = 1)
       1128    constructor <;> intro h <;> omega
       1129  
       1130  theorem fold_preserves_offline (z : Pt) : ¬ onLine (fold z) ↔ ¬ onLine z := by
       1131    rw [fold_onLine_iff]
       1132  
       1133  theorem fold_ne_of_offline (z : Pt) (h : ¬ onLine z) : fold z ≠ z :=
       1134    fun hf => h ((fold_fixed_iff z).mp hf)
       1135  
       1136  /-- A second involution on the chart, commuting with the fold and preserving the line. -/
       1137  structure ConjSymmetry where
       1138    conj : Pt → Pt
       1139    invol : ∀ z, conj (conj z) = z
       1140    commutes : ∀ z, conj (fold z) = fold (conj z)
       1141    preserves_line : ∀ z, onLine (conj z) ↔ onLine z
       1142  
       1143  /-- Under both symmetries one off-line zero forces its reflection, its conjugate and their
       1144      composite into the world, all off the line. -/
       1145  theorem offline_zero_quadruple (Z : World) (hF : FoldClosed Z) (C : ConjSymmetry)
       1146      (hC : ∀ z, Z z → Z (C.conj z)) (z : Pt) (hz : Z z) (hoff : ¬ onLine z) :
       1147      Z (fold z) ∧ Z (C.conj z) ∧ Z (C.conj (fold z)) ∧
       1148        ¬ onLine (fold z) ∧ ¬ onLine (C.conj z) ∧ ¬ onLine (C.conj (fold z)) ∧ fold z ≠ z :=
       1149    ⟨hF z hz, hC z hz, hC (fold z) (hF z hz),
       1150     (fold_preserves_offline z).mpr hoff,
       1151     fun h => hoff ((C.preserves_line z).mp h),
       1152     fun h => hoff ((fold_onLine_iff z).mp ((C.preserves_line (fold z)).mp h)),
       1153     fold_ne_of_offline z hoff⟩
       1154  
       1155  /-- If the hypothesis fails on a world, some zero of it lies off the line. Classical. -/
       1156  theorem not_rh_has_offline_witness (Z : World) (h : ¬ RH Z) : OffLine Z := by
       1157    apply Classical.byContradiction
       1158    intro hno
       1159    apply h
       1160    intro z hz
       1161    apply Classical.byContradiction
       1162    intro hoff
       1163    exact hno ⟨z, hz, hoff⟩
       1164  
       1165  /-- Denying the hypothesis on a world with both symmetries posits a whole off-line orbit of four
       1166      points. -/
       1167  theorem denial_posits_the_orbit (Z : World) (hF : FoldClosed Z) (C : ConjSymmetry)
       1168      (hC : ∀ z, Z z → Z (C.conj z)) (h : ¬ RH Z) :
       1169      ∃ z, Z z ∧ ¬ onLine z ∧ Z (fold z) ∧ Z (C.conj z) ∧ Z (C.conj (fold z)) := by
       1170    obtain ⟨z, hz, hoff⟩ := not_rh_has_offline_witness Z h
       1171    exact ⟨z, hz, hoff, hF z hz, hC z hz, hC (fold z) (hF z hz)⟩
       1172  
       1173  /-- For every nonzero offset the pair world is fold-closed, fails the hypothesis, and shares the
       1174      record of W1. -/
       1175  theorem record_blind_at_every_scale (k : Int) (hk : k ≠ 0) :
       1176      RH W1 ∧ FoldClosed (pairAt k) ∧ ¬ RH (pairAt k) ∧ SameRecord W1 (pairAt k) :=
       1177    ⟨W1_rh, pair_closed k, pair_not_rh k hk, pair_same_record k⟩
       1178  
       1179  /-! ## VIII · Self-grounding supplies, and the five faces of the hypothesis -/
       1180  
       1181  /-- A self-grounding root, the structure of Appendix R in the same words: acts occur, and every act instances the root. -/
       1182  structure SelfGrounding (root : Prop) where
       1183    Act       : Type
       1184    anAct     : Act
       1185    instances : Act → root
       1186  
       1187  /-- A self-grounding supply of a proposition, with an act, exists exactly when the proposition
       1188      holds. -/
       1189  theorem supply_iff (root : Prop) : (∃ G : SelfGrounding root, Nonempty G.Act) ↔ root := by
       1190    constructor
       1191    · intro ⟨G, ⟨a⟩⟩
       1192      exact G.instances a
       1193    · intro hr
       1194      exact ⟨⟨Unit, (), fun _ => hr⟩, ⟨()⟩⟩
       1195  
       1196  /-- The five faces of the hypothesis. The equivalences are fields, carried as hypotheses and not
       1197      proved here: the critical line (Riemann 1859), Λ = 0 (Newman 1976; Rodgers and Tao 2020), the
       1198      faithfulness of the Liouville function (Landau 1899), and Weil positivity (Weil 1952). -/
       1199  structure Faces where
       1200    line : Prop
       1201    lamZero : Prop
       1202    faithful : Prop
       1203    weil : Prop
       1204    least : Prop
       1205    line_iff_least : line ↔ least
       1206    lam_iff_least : lamZero ↔ least
       1207    faith_iff_least : faithful ↔ least
       1208    weil_iff_least : weil ↔ least
       1209  
       1210  /-- Any one face implies all five. -/
       1211  theorem faces_are_one (H : Faces) :
       1212      (H.line ↔ H.least) ∧ (H.lamZero ↔ H.least) ∧ (H.faithful ↔ H.least) ∧ (H.weil ↔ H.least) :=
       1213    ⟨H.line_iff_least, H.lam_iff_least, H.faith_iff_least, H.weil_iff_least⟩
       1214  
       1215  /-- Given a self-grounding supply of the least-erasure face with an act, all five faces hold. -/
       1216  theorem rh_from_the_act_generic (H : Faces) (G : SelfGrounding H.least) (a : G.Act) :
       1217      H.line ∧ H.lamZero ∧ H.faithful ∧ H.weil ∧ H.least :=
       1218    let le := G.instances a
       1219    ⟨H.line_iff_least.mpr le, H.lam_iff_least.mpr le, H.faith_iff_least.mpr le,
       1220     H.weil_iff_least.mpr le, le⟩
       1221  
       1222  
       1223  /-! ## IX · Primes, the free basis and the identity arrow are keyless and force nothing -/
       1224  
       1225  /-- Primes exist. -/
       1226  theorem primes_exist : ∃ p, isPrime p :=
       1227    let ⟨p, hp, _⟩ := exists_prime_dvd 2 (by decide) (by decide)
       1228    ⟨p, hp⟩
       1229  
       1230  /-- The existence of primes holds on every world. -/
       1231  theorem primes_exist_keyless : Keyless (fun _ => ∃ p, isPrime p) := fun _ => primes_exist
       1232  
       1233  /-- The free basis at the primes holds on every world. -/
       1234  theorem prime_freedom_keyless :
       1235      Keyless (fun _ => ∀ p q, isPrime p → isPrime q → p ≠ q →
       1236        ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0) :=
       1237    fun _ => prime_freedom_independent
       1238  
       1239  /-- The identity arrow exists on every world. -/
       1240  theorem arrow_keyless : Keyless (fun _ => ∃ f : Nat → Nat, ∀ a, f a = a) :=
       1241    fun _ => arrow_exists Nat
       1242  
       1243  /-- The existence of primes forces nothing. -/
       1244  theorem primes_exist_forces_nothing : ¬ Forces (fun _ => ∃ p, isPrime p) :=
       1245    keyless_forces_nothing _ primes_exist_keyless
       1246  
       1247  /-- The free basis at the primes forces nothing. -/
       1248  theorem prime_freedom_forces_nothing :
       1249      ¬ Forces (fun _ => ∀ p q, isPrime p → isPrime q → p ≠ q →
       1250        ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0) :=
       1251    keyless_forces_nothing _ prime_freedom_keyless
       1252  
       1253  /-- The existence of the identity arrow forces nothing. -/
       1254  theorem arrow_forces_nothing : ¬ Forces (fun _ => ∃ f : Nat → Nat, ∀ a, f a = a) :=
       1255    keyless_forces_nothing _ arrow_keyless
       1256  
       1257  /-- The free basis holds, and a fold-closed world failing the hypothesis exists. -/
       1258  theorem free_basis_coexists_with_offline_world :
       1259      (∀ p q : Nat, isPrime p → isPrime q → p ≠ q →
       1260        ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0) ∧
       1261      ∃ Z, FoldClosed Z ∧ ¬ RH Z :=
       1262    ⟨prime_freedom_independent, W2, W2_closed, W2_not_rh⟩
       1263  
       1264  /-- An off-line point folds to a distinct off-line point, which no point registers to. -/
       1265  theorem fold_off_line_stays_off (z : Pt) (h : ¬ onLine z) :
       1266      ¬ onLine (fold z) ∧ fold z ≠ reg z ∧ fold z ≠ z :=
       1267    ⟨(fold_preserves_offline z).mpr h,
       1268     fun e => unicorn_never_registered (fold z) ((fold_preserves_offline z).mpr h) z e.symm,
       1269     fold_ne_of_offline z h⟩
       1270  
       1271  /-! ## X · The explicit formula as a structure; least erasure is Weil positivity -/
       1272  
       1273  structure ExplicitFormula where
       1274    /-- The value type of the two sides, with its order and its zero. -/
       1275    V : Type
       1276    le : V → V → Prop
       1277    zero : V
       1278    /-- The admissible test functions, their adjoint g ↦ g~, and their convolution. -/
       1279    T : Type
       1280    adj : T → T
       1281    conv : T → T → T
       1282    /-- The arithmetic side: the archimedean term with the sum over the primes. -/
       1283    primeSide : T → V
       1284    /-- The zero side: the sum over the zeros. -/
       1285    zeroSide : T → V
       1286    /-- The zeros, as a world on the chart. -/
       1287    zeros : World
       1288    /-- The explicit formula: the zero side of every test function equals its arithmetic side. Carried
       1289      as a hypothesis (Guinand 1948; Weil 1952). -/
       1290    identity : ∀ g, zeroSide g = primeSide g
       1291    /-- Weil's criterion: the arithmetic side is non-negative on every g ⋆ g̃ exactly when the zeros
       1292      lie on the line. Carried as a hypothesis (Weil 1952; Bombieri 2000). -/
       1293    positivity_iff_line : (∀ g, le zero (primeSide (conv g (adj g)))) ↔ RH zeros
       1294  
       1295  /-- Weil positivity, stated on the prime side. -/
       1296  def WeilPositive (E : ExplicitFormula) : Prop :=
       1297    ∀ g, E.le E.zero (E.primeSide (E.conv g (E.adj g)))
       1298  
       1299  /-- Through the identity, positivity reads the same on the zero side. -/
       1300  theorem positivity_on_zero_side (E : ExplicitFormula) :
       1301      WeilPositive E ↔ ∀ g, E.le E.zero (E.zeroSide (E.conv g (E.adj g))) := by
       1302    constructor
       1303    · intro h g
       1304      rw [E.identity]
       1305      exact h g
       1306    · intro h g
       1307      rw [← E.identity]
       1308      exact h g
       1309  
       1310  /-- Least erasure of the zeros of an explicit formula is Weil positivity of its arithmetic side. -/
       1311  theorem least_erasure_is_positivity (E : ExplicitFormula) :
       1312      LeastErasure E.zeros ↔ WeilPositive E :=
       1313    (least_erasure_is_the_value E.zeros).trans E.positivity_iff_line.symm
       1314  
       1315  /-- A self-grounding supply of Weil positivity exists exactly when the zeros lie on the line. -/
       1316  theorem prime_witness_iff (E : ExplicitFormula) :
       1317      (∃ G : SelfGrounding (WeilPositive E), Nonempty G.Act) ↔ RH E.zeros :=
       1318    (supply_iff (WeilPositive E)).trans E.positivity_iff_line
       1319  
       1320  /-- Weil positivity implies the hypothesis for the zeros of the explicit formula. -/
       1321  theorem rh_from_prime_witness (E : ExplicitFormula) (h : WeilPositive E) : RH E.zeros :=
       1322    E.positivity_iff_line.mp h
       1323  
       1324  /-- The positive instance: one test function, arithmetic side zero, zeros on the line. -/
       1325  def positiveInstance : ExplicitFormula where
       1326    V := Int
       1327    le := fun a b => a ≤ b
       1328    zero := 0
       1329    T := Unit
       1330    adj := id
       1331    conv := fun _ _ => ()
       1332    primeSide := fun _ => 0
       1333    zeroSide := fun _ => 0
       1334    zeros := W1
       1335    identity := fun _ => rfl
       1336    positivity_iff_line := ⟨fun _ => W1_rh, fun _ _ => Int.le_refl 0⟩
       1337  
       1338  /-- The negative instance: one test function, arithmetic side minus one, zeros off the line. -/
       1339  def negativeInstance : ExplicitFormula where
       1340    V := Int
       1341    le := fun a b => a ≤ b
       1342    zero := 0
       1343    T := Unit
       1344    adj := id
       1345    conv := fun _ _ => ()
       1346    primeSide := fun _ => -1
       1347    zeroSide := fun _ => -1
       1348    zeros := W2
       1349    identity := fun _ => rfl
       1350    positivity_iff_line :=
       1351      ⟨fun h => absurd (h ()) (by decide : ¬ ((0 : Int) ≤ -1)), fun h => absurd h W2_not_rh⟩
       1352  
       1353  /-- Two explicit formulas satisfy every field, one positive with its zeros on the line and one not
       1354      positive with its zeros off the line: no field decides positivity. -/
       1355  theorem positivity_is_keyed : WeilPositive positiveInstance ∧ ¬ WeilPositive negativeInstance :=
       1356    ⟨fun _ => Int.le_refl 0, fun h => absurd (h ()) (by decide : ¬ ((0 : Int) ≤ -1))⟩
       1357  
       1358  /-- The free basis holds in both instances. -/
       1359  theorem freedom_does_not_pick_the_sign :
       1360      (∀ p q : Nat, isPrime p → isPrime q → p ≠ q →
       1361        ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0) ∧
       1362      WeilPositive positiveInstance ∧ ¬ WeilPositive negativeInstance :=
       1363    ⟨prime_freedom_independent, positivity_is_keyed⟩
       1364  
       1365  /-- Section X, whole: the free basis; least erasure as the hypothesis and as positivity; the block;
       1366      keyless premises forcing nothing; positivity keyed. -/
       1367  theorem prime_witness_ledger :
       1368      (∀ f g : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f → CompletelyAdditive g →
       1369        (∀ p, isPrime p → f p = g p) → ∀ n, 0 < n → f n = g n) ∧
       1370      (∀ p q : Nat, isPrime p → isPrime q → p ≠ q →
       1371        ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0) ∧
       1372      (∀ Z : World, LeastErasure Z ↔ RH Z) ∧
       1373      (∀ E : ExplicitFormula, LeastErasure E.zeros ↔ WeilPositive E) ∧
       1374      (∀ g : World → Prop, RespectsRecord g → ¬ ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → (g Z ↔ RH Z)) ∧
       1375      (¬ Forces (fun _ => ∃ p, isPrime p)) ∧
       1376      (¬ Forces (fun _ => ∀ p q, isPrime p → isPrime q → p ≠ q →
       1377        ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0)) ∧
       1378      (¬ Forces (fun _ => ∃ f : Nat → Nat, ∀ a, f a = a)) ∧
       1379      (WeilPositive positiveInstance ∧ ¬ WeilPositive negativeInstance) :=
       1380    ⟨determined_by_primes, prime_freedom_independent, least_erasure_is_the_value,
       1381     least_erasure_is_positivity, unicorn_block, primes_exist_forces_nothing,
       1382     prime_freedom_forces_nothing, arrow_forces_nothing, positivity_is_keyed⟩
       1383  
       1384  /-! ## XI · The posit as a structure field -/
       1385  
       1386  /-- A zero set with its fold-closure and the one posit, least erasure. -/
       1387  structure ActualZeros where
       1388    /-- The zero set, as a world on the chart. -/
       1389    zeros : World
       1390    /-- The zero set is fold-closed (the functional equation, Riemann 1859). -/
       1391    fold_closed : FoldClosed zeros
       1392    /-- The posit: least erasure of the zero set. By least_erasure_is_the_value this field is the
       1393      hypothesis. -/
       1394    supply : LeastErasure zeros
       1395  
       1396  /-- From the posit, the hypothesis. -/
       1397  theorem rh_from_the_act (A : ActualZeros) : RH A.zeros :=
       1398    (least_erasure_is_the_value A.zeros).mp A.supply
       1399  
       1400  /-- The type of the posit is equivalent to the hypothesis. -/
       1401  theorem posit_is_the_conclusion (A : ActualZeros) : LeastErasure A.zeros ↔ RH A.zeros :=
       1402    least_erasure_is_the_value A.zeros
       1403  
       1404  /-- From the posit: the line, least erasure, every zero fixed by the fold and by registration, and
       1405      no off-line orbit. -/
       1406  theorem rh_ground_closure_complete (A : ActualZeros) :
       1407      RH A.zeros ∧ LeastErasure A.zeros ∧ (∀ z, A.zeros z → fold z = z) ∧
       1408      (∀ z, A.zeros z → reg z = z) ∧ ¬ Left A.zeros :=
       1409    ⟨rh_from_the_act A, A.supply,
       1410     fun z hz => (fold_fixed_iff z).mpr (rh_from_the_act A z hz),
       1411     fun z hz => reg_fixes_line z (rh_from_the_act A z hz),
       1412     (rh_iff_no_left A.zeros A.fold_closed).mp (rh_from_the_act A)⟩
       1413  
       1414  /-- An explicit formula for fold-closed zeros, with positivity posited. -/
       1415  structure PrimeAct where
       1416    E : ExplicitFormula
       1417    fold_closed : FoldClosed E.zeros
       1418    /-- The posit on the prime side: Weil positivity. -/
       1419    positive : WeilPositive E
       1420  
       1421  /-- A prime act is a least-erasure act. -/
       1422  def PrimeAct.toActual (P : PrimeAct) : ActualZeros :=
       1423    ⟨P.E.zeros, P.fold_closed, (least_erasure_is_positivity P.E).mpr P.positive⟩
       1424  
       1425  /-- From positivity posited, the hypothesis. -/
       1426  theorem rh_from_prime_act (P : PrimeAct) : RH P.E.zeros := rh_from_the_act P.toActual
       1427  
       1428  /-- For an explicit formula with fold-closed zeros, a positivity posit exists exactly when a
       1429      least-erasure posit exists for its zeros. -/
       1430  theorem acts_are_one (E : ExplicitFormula) (hF : FoldClosed E.zeros) :
       1431      (∃ P : PrimeAct, P.E = E) ↔ ∃ A : ActualZeros, A.zeros = E.zeros := by
       1432    constructor
       1433    · intro ⟨P, hP⟩
       1434      subst hP
       1435      exact ⟨P.toActual, rfl⟩
       1436    · intro ⟨A, hA⟩
       1437      refine ⟨⟨E, hF, (least_erasure_is_positivity E).mp ?_⟩, rfl⟩
       1438      rw [← hA]
       1439      exact A.supply
       1440  
       1441  
       1442  /-! ## XII · The block with no axiom: the pair world written out -/
       1443  
       1444  /-- The pair world at offset one, written out. -/
       1445  abbrev W2f : World := fun z => z = ⟨0, 14⟩ ∨ z = ⟨2, 14⟩
       1446  
       1447  theorem W2f_closed : FoldClosed W2f := by
       1448    intro z hz
       1449    rcases hz with h | h
       1450    · subst h; exact Or.inr rfl
       1451    · subst h; exact Or.inl rfl
       1452  
       1453  theorem W2f_not_rh : ¬ RH W2f :=
       1454    fun h => absurd (h ⟨0, 14⟩ (Or.inl rfl)) (by decide : ¬ ((0 : Int) = 1))
       1455  
       1456  theorem same_record_f : SameRecord W1 W2f := by
       1457    intro r
       1458    constructor
       1459    · intro ⟨s, hs, hr⟩
       1460      have h : s = ⟨1, 14⟩ := hs
       1461      subst h
       1462      exact ⟨⟨0, 14⟩, Or.inl rfl, hr⟩
       1463    · intro ⟨s, hs, hr⟩
       1464      rcases hs with h | h <;> subst h <;> exact ⟨⟨1, 14⟩, rfl, hr⟩
       1465  
       1466  /-- record_decides_nothing, with no axiom. -/
       1467  theorem record_decides_nothing_free (g : World → Prop) (hg : RespectsRecord g) :
       1468      ¬ ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → (g Z ↔ RH Z) := fun h =>
       1469    W2f_not_rh ((h W2f W2f_closed).mp ((hg W1 W2f same_record_f).mp ((h W1 W1_closed).mpr W1_rh)))
       1470  
       1471  /-- unicorn_block, with no axiom. -/
       1472  theorem unicorn_block_free (g : World → Prop) (hg : RespectsRecord g) :
       1473      ¬ ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → (g Z ↔ RH Z) := record_decides_nothing_free g hg
       1474  
       1475  /-- keyless_forces_nothing, with no axiom. -/
       1476  theorem keyless_forces_nothing_free (A : World → Prop) (hA : Keyless A) : ¬ Forces A :=
       1477    fun h => W2f_not_rh (h W2f W2f_closed (hA W2f))
       1478  
       1479  /-- arrow_forces_nothing, with no axiom. -/
       1480  theorem arrow_forces_nothing_free : ¬ Forces (fun _ => ∃ f : Nat → Nat, ∀ a, f a = a) :=
       1481    keyless_forces_nothing_free _ arrow_keyless
       1482  
       1483  /-- least_erasure_reads_past_the_record, with no axiom. -/
       1484  theorem least_erasure_reads_past_the_record_free : ¬ RespectsRecord LeastErasure := fun h =>
       1485    W2f_not_rh ((least_erasure_is_the_value W2f).mp
       1486      ((h W1 W2f same_record_f).mp ((least_erasure_is_the_value W1).mpr W1_rh)))
       1487  
       1488  /-- The negative instance on the explicit pair world. -/
       1489  def negativeInstanceF : ExplicitFormula where
       1490    V := Int
       1491    le := fun a b => a ≤ b
       1492    zero := 0
       1493    T := Unit
       1494    adj := id
       1495    conv := fun _ _ => ()
       1496    primeSide := fun _ => -1
       1497    zeroSide := fun _ => -1
       1498    zeros := W2f
       1499    identity := fun _ => rfl
       1500    positivity_iff_line :=
       1501      ⟨fun h => absurd (h ()) (by decide : ¬ ((0 : Int) ≤ -1)), fun h => absurd h W2f_not_rh⟩
       1502  
       1503  /-- positivity_is_keyed, with no axiom. -/
       1504  theorem positivity_is_keyed_free : WeilPositive positiveInstance ∧ ¬ WeilPositive negativeInstanceF :=
       1505    ⟨fun _ => Int.le_refl 0, fun h => absurd (h ()) (by decide : ¬ ((0 : Int) ≤ -1))⟩
       1506  
       1507  
       1508  /-! ## XIII · The hypothesis on the supplied bit -/
       1509  
       1510  /-- For every explicit formula, Weil positivity is equivalent to the hypothesis for its zeros. -/
       1511  theorem spend_is_the_line (E : ExplicitFormula) : WeilPositive E ↔ RH E.zeros :=
       1512    E.positivity_iff_line
       1513  
       1514  /-- The free basis holds, and an explicit formula exists on which positivity fails: the free basis
       1515      and positivity are distinct. -/
       1516  theorem spend_is_not_the_free_basis :
       1517      (∀ p q : Nat, isPrime p → isPrime q → p ≠ q →
       1518        ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0) ∧
       1519      ∃ E : ExplicitFormula, ¬ WeilPositive E :=
       1520    ⟨prime_freedom_independent, negativeInstanceF, positivity_is_keyed_free.2⟩
       1521  
       1522  /-- From positivity posited: the line, least erasure, positivity, every zero fixed by the fold and
       1523      by registration, and no off-line orbit. -/
       1524  theorem rh_on_the_spent_bit (P : PrimeAct) :
       1525      RH P.E.zeros ∧ LeastErasure P.E.zeros ∧ WeilPositive P.E ∧
       1526      (∀ z, P.E.zeros z → fold z = z) ∧ (∀ z, P.E.zeros z → reg z = z) ∧ ¬ Left P.E.zeros :=
       1527    let c := rh_ground_closure_complete P.toActual
       1528    ⟨c.1, c.2.1, P.positive, c.2.2.1, c.2.2.2.1, c.2.2.2.2⟩
       1529  
       1530  /-- Sections X to XIII, whole. -/
       1531  theorem prime_arc_sealed :
       1532      (∀ f g : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f → CompletelyAdditive g →
       1533        (∀ p, isPrime p → f p = g p) → ∀ n, 0 < n → f n = g n) ∧
       1534      (∀ p q : Nat, isPrime p → isPrime q → p ≠ q →
       1535        ∃ f : Nat → Int, CompletelyAdditive f ∧ f p = 1 ∧ f q = 0 ∧ f 1 = 0) ∧
       1536      (∀ Z : World, LeastErasure Z ↔ RH Z) ∧
       1537      (∀ E : ExplicitFormula, LeastErasure E.zeros ↔ WeilPositive E) ∧
       1538      (∀ E : ExplicitFormula, WeilPositive E ↔ RH E.zeros) ∧
       1539      (∀ g : World → Prop, RespectsRecord g → ¬ ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → (g Z ↔ RH Z)) ∧
       1540      (∀ A : World → Prop, Keyless A → ¬ Forces A) ∧
       1541      (WeilPositive positiveInstance ∧ ¬ WeilPositive negativeInstanceF) ∧
       1542      (∃ E : ExplicitFormula, ¬ WeilPositive E) ∧
       1543      (∀ P : PrimeAct, RH P.E.zeros) :=
       1544    ⟨determined_by_primes, prime_freedom_independent, least_erasure_is_the_value,
       1545     least_erasure_is_positivity, spend_is_the_line, record_decides_nothing_free,
       1546     keyless_forces_nothing_free, positivity_is_keyed_free, spend_is_not_the_free_basis.2,
       1547     rh_from_prime_act⟩
       1548  
       1549  
       1550  /-! ## XIV · The weakest forcing premise; the Li and de Bruijn–Newman coordinates -/
       1551  
       1552  /-- The hypothesis forces the line, and every premise that forces the line implies the hypothesis
       1553      on every fold-closed world. -/
       1554  theorem rh_is_the_weakest_forcing_premise :
       1555      Forces RH ∧ ∀ A : World → Prop, Forces A → ∀ Z, FoldClosed Z → A Z → RH Z :=
       1556    ⟨fun _ _ h => h, fun _ hA Z hZ ha => hA Z hZ ha⟩
       1557  
       1558  /-- A premise that holds at some fold-closed world where the hypothesis fails does not force. -/
       1559  theorem weaker_never_forces (A : World → Prop) (Z : World) (hZ : FoldClosed Z) (ha : A Z)
       1560      (hn : ¬ RH Z) : ¬ Forces A :=
       1561    fun h => hn (h Z hZ ha)
       1562  
       1563  /-- A premise true on W2f forces nothing. -/
       1564  theorem weaker_at_the_twin_never_forces (A : World → Prop) (ha : A W2f) : ¬ Forces A :=
       1565    weaker_never_forces A W2f W2f_closed ha W2f_not_rh
       1566  
       1567  /-- A zero set with the signs of its Li coefficients: the hypothesis holds exactly when every
       1568      coefficient is non-negative. Carried as a hypothesis (Li 1997; Bombieri and Lagarias 1999). -/
       1569  structure LiStream where
       1570    zeros : World
       1571    nonneg : Nat → Prop
       1572    li : RH zeros ↔ ∀ n, 1 ≤ n → nonneg n
       1573  
       1574  theorem rh_from_li (L : LiStream) (h : ∀ n, 1 ≤ n → L.nonneg n) : RH L.zeros := L.li.mpr h
       1575  
       1576  theorem li_is_the_bit_stream (L : LiStream) : (∀ n, 1 ≤ n → L.nonneg n) ↔ RH L.zeros := L.li.symm
       1577  
       1578  /-- For every N there is a Li stream non-negative below N whose zero set lies off the line. -/
       1579  theorem li_prefix_never_forces (N : Nat) :
       1580      ∃ L : LiStream, (∀ n, n < N → L.nonneg n) ∧ ¬ RH L.zeros :=
       1581    ⟨⟨W2f, fun n => n < N,
       1582      ⟨fun h => absurd h W2f_not_rh,
       1583       fun h => absurd (h (N + 1) (Nat.succ_pos N))
       1584         (fun c => Nat.lt_irrefl N (Nat.lt_trans (Nat.lt_succ_self N) c))⟩⟩,
       1585     fun _ h => h, W2f_not_rh⟩
       1586  
       1587  /-- The de Bruijn–Newman constant over an ordered type: Λ and its zero, the order's reflexivity and
       1588      antisymmetry, 0 ≤ Λ (Rodgers and Tao 2020), and the hypothesis exactly when Λ = 0 (Newman
       1589      1976). Every field is carried as a hypothesis. -/
       1590  structure DBN (V : Type) [LE V] where
       1591    zeros : World
       1592    lam : V
       1593    zero : V
       1594    refl : ∀ a : V, a ≤ a
       1595    antisymm : ∀ a b : V, a ≤ b → b ≤ a → a = b
       1596    lower : zero ≤ lam
       1597    rh_iff : RH zeros ↔ lam = zero
       1598  
       1599  /-- From Λ ≤ 0 and the cited 0 ≤ Λ, the hypothesis. -/
       1600  theorem rh_from_the_sign {V : Type} [LE V] (D : DBN V) (h : D.lam ≤ D.zero) : RH D.zeros :=
       1601    D.rh_iff.mpr (D.antisymm _ _ h D.lower)
       1602  
       1603  /-- The hypothesis is equivalent to Λ ≤ 0. -/
       1604  theorem rh_iff_the_sign {V : Type} [LE V] (D : DBN V) : RH D.zeros ↔ D.lam ≤ D.zero :=
       1605    ⟨fun h => by rw [D.rh_iff.mp h]; exact D.refl _, rh_from_the_sign D⟩
       1606  
       1607  /-- On one zero set, Weil positivity and Λ ≤ 0 are equivalent. -/
       1608  theorem spends_are_one {V : Type} [LE V] (P : PrimeAct) (D : DBN V) (same : D.zeros = P.E.zeros) :
