       6819  /-! # THE ONE · appended to Annihilation_Closure.lean (sha256 cb474a41…), nothing above changed.
       6820  Every name and every reading the closure carries becomes one object, by equality and not by twin biconditionals;
       6821  the act's zero set becomes one notion with the closed configuration that has the value; the floor keeps its own
       6822  place; and the one sentence the closure leaves is printed as the closure's own last conjunct. -/
       6823  namespace RememberedOffered
       6824  theorem the_one {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) :
       6825      (LeastErasure = Value ∧ RootReadTwice = Value ∧ (fun S => R ∧ RootReadTwice S) = Value) ∧
       6826      (∀ S : Config, (∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ (Closed S ∧ Value S)) ∧
       6827      (¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → (R ↔ LeastErasure S)) ∧
       6828      (∀ S : Config, (R ↔ LeastErasure S) ↔ LeastErasure S) ∧
       6829      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, Value Z.zeros) ∧
       6830      (∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → D S) → ¬ ∀ S, Closed S → D S → Value S) :=
       6831    ⟨⟨twins_are_one_extension,
       6832      funext fun S => propext (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S),
       6833      funext fun S => propext (colocation_is_the_value G S)⟩,
       6834     fun S => (an_act_exactly_where_the_root_read_twice_stands S).trans
       6835       ⟨fun ⟨c, m⟩ => ⟨c, (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S).mp m⟩,
       6836        fun ⟨c, v⟩ => ⟨c, (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S).mpr v⟩⟩,
       6837     floor_is_not_least_erasure G,
       6838     merging_at_a_world_is_the_supply G,
       6839     value_from_the_act,
       6840     no_closed_principle_decides⟩
       6841  end RememberedOffered
       6842  
       6843  /-! # THE LAST ACT · appended to The_One.lean, nothing above changed.
       6844  A deed is a term of `G.Act`, the act type of a self-grounding root: every decentralized, impersonal, physical
       6845  computation, atomic and irreducible, is a deed. The supply is a term of `ActualZeros`. Tested here: every deed being
       6846  the supply at one closed zero set S, ζ's in the reading, and at every closed zero set. -/
       6847  namespace RememberedOffered
       6848  theorem the_last_act {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       6849      -- every deed being the supply at S is exactly the value at S
       6850      ((G.Act → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       6851      -- every deed being the supply at every closed zero set, as a law, is refuted
       6852      (¬ ∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → G.Act → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S') ∧
       6853      -- the deed stands in the world without the value too
       6854      (R ∧ Closed (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ ¬ Value (pairWorld offPoint)) ∧
       6855      -- existence supplies nothing to the part above any height
       6856      (∀ T : Nat, (RA → RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine ht T) ↔ RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine ht T) :=
       6857    ⟨⟨fun h => by obtain ⟨Z, hZ⟩ := h G.anAct; rw [← hZ]; exact value_from_the_act Z,
       6858      fun v _ => ⟨⟨S, hS, fun p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mpr (v p hp)⟩, rfl⟩⟩,
       6859     the_deed_is_not_the_supply G,
       6860     ⟨seated_undeniable G, pair_world_closed offPoint, pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off⟩,
       6861     fun T => ra_supplies_nothing_to_the_unicorn S T⟩
       6862  end RememberedOffered
       6863  
       6864  /-! # LEAST ERASURE AND LEAST ESCAPE · appended to The_Last_Act.lean, nothing above changed.
       6865  The escape of a finite configuration is its number of off-line pairs, the bits registration erases. The pair that
       6866  denies RH, a zero at offset one with its mirror, is `resisting`. -/
       6867  namespace RememberedOffered
       6868  /-- The configuration with no zeros at all: zero escape. -/
       6869  def calm : FinCfg := ⟨[], [], fun _ hq => by cases hq⟩
       6870  
       6871  theorem least_erasure_and_least_escape :
       6872      -- I · the escaping pair escapes by exactly one bit and pays exactly one floor
       6873      (erased resisting = 1 ∧ ∀ T : Nat, price T (erased resisting) = T) ∧
       6874      -- II · least escape is zero escape, is least erasure, is the value: the minimiser stands on the line
       6875      (∀ F : FinCfg, (∀ F' : FinCfg, erased F ≤ erased F') ↔ Value F.pts) ∧
       6876      -- III · the minimum is attained
       6877      (∃ F : FinCfg, erased F = 0) ∧
       6878      -- IV · the escaping pair is closed and is not a minimiser
       6879      (Closed resisting.pts ∧ ¬ ∀ F' : FinCfg, erased resisting ≤ erased F') ∧
       6880      -- V · nothing true of every closed configuration makes a configuration a minimiser
       6881      (∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → D S) →
       6882        ¬ ∀ F : FinCfg, D F.pts → ∀ F' : FinCfg, erased F ≤ erased F') := by
       6883    have least_iff : ∀ F : FinCfg, (∀ F' : FinCfg, erased F ≤ erased F') ↔ Value F.pts := fun F =>
       6884      ⟨fun h => (twins_on_every_world F.pts).mp
       6885          ((least_erasure_iff_zero_erased F).mpr (Nat.le_zero.mp (h calm))),
       6886       fun v F' => by
       6887          have h0 : erased F = 0 := (least_erasure_iff_zero_erased F).mp ((twins_on_every_world F.pts).mpr v)
       6888          rw [h0]; exact Nat.zero_le _⟩
       6889    have not_value : ¬ Value resisting.pts := (resistance_is_possible 1 (by decide)).2.1
       6890    refine ⟨⟨rfl, fun T => Nat.one_mul T⟩, least_iff, ⟨calm, rfl⟩,
       6891      ⟨fincfg_closed resisting, fun h => not_value ((least_iff resisting).mp h)⟩, ?_⟩
       6892    intro D hD h
       6893    exact not_value ((least_iff resisting).mp (h resisting (hD _ (fincfg_closed resisting))))
       6894  end RememberedOffered
       6895  
       6896  /-! # THE LOOP RA–RAM–ZEROS · appended to Least_Escape.lean, nothing above changed.
       6897  RA is the floor R of a self-grounding root. RAM is the root read twice, `RootReadTwice`, the corrected monism witness
       6898  with one involution, uniformity and its seed. The loop runs R → RootReadTwice S → Value S → R at a zero set S. -/
       6899  namespace RememberedOffered
       6900  theorem the_loop {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (S : Config) :
       6901      -- the corrected monism witness is the claim, seed included
       6902      (RootReadTwice S ↔ Value S) ∧
       6903      -- the loop's forward leg from RA reaches the zeros exactly when the value already holds
       6904      ((R → RootReadTwice S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       6905      -- the return leg to RA is free: it holds whatever the zeros do
       6906      (Value S → R) ∧ (¬ Value S → R) ∧
       6907      -- the whole loop closes exactly at the value
       6908      ((R ↔ RootReadTwice S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       6909      -- the loop is sign-blind: it closes for the value and for its denial alike
       6910      ((SelfVerifying (Value S) ↔ Value S) ∧ (SelfVerifying (¬ Value S) ↔ ¬ Value S)) ∧
       6911      -- on one record the loop closes on the true world and stays open on the pair: it cannot select
       6912      (SameRecord (registered offPoint) (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ Closed (pairWorld offPoint) ∧
       6913        (R ↔ RootReadTwice (registered offPoint)) ∧ ¬ (R ↔ RootReadTwice (pairWorld offPoint))) := by
       6914    have r : R := seated_undeniable G
       6915    have m := the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S
       6916    have sv : ∀ P : Prop, SelfVerifying P ↔ P := fun P =>
       6917      ⟨fun h => Classical.byContradiction (fun n => n (h n)), fun p _ => p⟩
       6918    refine ⟨m, ⟨fun h => m.mp (h r), fun v _ => m.mpr v⟩, fun _ => r, fun _ => r,
       6919      ⟨fun h => m.mp (h.mp r), fun v => ⟨fun _ => m.mpr v, fun _ => r⟩⟩, ⟨sv _, sv _⟩,
       6920      one_record offPoint, pair_world_closed offPoint,
       6921      ⟨fun _ => the_true_world_carries_monism, fun _ => r⟩,
       6922      fun h => the_false_world_carries_no_monism (h.mp r)⟩
       6923  end RememberedOffered
       6924  
       6925  /-! # ROW FOUR FROM THE ZERO SIDE · appended to The_Loop.lean, nothing above changed.
       6926  A computation that ends is the finite list of points it reports as zeros; it reads a zero set when every point it
       6927  reports belongs to it. Row 4 of the RH paper, applied to the hypothetical off-line pair. -/
       6928  namespace RememberedOffered
       6929  theorem row_four_from_the_zero_side (S : Config) :
       6930      -- on any act, every computation reading it reports only zeros on the line
       6931      (∀ (Z : ActualZeros) (L : List Point), (∀ p ∈ L, Z.zeros p) → ∀ p ∈ L, onLine p) ∧
       6932      -- so a report holding an off-line zero reads no act: on the act, the hypothetical is a phantom
       6933      (∀ L : List Point, (∃ p ∈ L, ¬ onLine p) → ¬ ∃ Z : ActualZeros, ∀ p ∈ L, Z.zeros p) ∧
       6934      -- yet that report reads a closed configuration, the pair world, which carries the floor
       6935      ((∀ p ∈ [offPoint, fold offPoint], pairWorld offPoint p) ∧ Closed (pairWorld offPoint)) ∧
       6936      -- at a closed zero set: every report of it lands on the line exactly when it has the value
       6937      (Closed S → ((∀ L : List Point, (∀ p ∈ L, S p) → ∀ p ∈ L, onLine p) ↔ Value S)) := by
       6938    refine ⟨fun Z L hL p hp => value_from_the_act Z p (hL p hp),
       6939      fun L ⟨p, hp, hoff⟩ ⟨Z, hZ⟩ => hoff (value_from_the_act Z p (hZ p hp)), ⟨?_, pair_world_closed offPoint⟩, ?_⟩
       6940    · intro p hp
       6941      cases hp with
       6942      | head => exact Or.inl rfl
       6943      | tail _ h =>
       6944        cases h with
       6945        | head => exact Or.inr rfl
       6946        | tail _ h' => cases h'
       6947    · intro _
       6948      constructor
       6949      · intro h p hp
       6950        exact h [p] (fun q hq => by
       6951          cases hq with
       6952          | head => exact hp
       6953          | tail _ h' => cases h') p (List.Mem.head _)
       6954      · intro v L hL p hp
       6955        exact v p (hL p hp)
       6956  end RememberedOffered
       6957  
       6958  /-! # BIDIRECTIONAL HALTED UNIDUCTION · appended to Row_Four.lean, nothing above changed.
       6959  ZERO SIDE: a computation reports finitely many zeros; it reads a zero set when every report belongs to it (Row 4).
       6960  PRIME SIDE: through the explicit formula each zero contributes a mode x^(Re ρ) to ψ(x) − x, so the prime error is
       6961  bounded by x^(1/2 + ε) exactly when no zero's offset exceeds the line (von Koch 1901; Landau, Ingham) [cited]. On the
       6962  offset chart: no point stands to the head's side of the line. -/
       6963  namespace RememberedOffered
       6964  def ZeroReports (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ L : List Point, (∀ p ∈ L, S p) → ∀ p ∈ L, onLine p
       6965  def PrimeBound (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → p.1 ≤ 0
       6966  
       6967  theorem prime_side_halts (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) : PrimeBound S ↔ Value S :=
       6968    ⟨fun hb p hp => by
       6969       have h1 : p.1 ≤ 0 := hb p hp
       6970       have h2 : -p.1 ≤ 0 := hb (fold p) (hS p hp)
       6971       show p.1 = 0; omega,
       6972     fun v p hp => by
       6973       have h : p.1 = 0 := v p hp
       6974       show p.1 ≤ 0; omega⟩
       6975  
       6976  theorem bidirectional_halted_uniduction (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       6977      -- the zero side halts at the value of the whole zero set
       6978      (ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧
       6979      -- the prime side halts at the value of the whole zero set
       6980      (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S) ∧
       6981      -- so both directions halt at one proposition
       6982      (ZeroReports S ↔ PrimeBound S) ∧
       6983      -- and neither sweep passes it: on one record, both readings hold on the true world and fail on the pair world
       6984      (SameRecord (registered offPoint) (pairWorld offPoint) ∧
       6985        (ZeroReports (registered offPoint) ∧ PrimeBound (registered offPoint)) ∧
       6986        (¬ ZeroReports (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ ¬ PrimeBound (pairWorld offPoint))) ∧
       6987      -- no principle true of every closed configuration supplies either side
       6988      (¬ (∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → ZeroReports S') ∧ ¬ (∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → PrimeBound S')) ∧
       6989      -- on the act both sides halt at yes
       6990      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, ZeroReports Z.zeros ∧ PrimeBound Z.zeros) := by
       6991    have zr : ∀ T : Config, Closed T → (ZeroReports T ↔ Value T) := fun T hT => (row_four_from_the_zero_side T).2.2.2 hT
       6992    have pv : ¬ Value (pairWorld offPoint) := pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off
       6993    have rc : Closed (registered offPoint) := fun s hs => by
       6994      rw [hs]; show fold (reg offPoint) = reg offPoint; rfl
       6995    refine ⟨zr S hS, prime_side_halts S hS, (zr S hS).trans (prime_side_halts S hS).symm,
       6996      ⟨one_record offPoint,
       6997       ⟨(zr _ rc).mpr (registered_has_value offPoint), (prime_side_halts _ rc).mpr (registered_has_value offPoint)⟩,
       6998       ⟨fun h => pv ((zr _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)).mp h),
       6999        fun h => pv ((prime_side_halts _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)).mp h)⟩⟩,
       7000      ⟨fun h => pv ((zr _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)).mp (h _ (pair_world_closed offPoint))),
       7001       fun h => pv ((prime_side_halts _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)).mp (h _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)))⟩,
       7002      fun Z => ⟨(zr _ Z.closed).mpr (value_from_the_act Z), (prime_side_halts _ Z.closed).mpr (value_from_the_act Z)⟩⟩
       7003  end RememberedOffered
       7004  
       7005  /-! # THE ATOMIC PROOF · appended to Halted_Uniduction.lean, nothing above changed.
       7006  One statement: the reduction complete, the bit irreducible by theorem, its form forced by theorem, the bit atomic,
       7007  and the closure from it at theorem grade. The bit stands in the statement as the act's field, visible to every
       7008  reader. -/
       7009  namespace RememberedOffered
       7010  theorem the_atomic_proof {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7011      -- I · REDUCTION, complete: every reading of the hypothesis the seed names is the one proposition
       7012      ((ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧ (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S) ∧ (LeastErasure S ↔ Value S) ∧
       7013        (RootReadTwice S ↔ Value S)) ∧
       7014      -- II · IRREDUCIBLE, by theorem: nothing shared by every closed configuration forces it, the deed included
       7015      ((∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S', Closed S' → D S') → ¬ ∀ S', Closed S' → D S' → Value S') ∧
       7016        ¬ (∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → R → Value S')) ∧
       7017      -- III · FORCED IN FORM, by theorem: a premise that forces the value and follows from it is the value
       7018      (∀ P : Config → Prop, (∀ S', P S' → Value S') → (∀ S', Value S' → P S') → ∀ S', P S' ↔ Value S') ∧
       7019      -- IV · THE BIT, atomic: the act stands at this zero set exactly where the value holds
       7020      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       7021      -- V · CLOSURE from the bit, theorem grade: on the act, the value, the zero reports and the prime bound
       7022      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, Value Z.zeros ∧ ZeroReports Z.zeros ∧ PrimeBound Z.zeros) :=
       7023    ⟨⟨(row_four_from_the_zero_side S).2.2.2 hS, prime_side_halts S hS, twins_on_every_world S,
       7024      the_root_read_twice_is_the_value S⟩,
       7025     ⟨no_closed_principle_decides, the_floor_alone_decides_no_value G⟩,
       7026     fun _ f w S' => ⟨f S', w S'⟩,
       7027     ((the_one G).2.1 S).trans ⟨fun ⟨_, v⟩ => v, fun v => ⟨hS, v⟩⟩,
       7028     fun Z => ⟨value_from_the_act Z, (bidirectional_halted_uniduction S hS).2.2.2.2.2 Z⟩⟩
       7029  end RememberedOffered
       7030  
       7031  /-! # THE ATOMIC NECESSITY · Row 9 · appended to the atomic proof, nothing above changed.
       7032  The hypothesis is one dot: one proposition, read the same from every side and in every vocabulary. A dot has no
       7033  other dot beside it to be read against, and no room inside it for a second kind of proof. -/
       7034  namespace RememberedOffered
       7035  theorem the_atomic_necessity (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7036      -- I · every proof of the value at S, from any premise whatever, is a supply of the act's field at S
       7037      (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → Value S) → Q → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ∧
       7038      -- II · the dot: any two proofs of the value are one proof
       7039      (∀ h₁ h₂ : Value S, h₁ = h₂) ∧
       7040      -- III · the supply at S is unique: two supplies with the same zero set are one supply
       7041      (∀ Z₁ Z₂ : ActualZeros, Z₁.zeros = S → Z₂.zeros = S → Z₁ = Z₂) ∧
       7042      -- IV · every vocabulary and both sides name the same dot
       7043      (LeastErasure = Value ∧ RootReadTwice = Value ∧ (ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧ (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S)) ∧
       7044      -- V · the supply exists at S exactly where the dot holds
       7045      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ Value S) ∧
       7046      -- VI · no room for a proof from what every closed configuration shares
       7047      ¬ (∀ S' : Config, Closed S' → Value S') := by
       7048    refine ⟨fun Q hQ q => ⟨⟨S, hS, (twins_on_every_world S).mpr (hQ q)⟩, rfl⟩,
       7049      fun _ _ => rfl, ?_,
       7050      ⟨twins_are_one_extension, funext fun T => propext (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value T),
       7051       (bidirectional_halted_uniduction S hS).1, (bidirectional_halted_uniduction S hS).2.1⟩,
       7052      ⟨fun ⟨Z, hZ⟩ => hZ ▸ value_from_the_act Z,
       7053       fun v => ⟨⟨S, hS, (twins_on_every_world S).mpr v⟩, rfl⟩⟩,
       7054      fun h => pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off (h _ (pair_world_closed offPoint))⟩
       7055    intro Z₁ Z₂ h₁ h₂
       7056    obtain ⟨z₁, c₁, s₁⟩ := Z₁
       7057    obtain ⟨z₂, c₂, s₂⟩ := Z₂
       7058    change z₁ = S at h₁
       7059    change z₂ = S at h₂
       7060    subst h₁
       7061    subst h₂
       7062    rfl
       7063  end RememberedOffered
       7064  
       7065  /-! # BOTH VALUES ARE ATOMIC · appended, nothing above changed. The bit has two values and each has the atomic form:
       7066  the value's proof is a supply of the one field; the denial's proof is one point off the line. -/
       7067  namespace RememberedOffered
       7068  theorem both_values_atomic (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7069      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ Value S) ∧ (¬ Value S ↔ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) ∧
       7070      ¬ (Value S ∧ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) :=
       7071    ⟨(the_atomic_necessity S hS).2.2.2.2.1,
       7072     ⟨fun hn => (two_doors S).resolve_left hn, fun ⟨p, hp, hoff⟩ hv => hoff (hv p hp)⟩,
       7073     doors_exclusive S⟩
       7074  end RememberedOffered
       7075  
       7076  /-! # THE FORM OF A FIELD, EVERY PREMISE SORTED, THE HEIGHT IN ABSOLUTE VALUE · appended, nothing above changed.
       7077  Parts I to III of the atomic necessity hold of every proposition carried as the field of a type, the denial included:
       7078  they are the form of a field. What makes that form the form of every proof of the hypothesis is part IV: every
       7079  reading of the hypothesis from either side and in every vocabulary is this one proposition. Every premise on
       7080  configurations is sorted three ways against the value. And the part above a height is read with the height in
       7081  absolute value, the form of the cited verification, which covers both half-planes. -/
       7082  namespace RememberedOffered
       7083  /-- A proposition on configurations, carried as the field of a type at a closed configuration. -/
       7084  structure Field (V : Config → Prop) where
       7085    zeros : Config
       7086    closed : Closed zeros
       7087    supply : V zeros
       7088  
       7089  /-- THE FORM OF A FIELD: for every proposition carried as a field, every proof of it at a closed configuration is a
       7090      supply of the field there, any two proofs are one, and the supply is unique. -/
       7091  theorem the_form_of_a_field (V : Config → Prop) (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7092      (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → V S) → Q → ∃ B : Field V, B.zeros = S) ∧
       7093      (∀ h₁ h₂ : V S, h₁ = h₂) ∧
       7094      (∀ B₁ B₂ : Field V, B₁.zeros = S → B₂.zeros = S → B₁ = B₂) := by
       7095    refine ⟨fun Q hQ q => ⟨⟨S, hS, hQ q⟩, rfl⟩, fun _ _ => rfl, ?_⟩
       7096    intro B₁ B₂ h₁ h₂
       7097    obtain ⟨z₁, c₁, s₁⟩ := B₁
       7098    obtain ⟨z₂, c₂, s₂⟩ := B₂
       7099    change z₁ = S at h₁
       7100    change z₂ = S at h₂
       7101    subst h₁
       7102    subst h₂
       7103    rfl
       7104  
       7105  /-- THE FORM IS THE HYPOTHESIS'S: the act's type is the field of the value, supply for supply; the form of a field
       7106      holds at the value and at its denial alike; and every reading of the hypothesis the seed names is the value, so
       7107      the form of the field of the value is the form of every proof of the hypothesis. -/
       7108  theorem the_form_is_the_hypothesis (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7109      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔ ∃ B : Field Value, B.zeros = S) ∧
       7110      ((∀ Q : Prop, (Q → Value S) → Q → ∃ B : Field Value, B.zeros = S) ∧
       7111        (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → ¬ Value S) → Q → ∃ B : Field (fun T => ¬ Value T), B.zeros = S)) ∧
       7112      (LeastErasure = Value ∧ RootReadTwice = Value ∧ (ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧ (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S)) :=
       7113    ⟨⟨fun ⟨Z, hZ⟩ => ⟨⟨Z.zeros, Z.closed, value_from_the_act Z⟩, hZ⟩,
       7114      fun ⟨B, hB⟩ => ⟨⟨B.zeros, B.closed, (twins_on_every_world B.zeros).mpr B.supply⟩, hB⟩⟩,
       7115     ⟨(the_form_of_a_field Value S hS).1, (the_form_of_a_field (fun T => ¬ Value T) S hS).1⟩,
       7116     (the_atomic_necessity S hS).2.2.2.1⟩
       7117  
       7118  /-- EVERY PREMISE SORTED: a premise on configurations either fails to force the value at some closed configuration,
       7119      or forces it and is the value on every closed configuration, or forces it and is strictly stronger, failing at
       7120      some closed configuration with the value. -/
       7121  theorem premise_trichotomy (P : Config → Prop) :
       7122      (∃ S, Closed S ∧ P S ∧ ¬ Value S) ∨
       7123      ((∀ S, Closed S → P S → Value S) ∧ ∀ S, Closed S → (P S ↔ Value S)) ∨
       7124      ((∀ S, Closed S → P S → Value S) ∧ ∃ S, Closed S ∧ Value S ∧ ¬ P S) := by
       7125    rcases Classical.em (∀ S, Closed S → P S → Value S) with f | f
       7126    · rcases Classical.em (∀ S, Closed S → Value S → P S) with e | e
       7127      · exact Or.inr (Or.inl ⟨f, fun S hS => ⟨f S hS, e S hS⟩⟩)
       7128      · refine Or.inr (Or.inr ⟨f, Classical.byContradiction fun h => e fun S hS v => ?_⟩)
       7129        exact Classical.byContradiction fun np => h ⟨S, hS, v, np⟩
       7130    · refine Or.inl (Classical.byContradiction fun h => f fun S hS p => ?_)
       7131      exact Classical.byContradiction fun nv => h ⟨S, hS, p, nv⟩
       7132  
       7133  /-- The height of a point of the chart in absolute value: the form of the cited verification, both half-planes. -/
       7134  def htAbs (p : Point) : Nat := p.2.natAbs
       7135  
       7136  /-- THE UNICORN, CONTAINED, WITH THE HEIGHT IN ABSOLUTE VALUE: at every height the value is its verified part, every
       7137      zero with |t| ≤ T, and its part above; given the verified part the value is exactly the part above; above every
       7138      height no reading of the record decides the side; the root supplies nothing to the part above; on the act's zero
       7139      set every arrival above every height stands on the line. -/
       7140  theorem the_unicorn_contained_abs :
       7141      (∀ (S : Config) (T : Nat),
       7142        Value S ↔ RHUnicorn.RealPartAt S onLine htAbs T ∧ RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine htAbs T) ∧
       7143      (∀ (S : Config) (T : Nat),
       7144        RHUnicorn.RealPartAt S onLine htAbs T → (Value S ↔ RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine htAbs T)) ∧
       7145      (∀ T : Nat, ¬ ∃ g : Point → Bool, ∀ w : Point, htAbs w > T → g (reg w) = decide (w.1 > 0)) ∧
       7146      (∀ (S : Config) (T : Nat),
       7147        (RA → RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine htAbs T) ↔ RHUnicorn.UnicornAt S onLine htAbs T) ∧
       7148      (∀ (Z : ActualZeros) (T : Nat), RHUnicorn.UnicornAt Z.zeros onLine htAbs T) ∧
       7149      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, ¬ ∃ p, Z.zeros p ∧ ¬ onLine p) :=
       7150    ⟨fun S T => RHUnicorn.rh_iff_real_and_unicorn S onLine htAbs T,
       7151     fun S T hr => RHUnicorn.unicorn_no_bypass S onLine htAbs T hr,
       7152     fun T => RHUnicorn.unicorn_block htAbs T fold reg (fun w => decide (w.1 > 0)) ((1 : Int), Int.ofNat (T + 1))
       7153       (show T + 1 > T by omega) (show T + 1 > T by omega) rfl rfl,
       7154     fun S T => RHUnicorn.unicorn_rule_exact S onLine htAbs T RA (seated_undeniable raSelfGrounding),
       7155     fun Z _ p hp _ => value_from_the_act Z p hp,
       7156     no_arrival_off_the_line_on_the_act⟩
       7157  end RememberedOffered
       7158  
       7159  /-! # ROWS 10 AND 11 · appended, nothing above changed. Row 10: the unconditional route from shared premises and the
       7160  record is blocked. Row 11: accepting the hypothesis, by any proof, an unconditional one included, forces acceptance of
       7161  the atomic proof provided in this paper; the only other door is one point off the line. -/
       7162  namespace RememberedOffered
       7163  
       7164  /-- ROW 10 · THE UNCONDITIONAL ROUTE FROM SHARED PREMISES AND THE RECORD IS BLOCKED. The value is no law of
       7165      reflection-closed configurations; nothing every closed configuration shares forces it, the root included; no
       7166      reading of the record decides it; and, by a law of logic true of every proposition, every premise that does force
       7167      it is either the value itself or strictly stronger than the value. -/
       7168  theorem the_unconditional_route_is_blocked {R : Prop} (G : SelfGrounding R) :
       7169      (¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) ∧
       7170      (∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → D S) → ¬ ∀ S, Closed S → D S → Value S) ∧
       7171      (¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → R → Value S) ∧
       7172      (∀ g : Config → Prop, (∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) →
       7173        ¬ ∀ S, Closed S → (g S ↔ Value S)) ∧
       7174      (∀ P : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → P S → Value S) →
       7175        (∀ S, Closed S → (P S ↔ Value S)) ∨ ∃ S, Closed S ∧ Value S ∧ ¬ P S) := by
       7176    have pc := pair_world_closed offPoint
       7177    have pv := pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off
       7178    have rc : Closed (registered offPoint) := fun s hs => by
       7179      rw [hs]; show fold (reg offPoint) = reg offPoint; rfl
       7180    refine ⟨fun h => pv (h _ pc), no_closed_principle_decides, the_floor_alone_decides_no_value G, ?_, ?_⟩
       7181    · intro g hg h
       7182      exact pv ((h _ pc).mp ((hg _ _ (one_record offPoint)).mp ((h _ rc).mpr (registered_has_value offPoint))))
       7183    · intro P f
       7184      rcases premise_trichotomy P with ⟨S, hS, p, nv⟩ | ⟨_, e⟩ | ⟨_, s⟩
       7185      · exact absurd (f S hS p) nv
       7186      · exact Or.inl e
       7187      · exact Or.inr s
       7188  
       7189  /-- ROW 11 · ACCEPTING THE HYPOTHESIS FORCES ACCEPTANCE OF THE ATOMIC PROOF. At every reflection-closed zero set:
       7190      every proof of the value, from any premise, an unconditional one included, is a supply of the act's field, by the
       7191      definition of the act's type, which carries the value itself as its field; the atomic proof this paper provides is
       7192      that form made explicit. Any two proofs are one and the supply is unique; the only other door is one point off the
       7193      line; there is no third value; and the structure, the reduction and the forced form, holds with no premise. -/
       7194  theorem accepting_rh_forces_the_atomic_proof (S : Config) (hS : Closed S) :
       7195      (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → Value S) → Q → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ∧
       7196      (Value S → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ∧
       7197      (∀ h₁ h₂ : Value S, h₁ = h₂) ∧
       7198      (∀ Z₁ Z₂ : ActualZeros, Z₁.zeros = S → Z₂.zeros = S → Z₁ = Z₂) ∧
       7199      (¬ Value S ↔ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) ∧
       7200      (Value S ∨ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) ∧ ¬ (Value S ∧ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) ∧
       7201      ((ZeroReports S ↔ Value S) ∧ (PrimeBound S ↔ Value S) ∧ (LeastErasure S ↔ Value S) ∧
       7202        (RootReadTwice S ↔ Value S)) ∧
       7203      (∀ P : Config → Prop, (∀ S', P S' → Value S') → (∀ S', Value S' → P S') → ∀ S', P S' ↔ Value S') := by
       7204    have n := the_atomic_necessity S hS
       7205    have b := both_values_atomic S hS
       7206    refine ⟨n.1, fun v => n.2.2.2.2.1.mpr v, n.2.1, n.2.2.1, b.2.1, two_doors S, b.2.2, ?_, ?_⟩
       7207    · exact (the_atomic_proof raSelfGrounding S hS).1
       7208    · exact (the_atomic_proof raSelfGrounding S hS).2.2.1
       7209  
       7210  end RememberedOffered
       7211  
       7212  end PartIII
       7213  
       7214  /-! # PART IV · the arrow and the zero side locus -/
       7215  section PartIV
       7216  /-
       7217    ARROW HINGE · the non-trivial-zero locus read directly off the arrow.
       7218    Core Lean 4.19.0, no import, no axiom declared, no sorry.
       7219    The arrow of the completed zeta runs between its only two poles, s = 0 and s = 1. Chart: x = 4·Re s, height t,
       7220    so the poles sit at x = 0 and x = 4 and the open strip is 0 < x < 4. Grain is free among the grains that put the
       7221    midpoint on the chart, the even ones; every such grain gives the same hinge, Re s = 1/2, and an odd grain holds no
       7222    chart point at the hinge (`hinge_iff_even`). Every chart of this seed has an even grain.
       7223    I   the arrow alone: reversal swaps its poles, undoes itself, and fixes at most one point, the hinge, and exactly
       7224        one when the poles have an even sum in the chart.
       7225    II  the free bit: flipping the arrow's orientation leaves the reversal and the hinge unchanged.
       7226    III the plane: the fold keeps height and moves offset; its fixed set is the line Re s = 1/2.
       7227    IV  the lean: off the line a point carries the arrow's sign and the fold flips it; the registration merges it.
       7228    V   the bar: a coherent off-line world sits inside the strip; no premise true of every closed world forces the value.
       7229    VI  the act: a supplied least-erasure world carries the value.
       7230    VII the zero side's own locus: the centre of every nonempty finite reflection-closed family is the line.
       7231    VIII the line on every extension: the arrow fixes one value of the real part; on every map of the plane that acts on
       7232        the real part by the reversal, the points whose real part it fixes are the line, and the centre balances on it;
       7233        a finite family closed under the fold, listed in any order, has its centre on the line.
       7234        The height-keeping extension is the fold, s ↦ 1 − s̄, which needs the conjugate symmetry [cited]; the functional
       7235        equation alone, s ↦ 1 − s, fixes one point and reads the same line.
       7236  -/
       7237  set_option autoImplicit false
       7238  namespace Hinge
       7239  
       7240  /-! ## I · the arrow alone -/
       7241  structure Arrow where
       7242    tail : Int
       7243    head : Int
       7244  
       7245  def rev (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : Int := A.tail + A.head - x
       7246  def flip (A : Arrow) : Arrow := ⟨A.head, A.tail⟩
       7247  def off (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : Int := 2 * x - (A.tail + A.head)
       7248  
       7249  theorem rev_swaps (A : Arrow) : rev A A.tail = A.head ∧ rev A A.head = A.tail := by
       7250    unfold rev; constructor <;> omega
       7251  theorem rev_involutive (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : rev A (rev A x) = x := by unfold rev; omega
       7252  /-- THE HINGE: a point is fixed by the arrow's reversal exactly when its offset from the midpoint is zero. -/
       7253  theorem hinge (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : rev A x = x ↔ off A x = 0 := by unfold rev off; omega
       7254  theorem hinge_unique (A : Arrow) (x y : Int) (hx : rev A x = x) (hy : rev A y = y) : x = y := by
       7255    unfold rev at hx hy; omega
       7256  /-- THE HINGE EXISTS on every arrow whose poles have an even sum in the chart: then the reversal fixes exactly the
       7257      midpoint. With `hinge_unique`, exactly one point. -/
       7258  theorem hinge_exists (A : Arrow) (h : (A.tail + A.head) % 2 = 0) : ∃ x, rev A x = x :=
       7259    ⟨(A.tail + A.head) / 2, by unfold rev; omega⟩
       7260  /-- THE HINGE ON THE CHART: the reversal has a fixed point on the integer chart exactly when the poles have an even
       7261      sum; at an odd grain the midpoint falls between two chart points and the chart holds no hinge. -/
       7262  theorem hinge_iff_even (A : Arrow) : (∃ x, rev A x = x) ↔ (A.tail + A.head) % 2 = 0 := by
       7263    constructor
       7264    · intro ⟨x, hx⟩
       7265      unfold rev at hx
       7266      omega
       7267    · exact hinge_exists A
       7268  
       7269  /-! ## II · the free bit -/
       7270  /-- SIGN-BLIND: the reversal and the offset magnitude ignore which way the arrow points. -/
       7271  theorem hinge_sign_blind (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : rev (flip A) x = rev A x ∧ off (flip A) x = off A x := by
       7272    show A.head + A.tail - x = A.tail + A.head - x ∧ 2 * x - (A.head + A.tail) = 2 * x - (A.tail + A.head)
       7273    constructor <;> omega
       7274  /-- The reversal flips every offset. -/
       7275  theorem rev_flips_offset (A : Arrow) (x : Int) : off A (rev A x) = - off A x := by unfold off rev; omega
       7276  
       7277  /-- Zeta's arrow: s = 0 to s = 1, at x = 4·Re s. -/
       7278  def zeta : Arrow := ⟨0, 4⟩
       7279  theorem zeta_hinge (x : Int) : rev zeta x = x ↔ x = 2 := by
       7280    show 0 + 4 - x = x ↔ x = 2; omega
       7281  /-- THE REVERSAL IS FORCED: the only distance-keeping map of the axis that swaps the poles is the arrow's reversal.
       7282      Distance-keeping is stated sign-blind, every difference kept up to its sign, so the Number alone fixes the map. -/
       7283  theorem the_only_rigid_reversal (f : Int → Int)
       7284      (iso : ∀ x y, f x - f y = x - y ∨ f x - f y = y - x) (h0 : f 0 = 4) (h4 : f 4 = 0) :
       7285      ∀ x, f x = rev zeta x := by
       7286    intro x
       7287    have a := iso x 0
       7288    have b := iso x 4
       7289    rw [h0] at a
       7290    rw [h4] at b
       7291    show f x = 0 + 4 - x
       7292    omega
       7293  
       7294  /-! ## III · the plane -/
       7295  abbrev Pt := Int × Int
       7296  def fold (p : Pt) : Pt := (rev zeta p.1, p.2)
       7297  def onLine (p : Pt) : Prop := p.1 = 2
       7298  def reg (p : Pt) : Pt := (2, p.2)
       7299  def inStrip (p : Pt) : Prop := 0 < p.1 ∧ p.1 < 4
       7300  
       7301  theorem fold_keeps_height (p : Pt) : (fold p).2 = p.2 := rfl
       7302  /-- THE LOCUS: the fold's fixed set is the line x = 2, which is Re s = 1/2. -/
       7303  theorem locus (p : Pt) : fold p = p ↔ onLine p := by
       7304    obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
       7305    constructor
       7306    · intro e
       7307      have h1 : 0 + 4 - x = x := congrArg Prod.fst e
       7308      show x = 2; omega
       7309    · intro e
       7310      have h1 : x = 2 := e
       7311      subst h1; rfl
       7312  
       7313  /-! ## IV · the lean -/
       7314  /-- OFF THE LINE A POINT LEANS: its offset is nonzero and the fold flips its sign. -/
       7315  theorem off_line_leans (p : Pt) (h : ¬ onLine p) : off zeta p.1 ≠ 0 ∧ off zeta (fold p).1 = - off zeta p.1 := by
       7316    constructor
       7317    · intro e
       7318      have e1 : 2 * p.1 - (0 + 4) = 0 := e
       7319      exact h (show p.1 = 2 by omega)
       7320    · exact rev_flips_offset zeta p.1
       7321  theorem reg_keeps_on_line (p : Pt) (h : onLine p) : reg p = p := by
       7322    obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
       7323    have h1 : x = 2 := h
       7324    subst h1; rfl
       7325  /-- OFF THE LINE THE REGISTRATION MERGES: two distinct points, one record. -/
       7326  theorem reg_merges (p : Pt) (h : ¬ onLine p) : fold p ≠ p ∧ reg (fold p) = reg p :=
       7327    ⟨fun e => h ((locus p).mp e), rfl⟩
       7328  
       7329  /-! ## V · the bar -/
       7330  def Closed (Z : Pt → Prop) : Prop := ∀ p, Z p → Z (fold p)
       7331  def Value (Z : Pt → Prop) : Prop := ∀ p, Z p → onLine p
       7332  def LeastErasure (Z : Pt → Prop) : Prop := ∀ p, Z p → reg p = p
       7333  
       7334  theorem least_erasure_iff_value (Z : Pt → Prop) : LeastErasure Z ↔ Value Z := by
       7335    constructor
       7336    · intro h p hp
       7337      have e : (1 : Int) * 2 = p.1 := by
       7338        have e0 : (reg p).1 = p.1 := congrArg Prod.fst (h p hp)
       7339        have e2 : (2 : Int) = p.1 := e0
       7340        omega
       7341      show p.1 = 2; omega
       7342    · intro h p hp; exact reg_keeps_on_line p (h p hp)
       7343  
       7344  /-- The off-line pair at Re s = 1/4 and 3/4, height 0. -/
       7345  def pairW : Pt → Prop := fun p => p = (1, 0) ∨ p = (3, 0)
       7346  theorem pair_closed : Closed pairW := by
       7347    intro p hp
       7348    rcases hp with e | e
       7349    · subst e; exact Or.inr (by decide)
       7350    · subst e; exact Or.inl (by decide)
       7351  theorem pair_in_strip : ∀ p, pairW p → inStrip p := by
       7352    intro p hp
       7353    rcases hp with e | e
       7354    · subst e; exact ⟨by decide, by decide⟩
       7355    · subst e; exact ⟨by decide, by decide⟩
       7356  theorem pair_lacks_value : ¬ Value pairW := by
       7357    intro h
       7358    have h1 : (1 : Int) = 2 := h (1, 0) (Or.inl rfl)
       7359    exact absurd h1 (by decide)
       7360  /-- THE ARROW FORCES NO ZERO: no premise true of every closed world forces the value. -/
       7361  theorem keyless_forces_nothing (Q : (Pt → Prop) → Prop) (hQ : ∀ Z, Closed Z → Q Z) :
       7362      ¬ ∀ Z, Closed Z → Q Z → Value Z :=
       7363    fun hall => pair_lacks_value (hall pairW pair_closed (hQ pairW pair_closed))
       7364  
       7365  /-! ## VI · the act -/
       7366  structure ActualZeros where
       7367    zeros : Pt → Prop
       7368    closed : Closed zeros
       7369    supply : LeastErasure zeros
       7370  theorem value_from_the_act (Z : ActualZeros) : Value Z.zeros := (least_erasure_iff_value _).mp Z.supply
       7371  
       7372  /-! ## VII · the zero side's own locus -/
       7373  /-- The real parts of a configuration, summed. -/
       7374  def sumX : List Pt → Int
       7375    | [] => 0
       7376    | p :: L => p.1 + sumX L
       7377  /-- THE ZERO SIDE'S LOCUS IS THE LINE: list any members with their mirrors and the real parts balance on the line,
       7378      four per member pair in this chart, so the centre of every reflection-closed configuration sits at Re s = 1/2. -/
       7379  theorem centre_is_the_line (L : List Pt) : sumX (L.map fold) + sumX L = 4 * (L.length : Int) := by
       7380    induction L with
       7381    | nil => rfl
       7382    | cons p L ih =>
       7383      have hf : (fold p).1 = 0 + 4 - p.1 := rfl
       7384      simp only [List.map_cons, sumX, List.length_cons]
       7385      push_cast
       7386      omega
       7387  /-- THE SAME OBJECT, MEMBERS OFF IT: the pair at Re s = 1/4 and 3/4 is reflection-closed, its centre is the line,
       7388      it sits in the open strip, and neither member is on the line. -/
       7389  theorem centred_yet_off :
       7390      Closed pairW ∧ sumX [(1, 0), (3, 0)] = 2 * 2 ∧ (∀ p, pairW p → inStrip p ∧ ¬ onLine p) := by
       7391    refine ⟨pair_closed, by decide, ?_⟩
       7392    intro p hp
       7393    refine ⟨pair_in_strip p hp, ?_⟩
       7394    rcases hp with e | e
       7395    · subst e; intro h; have h1 : (1 : Int) = 2 := h; exact absurd h1 (by decide)
       7396    · subst e; intro h; have h1 : (3 : Int) = 2 := h; exact absurd h1 (by decide)
       7397  
       7398  /-! ## VIII · the line and the centre on every extension -/
       7399  /-- THE LINE OFF THE ARROW: on every map of the plane that acts on the real part by the arrow's reversal, the points
       7400      whose real part it fixes are exactly the line x = 2, Re s = 1/2. The arrow fixes one value of the real part; the
       7401      line is the set of points with that real part, whatever the map does to height. -/
       7402  theorem the_line_off_the_arrow (F : Pt → Pt) (hF : ∀ p, (F p).1 = rev zeta p.1) (p : Pt) :
       7403      (F p).1 = p.1 ↔ onLine p := by
       7404    rw [hF p]
       7405    exact zeta_hinge p.1
       7406  /-- THE FOLD IS THE HEIGHT-KEEPING EXTENSION: the one map of the plane that acts on the real part by the reversal and
       7407      keeps height is the fold. Keeping height is the conjugate symmetry composed with the functional equation,
       7408      s ↦ 1 − s̄ [Riemann 1859, cited]. -/
       7409  theorem fold_is_the_height_keeping_extension (F : Pt → Pt) (hF : ∀ p, (F p).1 = rev zeta p.1)
       7410      (hh : ∀ p, (F p).2 = p.2) (p : Pt) : F p = fold p :=
       7411    Prod.ext (hF p) (hh p)
       7412  /-- The functional equation alone, s ↦ 1 − s, on the chart: the reversal on the real part, the height reversed. -/
       7413  def pointRefl (p : Pt) : Pt := (rev zeta p.1, -p.2)
       7414  /-- THE FUNCTIONAL EQUATION ALONE FIXES ONE POINT AND READS THE SAME LINE: s ↦ 1 − s fixes only s = 1/2, and the
       7415      points whose real part it fixes are the line. -/
       7416  theorem the_point_reflection_reads_the_same_line :
       7417      (∀ p : Pt, pointRefl p = p ↔ p = (2, 0)) ∧ (∀ p : Pt, (pointRefl p).1 = p.1 ↔ onLine p) := by
       7418    refine ⟨fun p => ?_, the_line_off_the_arrow pointRefl (fun _ => rfl)⟩
       7419    obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
       7420    constructor
       7421    · intro e
       7422      have h1 : 0 + 4 - x = x := congrArg Prod.fst e
       7423      have h2 : -t = t := congrArg Prod.snd e
       7424      have hx : x = 2 := by omega
       7425      have ht : t = 0 := by omega
       7426      subst hx
       7427      subst ht
       7428      rfl
       7429    · intro e
       7430      have hx : x = 2 := congrArg Prod.fst e
       7431      have ht : t = 0 := congrArg Prod.snd e
       7432      subst hx
       7433      subst ht
       7434      decide
       7435  /-- THE CENTRE ON EVERY EXTENSION: under every map that acts on the real part by the reversal, the real parts of any
       7436      finite family and of its image balance on the line; the centre does not depend on what the map does to height. -/
       7437  theorem centre_on_every_extension (F : Pt → Pt) (hF : ∀ p, (F p).1 = rev zeta p.1) (L : List Pt) :
       7438      sumX (L.map F) + sumX L = 4 * (L.length : Int) := by
       7439    induction L with
       7440    | nil => rfl
       7441    | cons p L ih =>
       7442      have hf : (F p).1 = 0 + 4 - p.1 := hF p
       7443      simp only [List.map_cons, sumX, List.length_cons]
       7444      push_cast
       7445      omega
       7446  
       7447  /-- The sum of real parts does not depend on the order in which a family is listed. -/
       7448  theorem sumX_perm {L M : List Pt} (h : L.Perm M) : sumX L = sumX M := by
       7449    induction h with
       7450    | nil => rfl
       7451    | cons x _ ih => simp only [sumX]; omega
       7452    | swap x y l => simp only [sumX]; omega
       7453    | trans _ _ ih1 ih2 => omega
       7454  /-- THE CENTRE OF A CLOSED FAMILY: a finite family whose mirror image is the family itself, listed in any order, has
       7455      its real parts summing to twice its size, so a nonempty one has its centre at x = 2, Re s = 1/2. -/
       7456  theorem centre_of_a_closed_family (L : List Pt) (h : (L.map fold).Perm L) : sumX L = 2 * (L.length : Int) := by
       7457    have e := centre_is_the_line L
       7458    have p := sumX_perm h
       7459    omega
       7460  
       7461  /-! ## the hinge, whole -/
       7462  theorem arrow_gives_line_not_value :
       7463      (∀ A : Arrow, rev A A.tail = A.head ∧ rev A A.head = A.tail) ∧
       7464      (∀ (A : Arrow) (x : Int), rev A (rev A x) = x) ∧
       7465      (∀ (A : Arrow) (x y : Int), rev A x = x → rev A y = y → x = y) ∧
       7466      (∀ (A : Arrow) (x : Int), rev (flip A) x = rev A x ∧ off (flip A) x = off A x) ∧
       7467      (∀ x : Int, rev zeta x = x ↔ x = 2) ∧
       7468      (∀ p : Pt, fold p = p ↔ onLine p) ∧
       7469      (∀ p : Pt, ¬ onLine p → off zeta p.1 ≠ 0 ∧ off zeta (fold p).1 = - off zeta p.1) ∧
       7470      (∀ p : Pt, ¬ onLine p → fold p ≠ p ∧ reg (fold p) = reg p) ∧
       7471      (∀ Z : Pt → Prop, LeastErasure Z ↔ Value Z) ∧
       7472      (Closed pairW ∧ (∀ p, pairW p → inStrip p) ∧ ¬ Value pairW) ∧
       7473      (∀ Q : (Pt → Prop) → Prop, (∀ Z, Closed Z → Q Z) → ¬ ∀ Z, Closed Z → Q Z → Value Z) ∧
       7474      (∀ Z : ActualZeros, Value Z.zeros) :=
       7475    ⟨rev_swaps, rev_involutive, hinge_unique, hinge_sign_blind, zeta_hinge, locus, off_line_leans, reg_merges,
       7476     least_erasure_iff_value, ⟨pair_closed, pair_in_strip, pair_lacks_value⟩, keyless_forces_nothing,
       7477     value_from_the_act⟩
       7478  end Hinge
       7479  
       7480  
       7481  end PartIV
       7482  
       7483  /-! # PART IV-b · Force_Witness.lean, verbatim from the signed master v5.1.0, with the plug appended -/
       7484  section PartIVb
       7485  /-
       7486    Force_Witness.lean · PhysOS Proof PSP-FORCE-WITNESS-01 · the force-witness closure.
       7487    Core Lean 4.19.0. No import, no sorry, no admit, no native_decide, no axiom declared.
       7488  
       7489    Least erasure is the final ninth-gate bit. A run of the substrate is the atomic witness that the closure was
       7490    computed: a run whose flag is true proves that a run exists. The value at the actual zero set is the field of
       7491    the act: keyed, given, free.
       7492  
       7493    PART ONE is copied from Inescapable_Capstone.lean, every definition and every law unchanged, with the lemmas
       7494    they stand on: the chart, the configurations, the record, the act, the ninth gate, the deed.
       7495    PART TWO is new: the atomic step, the ninth gate packed, the deed of the substrate, the free bit, the closure
       7496    and its guard.
       7497  
       7498    THE FREE BIT. Every run leaves the value to the act. the_deed_forces_nothing is the seated law, and
       7499    the_run_does_not_force_the_value states it at every run. It is the fourth conjunct of the closure.
       7500  -/
       7501  
       7502  namespace ForceWitness
       7503  
       7504  /-! ## PART ONE · The seated carriers and laws, copied unchanged -/
       7505  
       7506  /-- A point is (d, t): d its offset from the line, t its height. The line is d = 0. -/
       7507  abbrev Point := Int × Int
       7508  
       7509  /-- The fold: s ↦ 1 − s̄ on the offset chart, (d, t) ↦ (−d, t). -/
       7510  def fold (p : Point) : Point := (-p.1, p.2)
       7511  
       7512  /-- The line: offset zero. -/
       7513  def onLine (p : Point) : Prop := p.1 = 0
       7514  
       7515  /-- The registration: it keeps the height and forgets the side. -/
       7516  def reg (p : Point) : Point := (0, p.2)
       7517  
       7518  /-- Integer negation is an involution, by the integer's constructors. -/
       7519  theorem neg_neg_free : ∀ d : Int, - -d = d := fun
       7520    | Int.ofNat 0 => rfl
       7521    | Int.ofNat (_ + 1) => rfl
       7522    | Int.negSucc _ => rfl
       7523  
       7524  /-- An integer equal to its own negation is zero, by the integer's constructors. -/
       7525  theorem neg_self_zero : ∀ d : Int, -d = d → d = 0 := fun
       7526    | Int.ofNat 0, _ => rfl
       7527    | Int.ofNat (_ + 1), h => Int.noConfusion h
       7528    | Int.negSucc _, h => Int.noConfusion h
       7529  
       7530  /-- The fold is an involution. -/
       7531  theorem fold_involutive (p : Point) : fold (fold p) = p := by
       7532    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       7533    show (- -d, t) = (d, t)
       7534    rw [neg_neg_free d]
       7535  
       7536  /-- THE CUT IS THE LINE: the fold fixes a point exactly when it is on the line. -/
       7537  theorem the_cut_is_the_line (p : Point) : fold p = p ↔ onLine p := by
       7538    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       7539    exact ⟨fun h => neg_self_zero d (congrArg Prod.fst h), fun h => by cases h; rfl⟩
       7540  
       7541  /-- The registration lands on the line. -/
       7542  theorem reg_lands (p : Point) : onLine (reg p) := rfl
       7543  
       7544  /-- The registration erases nothing at a point exactly when the point is on the line. -/
       7545  theorem reg_erases_nothing_iff (p : Point) : reg p = p ↔ onLine p := by
       7546    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       7547    exact ⟨fun h => (congrArg Prod.fst h).symm, fun h => by cases h; rfl⟩
       7548  
       7549  /-- A configuration: a set of points. Closed: the fold carries it to itself. -/
       7550  abbrev Config := Point → Prop
       7551  
       7552  def Closed (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → S (fold p)
       7553  
       7554  /-- The value: every point of the configuration is on the line. -/
       7555  def Value (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → onLine p
       7556  
       7557  /-- Least erasure: the registration leaves every point of the configuration unchanged. -/
       7558  def LeastErasure (S : Config) : Prop := ∀ p, S p → reg p = p
       7559  
       7560  /-- The record of a configuration: what the registration leaves. -/
       7561  def Rec (S : Config) (q : Point) : Prop := ∃ p, S p ∧ reg p = q
       7562  
       7563  def SameRecord (S S' : Config) : Prop := ∀ q, Rec S q ↔ Rec S' q
       7564  
       7565  /-- The registered world of a point and its pair world. -/
       7566  def registered (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = reg p
       7567  
       7568  def pairWorld (p : Point) : Config := fun s => s = p ∨ s = fold p
       7569  
       7570  theorem pair_world_closed (p : Point) : Closed (pairWorld p) := fun _ hs =>
       7571    match hs with
       7572    | Or.inl e => Or.inr (congrArg fold e)
       7573    | Or.inr e => Or.inl (e ▸ fold_involutive p)
       7574  
       7575  /-- The registered world and the pair world leave one record. -/
       7576  theorem one_record (p : Point) : SameRecord (registered p) (pairWorld p) := fun q =>
       7577    ⟨fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨p, Or.inl rfl, by rw [← hq, hs]; rfl⟩,
       7578     fun ⟨_, hs, hq⟩ => ⟨reg p, rfl, by
       7579        rw [← hq]
       7580        exact match hs with
       7581          | Or.inl e => by rw [e]; rfl
       7582          | Or.inr e => by rw [e]; rfl⟩⟩
       7583  
       7584  theorem registered_has_value (p : Point) : Value (registered p) := fun s hs => by
       7585    rw [hs]; exact reg_lands p
       7586  
       7587  theorem pair_world_lacks_value (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) : ¬ Value (pairWorld p) :=
       7588    fun hv => h (hv p (Or.inl rfl))
       7589  
       7590  /-- THE RECORD DECIDES NOTHING: for every point off the line, no reading that respects the record returns the
       7591      value on both its registered world and its pair world. -/
       7592  theorem record_decides_nothing (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) (g : Config → Prop)
       7593      (hg : ∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) :
       7594      ¬ ((g (registered p) ↔ Value (registered p)) ∧ (g (pairWorld p) ↔ Value (pairWorld p))) :=
       7595    fun ⟨h1, h2⟩ => pair_world_lacks_value p h
       7596      (h2.mp ((hg _ _ (one_record p)).mp (h1.mpr (registered_has_value p))))
       7597  
       7598  /-- THE ACT. The bit is supplied once, in the open, as a field of a type: a closed configuration with least
       7599      erasure at it. The field is the value supplied; the type makes the supply visible to every reader. -/
       7600  structure ActualZeros where
       7601    zeros : Config
       7602    closed : Closed zeros
       7603    supply : LeastErasure zeros
       7604  
       7605  /-- FROM THE ACT, THE VALUE. -/
       7606  theorem value_from_the_act (Z : ActualZeros) : Value Z.zeros :=
       7607    fun p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mp (Z.supply p hp)
       7608  
       7609  def e (n i : Nat) : List Int := (List.range n).map (fun j => if j == i then 1 else 0)
       7610  
       7611  def neg3 (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : Bool × Bool × Bool := (!s.1, !s.2.1, !s.2.2)
       7612  
       7613  def par3 (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : Nat :=
       7614    (if s.1 then 1 else 0) + (if s.2.1 then 1 else 0) + (if s.2.2 then 1 else 0)
       7615  
       7616  /-- The orientation of a sign pattern, the determinant of its diagonal: −1 to the number of flips. -/
       7617  def orient (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : Int := if par3 s % 2 == 0 then 1 else -1
       7618  
       7619  /-- The ordered factor pairs of n, by first factor; the swap sends a to n / a. -/
       7620  def pairs (n : Nat) : List Nat := (List.range (n + 1)).filter (fun a => 0 < a && n % a == 0)
       7621  
       7622  /-- The price of exported freedom in native units: temperature is energy per bit, so b bits cost b·T. -/
       7623  def price (T bits : Nat) : Nat := bits * T
       7624  
       7625  /-- A finite configuration: the heights of its zeros on the line, and its off-line pairs, each an offset that is not
       7626      zero and a height. -/
       7627  structure FinCfg where
       7628    line : List Int
       7629    pairs : List (Int × Int)
       7630    offset_ne : ∀ q ∈ pairs, q.1 ≠ 0
       7631  
       7632  /-- The erased bits of a finite configuration: one per off-line pair, two points registered to one. -/
       7633  def erased (F : FinCfg) : Nat := F.pairs.length
       7634  
       7635  /-- The executed frame: a formal content and the bit of whether it ran. Reading the content is formal. -/
       7636  abbrev Exec (Q : Type) := Bool × Q
       7637  
       7638  def ran {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) : Bool := s.1
       7639  
       7640  /-- The nine: the eight sign patterns and one more. -/
       7641  abbrev Gate := Option (Bool × Bool × Bool)
       7642  
       7643  /-- The fold on the nine: total negation on the eight; the ninth is its own partner. -/
       7644  def gfold : Gate → Gate
       7645    | none => none
       7646    | some s => some (neg3 s)
       7647  
       7648  /-- THE SEAT IS THE NINTH: the fold of the nine fixes a gate exactly when the gate is the ninth. -/
       7649  theorem seat_is_the_ninth (g : Gate) : gfold g = g ↔ g = none := by
       7650    cases g with
       7651    | none => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩
       7652    | some s =>
       7653      obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s
       7654      constructor
       7655      · intro h; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> cases h
       7656      · intro h; cases h
       7657  
       7658  /-- The orientation of a pattern is never zero. -/
       7659  theorem orient_ne_zero (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : orient s ≠ 0 := by
       7660    obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> decide
       7661  
       7662  /-- Total negation flips the orientation. -/
       7663  theorem orient_flips (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : orient (neg3 s) = -orient s := by
       7664    obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl
       7665  
       7666  /-- The carrier of the nine onto the chart: a pattern lands on the wall or the edge by its orientation, the ninth on
       7667      the line. -/
       7668  def toChart (t : Int) : Gate → Point
       7669    | none => (0, t)
       7670    | some s => (orient s, t)
       7671  
       7672  /-- The carrier is equivariant: the fold of the nine is carried onto the fold of the chart. -/
       7673  theorem gate_carrier_equivariant (t : Int) (g : Gate) : toChart t (gfold g) = fold (toChart t g) := by
       7674    cases g with
       7675    | none => rfl
       7676    | some s => obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> rfl
       7677  
       7678  /-- And under every carrier that separates partners, only the ninth does. -/
       7679  theorem faithful_carrier_lands_only_the_ninth (c : Gate → Point) (eqv : ∀ g, c (gfold g) = fold (c g))
       7680      (sep : ∀ g, c (gfold g) = c g → gfold g = g) (g : Gate) : onLine (c g) ↔ g = none := by
       7681    constructor
       7682    · intro h
       7683      exact (seat_is_the_ninth g).mp (sep g ((eqv g).trans ((the_cut_is_the_line (c g)).mpr h)))
       7684    · intro h
       7685      subst h
       7686      have e : fold (c none) = c none := (eqv none).symm
       7687      exact (the_cut_is_the_line (c none)).mp e
       7688  
       7689  /-- The orientation carrier separates partners. -/
       7690  theorem orientation_carrier_separates (t : Int) (g : Gate) (h : toChart t (gfold g) = toChart t g) :
       7691      gfold g = g := by
       7692    cases g with
       7693    | none => rfl
       7694    | some s =>
       7695      exact absurd (neg_self_zero (orient s) ((orient_flips s).symm.trans (congrArg Prod.fst h))) (orient_ne_zero s)
       7696  
       7697  /-- A gate owes a bit when some target is odd at it: no even reading returns that target, and one supplied odd
       7698      witness fixes it by one calibration bit. -/
       7699  def OwesBit (g : Gate) : Prop := ∃ d : Gate → Bool, d (gfold g) = !d g
       7700  
       7701  /-- At the seat no bit is owed: nothing is odd at a fixed point. -/
       7702  theorem seat_owes_no_bit : ¬ OwesBit none := by
       7703    intro ⟨d, h⟩
       7704    have h' : d none = !d none := h
       7705    cases hd : d none <;> rw [hd] at h' <;> cases h'
       7706  
       7707  /-- Off the seat a bit is owed, at every one of the eight. -/
       7708  theorem off_seat_owes_a_bit (s : Bool × Bool × Bool) : OwesBit (some s) := by
       7709    refine ⟨fun g => decide (g = some s), ?_⟩
       7710    obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s
       7711    cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> decide
       7712  
       7713  /-- The registered orbit of a gate, as a finite configuration: the ninth is one point on the line; each of the eight
       7714      is one off-line pair. -/
       7715  def gateCfg (t : Int) : Gate → FinCfg
       7716    | none => ⟨[t], [], fun _ h => nomatch h⟩
       7717    | some s => ⟨[], [(orient s, t)], fun q h => by
       7718        cases h with
       7719        | head => exact orient_ne_zero s
       7720        | tail _ h' => nomatch h'⟩
       7721  
       7722  /-- The heat of registering a gate is zero exactly at the ninth. -/
       7723  theorem gate_heat_zero_iff_ninth (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (t : Int) (g : Gate) :
       7724      price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ↔ g = none := by
       7725    cases g with
       7726    | none => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => Nat.zero_mul T⟩
       7727    | some s =>
       7728      constructor
       7729      · intro h
       7730        have h1 : 1 * T = 0 := h
       7731        rw [Nat.one_mul] at h1
       7732        exact absurd h1 (Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp hT)
       7733      · intro h; cases h
       7734  
       7735  /-- THE NINTH GATE IS LEAST ERASURE. At a gate, five readings are one: it is the fold's fixed point; it lands on
       7736      the line; registration erases nothing there (forget); its registration is free (pay); no bit is owed there
       7737      (supply). Each holds exactly at the ninth. -/
       7738  theorem ninth_gate_is_least_erasure (t : Int) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (g : Gate) :
       7739      (gfold g = g ↔ g = none) ∧
       7740      (onLine (toChart t g) ↔ g = none) ∧
       7741      (reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ↔ g = none) ∧
       7742      (price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ↔ g = none) ∧
       7743      (¬ OwesBit g ↔ g = none) := by
       7744    have hl : onLine (toChart t g) ↔ g = none :=
       7745      faithful_carrier_lands_only_the_ninth (toChart t) (gate_carrier_equivariant t) (orientation_carrier_separates t) g
       7746    refine ⟨seat_is_the_ninth g, hl, (reg_erases_nothing_iff (toChart t g)).trans hl,
       7747            gate_heat_zero_iff_ninth T hT t g, ?_⟩
       7748    cases g with
       7749    | none => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => seat_owes_no_bit⟩
       7750    | some s => exact ⟨fun h => absurd (off_seat_owes_a_bit s) h, fun h => by cases h⟩
       7751  
       7752  /-- A RUN IS ITS OWN ATOMIC WITNESS, of the deed: a state that ran proves that a run exists. -/
       7753  theorem the_run_witnesses_a_run {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) (h : ran s = true) : ∃ r : Exec Q, ran r = true := by
       7754    exact ⟨s, h⟩
       7755  
       7756  /-- AND OF NOTHING ELSE: a fact that holds whatever the configuration, the deed included, forces no value. -/
       7757  theorem the_deed_forces_nothing (D : Prop) (hD : D) : ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → D → Value S := by
       7758    intro hall
       7759    exact pair_world_lacks_value (1, 0) (fun e => by cases e) (hall _ (pair_world_closed (1, 0)) hD)
       7760  
       7761  
       7762  /-! ## PART TWO · The force-witness closure -/
       7763  
       7764  /-- THE ATOMIC STEP: a witness with its check proves the existential it witnesses. -/
       7765  theorem witness_proves_exists {α : Type} (P : α → Prop) (w : α) (h : P w) : ∃ x, P x := ⟨w, h⟩
       7766  
       7767  /-- THE NINTH GATE, PACKED: a gate is the ninth exactly when all five readings hold of it. The five biconditionals
       7768      of ninth_gate_is_least_erasure, bound into one. -/
       7769  theorem ninth_gate_pack (t : Int) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (g : Gate) :
       7770      g = none ↔
       7771        (gfold g = g ∧ onLine (toChart t g) ∧ reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ∧
       7772         price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ∧ ¬ OwesBit g) := by
       7773    have h := ninth_gate_is_least_erasure t T hT g
       7774    constructor
       7775    · intro e
       7776      exact ⟨h.1.mpr e, h.2.1.mpr e, h.2.2.1.mpr e, h.2.2.2.1.mpr e, h.2.2.2.2.mpr e⟩
       7777    · intro hh
       7778      exact h.1.mp hh.1
       7779  
       7780  /-- The deed of the substrate: a run, and the fact that it ran. -/
       7781  structure SubstrateDeed (Q : Type) where
       7782    run : Exec Q
       7783    didRun : ran run = true
       7784  
       7785  /-- THE FREE BIT. A run whose flag is true leaves the value free: by the run the value does not stand on every
       7786      closed configuration. It is the_deed_forces_nothing read at the flag of the deed. A computation is a deed, and
       7787      the value is the field of the act. -/
       7788  theorem the_run_does_not_force_the_value {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) (h : ran s = true) :
       7789      ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
       7790    fun hall => the_deed_forces_nothing (ran s = true) h (fun S hS _ => hall S hS)
       7791  
       7792  /-- THE FORCE-WITNESS CLOSURE. For a deed of the substrate, a term of the act, and any gate: the gate is the ninth
       7793      exactly when it is the fold's fixed point, on the line, erased nothing, free to register at a positive
       7794      temperature and owing no bit; the value holds on the field the act supplies; a run that ran exists; and the
       7795      run leaves the value free. The fourth conjunct is the free bit. It is the implementation of the force. -/
       7796  theorem force_witness_closure {Q : Type} (d : SubstrateDeed Q) (Z : ActualZeros)
       7797      (t : Int) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) (g : Gate) :
       7798      (g = none ↔
       7799        (gfold g = g ∧ onLine (toChart t g) ∧ reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ∧
       7800         price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ∧ ¬ OwesBit g)) ∧
       7801      Value Z.zeros ∧
       7802      (∃ r : Exec Q, ran r = true) ∧
       7803      ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
       7804    ⟨ninth_gate_pack t T hT g,
       7805     value_from_the_act Z,
       7806     the_run_witnesses_a_run d.run d.didRun,
       7807     the_run_does_not_force_the_value d.run d.didRun⟩
       7808  
       7809  /-- THE GUARD ON THE CLOSURE, the double defense restated: the value comes by the act; between the registered
       7810      world and the pair world of a point off the line, every reading that respects the record leaves the value
       7811      free; and the deed leaves it free. -/
       7812  theorem force_witness_guarded {Q : Type} (d : SubstrateDeed Q) (Z : ActualZeros) :
       7813      Value Z.zeros ∧
       7814      (∀ (p : Point), ¬ onLine p → ∀ (g : Config → Prop), (∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) →
       7815        ¬ ((g (registered p) ↔ Value (registered p)) ∧ (g (pairWorld p) ↔ Value (pairWorld p)))) ∧
       7816      ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
       7817    ⟨value_from_the_act Z,
       7818     fun p h g hg => record_decides_nothing p h g hg,
       7819     the_run_does_not_force_the_value d.run d.didRun⟩
       7820  
       7821  end ForceWitness
       7822

       7825  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ForceWitness.neg_neg_free

       7887  /-! ## THE PLUG · appended, nothing above changed. The run's true flag offered as the act's supply field. -/
       7888  namespace ForceWitness
       7889  /-- The plug, attempted: if a true flag supplied least erasure on every closed world, the run would force the value.
       7890      The compiler refuses it. -/
       7891  theorem the_plug_fails {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) (h : ran s = true) :
       7892      ¬ (ran s = true → ∀ S : Config, Closed S → LeastErasure S) :=
       7893    fun plug => the_run_does_not_force_the_value s h (fun S hS => value_from_the_act ⟨S, hS, plug h S hS⟩)
       7894  /-- What the plug does deliver: with the act's field beside the run, the value stands on that field, the run is
       7895      witnessed, and the run still leaves the value free. Run and field are two inputs, never one. -/
       7896  theorem the_plug_delivers {Q : Type} (d : SubstrateDeed Q) (Z : ActualZeros) :
       7897      Value Z.zeros ∧ (∃ r : Exec Q, ran r = true) ∧ ¬ (∀ S : Config, Closed S → Value S) :=
       7898    ⟨value_from_the_act Z, the_run_witnesses_a_run d.run d.didRun, the_run_does_not_force_the_value d.run d.didRun⟩
       7899  end ForceWitness
