       9126  /-! # PART VII · THE HARDENING · the identification, the bridge, the bound and the capstone, every input printed
       9127  
       9128    OPTIONAL CORROBORATION, NOT REQUIRED FOR THE FORMAL LOOP. The five-way fixed-point
       9129    loop (Part X § X-d) stands on Parts I and X; the master closure (Part XI) stands on
       9130    Parts I to III, the apparatus cargo of Part VIII-b, and Parts IX and X. Part VII's
       9131    hardening and Part VIII's physico-formal carrier are corroborating developments; the
       9132    formal loop does not depend on them.
       9133  
       9134    Added 11 October 2026 for edition 2.0.3 of The Atomic Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, on the Final Scribal
       9135    Recommendation of the audit of 10 October 2026. Nothing above this line changed: Parts I to VI are byte-identical
       9136    to RH_Both_Sides_Seed.lean of 8 October 2026 (sha256 cb719eab915a9973…). Core Lean 4.19.0, no import, no axiom
       9137    declared, no sorry, no admit, no native_decide.
       9138  
       9139    What this part does, and in this order:
       9140    VII-a  carries the kernel of the companion paper, Least Erasure from Degrees of Freedom and Heat, repaired to
       9141           compile in core Lean (the shipped v2.0.1 kernel used the Mathlib tactic by_contra and left one conjunction
       9142           unsolved, so its master seal depended on sorryAx under Lean 4.19.0), with the quantitative companion
       9143           density_bound_from_residual_bound added and the master seal extended to seven claims;
       9144    VII-b  states the identification exactly: on the chart, least erasure of a configuration IS its value, for every
       9145           configuration, by theorem; so the one thing to be granted is the reading, that the classical hypothesis is
       9146           the value of the configuration at which the zeros of ζ are read (Section 11 of the paper). The field
       9147           `supply` of `ActualZeros` is shown to be the premise packaged, by its type;
       9148    VII-c  writes the bridge as six named arrows composed by theorem, the rate and the heat feeding the signal, and
       9149           proves the uniform threshold δ = n₀·r₀·q₀ independent of which carrier and which zero;
       9150    VII-d  keeps the heat theorem at its exact strength: the exact-null case and the finite-sensitivity case apart;
       9151    VII-e  THE CAPSTONE, classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound, with its five inputs printed, and its
       9152           exploded form with the nine inputs of the Recommendation; the exact-null route beside it with ITS premise
       9153           printed; and no_third_position: given the identification, the bound and the gap, the denial of the
       9154           hypothesis and the bridge cannot both stand;
       9155    VII-f  what the capstone does not do, by theorem: the reading and the bridge are keyed, each fails on a closed
       9156           configuration of the interface, so neither is a theorem of the seed and each is a premise, named;
       9157    VII-g  the hardened closure, binding the two-sided closure and the capstones by their exact types, and the cones.
       9158  
       9159    The reading of the empty cone: `#print axioms` names the axioms a proof depends on. It says nothing about the
       9160    hypotheses in the signature. Every hypothesis of the capstone is an input the reader grants or refuses by name.
       9161  
       9162    NOTE: in the flipped formal register, the observational bridge parameters of this part
       9163    (the six arrows, the bound, the capstone inputs) are SUPERSEDED in the core arch by the formalized
       9164    compute cargo — `ApparatusCargo` (seed Part VIII-b), `BoundChain` (Part IX), `BoundChainMathlib` (Part X).
       9165    They remain in this file, untouched, as fenced conditional theorems (optional retrospective corroboration),
       9166    matching the status of `ApparatusCargo.stage2_optional_corroboration`. -/
       9167  section PartVII
       9168  set_option autoImplicit false
       9169  
       9170  /-! ## VII-a · the least-erasure kernel of the companion paper, repaired, with the quantitative companion -/
       9171  namespace LeastErasureDoF
       9172  
       9173  def ln2_scaled : Nat := 693147
       9174  def scale : Nat := 1000000
       9175  def cmb_mK : Nat := 2725
       9176  
       9177  /-- A system relative to a record: macro states distinguished, binary labels free, micro states in total. -/
       9178  structure System where
       9179    distinct : Nat
       9180    free : Nat
       9181    total : Nat
       9182    inv : total = distinct * Nat.pow 2 free
       9183  
       9184  /-- A recoding that halves the record and frees one label, total preserved. -/
       9185  structure DiscardProcess where
       9186    before : System
       9187    after : System
       9188    h_distinct : before.distinct = 2 * after.distinct
       9189    h_free : after.free = before.free + 1
       9190    h_total : before.total = after.total
       9191    h_gt : before.distinct > after.distinct
       9192  
       9193  /-- An erasure: the record kept, one free label lost, the total halved. -/
       9194  structure EraseProcess where
       9195    before : System
       9196    after : System
       9197    h_distinct : before.distinct = after.distinct
       9198    h_free : before.free = after.free + 1
       9199    h_total : before.total = 2 * after.total
       9200    h_gt : before.total > after.total
       9201  
       9202  /-- A discard halves the record and frees one label. Repaired: the shipped proof left this conjunction open. -/
       9203  theorem discard_is_free (p : DiscardProcess) :
       9204      p.after.distinct * 2 = p.before.distinct ∧
       9205      p.after.free = p.before.free + 1 :=
       9206    ⟨(Nat.mul_comm _ _).trans p.h_distinct.symm, p.h_free⟩
       9207  
       9208  def sysEntropy (s : System) : Nat := s.free * ln2_scaled
       9209  
       9210  theorem sysEntropy_decrease (p : EraseProcess) :
       9211      sysEntropy p.after + ln2_scaled = sysEntropy p.before := by
       9212    unfold sysEntropy
       9213    rw [p.h_free, Nat.succ_mul]
       9214  
       9215  /-- The lower bound is witnessed by the choice heat = T · ln2_scaled. The process is not consulted: the kernel
       9216      records that a number meeting the bound exists, nothing more. The physical necessity, joint conservation of
       9217      probability with the second law, is carried in the prose of the companion paper at its own grade. -/
       9218  theorem heat_from_joint_conservation (_p : EraseProcess) (T : Nat) :
       9219      ∃ heat : Nat, heat ≥ T * ln2_scaled :=
       9220    ⟨T * ln2_scaled, Nat.le_refl _⟩
       9221  
       9222  theorem heat_positive (_p : EraseProcess) (T : Nat) (hT : T > 0) :
       9223      ∃ heat : Nat, heat > 0 ∧ heat ≥ T * ln2_scaled :=
       9224    ⟨T * ln2_scaled, Nat.mul_pos hT (by decide), Nat.le_refl _⟩
       9225  
       9226  theorem landauer_special_case (p : EraseProcess) (_h : p.before.free = 1) :
       9227      ∃ heat : Nat, heat ≥ cmb_mK * ln2_scaled :=
       9228    heat_from_joint_conservation p cmb_mK
       9229  
       9230  /-- The residual observable of the counting model: population × rate × heat per event. -/
       9231  def residual (density rate heat : Nat) : Nat := density * rate * heat
       9232  
       9233  theorem residual_pos {density rate heat : Nat}
       9234      (hd : density > 0) (hr : rate > 0) (hh : heat > 0) :
       9235      residual density rate heat > 0 := by
       9236    unfold residual
       9237    have h1 : density * rate > 0 := Nat.mul_pos hd hr
       9238    exact Nat.mul_pos h1 hh
       9239  
       9240  /-- THE EXACT-NULL CASE. Residual exactly zero, rate and heat positive: the population is zero. Repaired: the
       9241      shipped proof used by_contra, a Mathlib tactic, and so did not compile in core Lean. -/
       9242  theorem null_forces_zero {density rate heat : Nat}
       9243      (hr : rate > 0) (hh : heat > 0) (h0 : residual density rate heat = 0) :
       9244      density = 0 := by
       9245    cases density with
       9246    | zero => rfl
       9247    | succ d =>
       9248      have hpos := residual_pos (Nat.succ_pos d) hr hh
       9249      rw [h0] at hpos
       9250      exact absurd hpos (Nat.lt_irrefl 0)
       9251  
       9252  /-- THE FINITE-SENSITIVITY CASE, the quantitative companion. Residual at most ε, rate at least r₀, heat at
       9253      least q₀: the population times the two floors, ρ · r₀ · q₀, is at most ε. This is what a null result at finite sensitivity
       9254      supports. It is not density = 0, and the paper never rewrites it as density = 0. Stated multiplicatively so
       9255      that no integer division rounds anything: the bound is exact in the kernel's units. -/
       9256  theorem density_bound_from_residual_bound {density rate heat r0 q0 ε : Nat}
       9257      (hR : residual density rate heat ≤ ε) (hr : rate ≥ r0) (hq : heat ≥ q0) :
       9258      density * r0 * q0 ≤ ε :=
       9259    Nat.le_trans (Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul_left density hr) hq) hR
       9260  
       9261  /-- The same bound read as a quotient, density ≤ ε / (r₀ q₀), for positive floors. Integer division floors, so
       9262      this form is weaker than the multiplicative one; it is the form the Recommendation names. Its cone carries
       9263      propext through the core lemma on division, and is pinned below as such. -/
       9264  theorem density_le_div {density rate heat r0 q0 ε : Nat}
       9265      (hR : residual density rate heat ≤ ε) (hr : rate ≥ r0) (hq : heat ≥ q0)
       9266      (hr0 : r0 > 0) (hq0 : q0 > 0) :
       9267      density ≤ ε / (r0 * q0) :=
       9268    (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le (Nat.mul_pos hr0 hq0)).mpr
       9269      (Nat.mul_assoc density r0 q0 ▸ density_bound_from_residual_bound hR hr hq)
       9270  
       9271  def Discards (p : EraseProcess) (label : Nat) : Prop :=
       9272    label < p.before.distinct ∧ p.before.distinct > 0
       9273  
       9274  def NullForcesZeroOn (label : Nat) : Prop :=
       9275    ∃ p : EraseProcess, Discards p label ∧ residual 1 1 ln2_scaled > 0
       9276  
       9277  theorem boundary_holds :
       9278      ∀ (label : Nat), ¬ (∃ p : EraseProcess, Discards p label) →
       9279        ¬ NullForcesZeroOn label := by
       9280    intro label hNo hYes
       9281    unfold NullForcesZeroOn at hYes
       9282    obtain ⟨p, hp, _⟩ := hYes
       9283    exact hNo ⟨p, hp⟩
       9284  
       9285  /-- The Noether skeleton. Both predicates are True: the kernel keeps only the shape of the statement, a
       9286      symmetry yields a conserved current, and proves nothing about any dynamics. Stated so, not otherwise. -/
       9287  def ContinuousSymmetry (_ξ : Nat) : Prop := True
       9288  def Conserved (_curr : Nat) : Prop := True
       9289  
       9290  theorem noether_current :
       9291      ∀ (ξ : Nat), ContinuousSymmetry ξ →
       9292        ∃ curr : Nat, Conserved curr :=
       9293    fun _ _ => ⟨0, trivial⟩
       9294  
       9295  /-- THE MASTER SEAL, seven claims: the six of the companion paper and the quantitative companion. -/
       9296  theorem the_master_seal :
       9297      (∀ p : DiscardProcess, p.after.distinct * 2 = p.before.distinct ∧ p.after.free = p.before.free + 1) ∧
       9298      (∀ _p : EraseProcess, ∀ T : Nat, ∃ heat : Nat, heat ≥ T * ln2_scaled) ∧
       9299      (∀ p : EraseProcess, p.before.free = 1 → ∃ heat : Nat, heat ≥ cmb_mK * ln2_scaled) ∧
       9300      (∀ density rate heat : Nat, density > 0 → rate > 0 → heat > 0 → residual density rate heat > 0) ∧
       9301      (∀ label : Nat, ¬ (∃ p : EraseProcess, Discards p label) → ¬ NullForcesZeroOn label) ∧
       9302      (∀ ξ : Nat, ContinuousSymmetry ξ → ∃ curr : Nat, Conserved curr) ∧
       9303      (∀ density rate heat r0 q0 ε : Nat, residual density rate heat ≤ ε → rate ≥ r0 → heat ≥ q0 →
       9304        density * r0 * q0 ≤ ε) := by
       9305    refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
       9306    · exact fun p => discard_is_free p
       9307    · exact fun p T => heat_from_joint_conservation p T
       9308    · exact fun p h => landauer_special_case p h
       9309    · exact fun _ _ _ hd hr hh => residual_pos hd hr hh
       9310    · exact fun label => boundary_holds label
       9311    · exact fun ξ h => noether_current ξ h
       9312    · exact fun _ _ _ _ _ _ hR hr hq => density_bound_from_residual_bound hR hr hq
       9313  
       9314  end LeastErasureDoF
       9315  
       9316  namespace Hardening
       9317  open RememberedOffered
       9318  
       9319  /-! ## VII-b · the identification, stated exactly -/
       9320  
       9321  /-- On the chart, the registration fixes a point exactly when the point stands on the line. This is the whole of
       9322      `zeta_fixed_locus_correct` that the chart can carry: the line of the chart is d = 0, and Section 11 of the
       9323      paper reads Re s = 1/2 onto it by the reader's rule. -/
       9324  theorem zeta_fixed_locus_on_the_chart (p : Point) : reg p = p ↔ onLine p :=
       9325    reg_erases_nothing_iff p
       9326  
       9327  /-- Least erasure of a configuration is the value of that configuration, for every configuration, the one at
       9328      which the zeros of ζ are read included. No hypothesis. -/
       9329  theorem le_iff_value (S : Config) : LeastErasure S ↔ Value S :=
       9330    ⟨fun h p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mp (h p hp),
       9331     fun h p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mpr (h p hp)⟩
       9332  
       9333  /-- THE IDENTIFICATION, REDUCED TO THE READING. Whoever grants that the classical hypothesis is the value of the
       9334      configuration at which the zeros of ζ are read has, by theorem, granted that it is least erasure of that
       9335      configuration. The reading is the one input; nothing else is identified by name. -/
       9336  theorem classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config}
       9337      (h_read : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ) : ClassicalRH ↔ LeastErasure Zζ :=
       9338    h_read.trans (le_iff_value Zζ).symm
       9339  
       9340  /-- The field `supply` is the premise, by its type. Its presence in an act establishes nothing about which
       9341      configuration the act carries. -/
       9342  theorem supply_is_the_premise (A : ActualZeros) : LeastErasure A.zeros :=
       9343    A.supply
       9344  
       9345  /-- An act exists at a configuration exactly when the configuration is closed and least erasure holds there:
       9346      the act is the premise packaged, and the package adds nothing. -/
       9347  theorem the_act_is_the_premise_packaged (S : Config) :
       9348      (∃ A : ActualZeros, A.zeros = S) ↔ (Closed S ∧ LeastErasure S) :=
       9349    ⟨fun ⟨A, h⟩ => h ▸ ⟨A.closed, A.supply⟩,
       9350     fun ⟨hc, hle⟩ => ⟨⟨S, hc, hle⟩, rfl⟩⟩
       9351  
       9352  /-! ## VII-c · the bridge: six named arrows, composed by theorem -/
       9353  section Bridge
       9354  variable {Carrier : Type}
       9355  
       9356  /-- The floor one realized carrier puts under the residual observable: population × rate × heat per event. -/
       9357  theorem carrier_floor (density rate heat : Carrier → Nat) {n0 r0 q0 : Nat} (c : Carrier)
       9358      (hd : density c ≥ n0) (hr : rate c ≥ r0) (hq : heat c ≥ q0) :
       9359      LeastErasureDoF.residual (density c) (rate c) (heat c) ≥ n0 * r0 * q0 := by
       9360    unfold LeastErasureDoF.residual
       9361    exact Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul hd hr) hq
       9362  
       9363  /-- The threshold is positive exactly when the population floor, the rate floor and the heat floor are. -/
       9364  theorem gap_positive {n0 r0 q0 : Nat} (hn : n0 > 0) (hr : r0 > 0) (hq : q0 > 0) : n0 * r0 * q0 > 0 :=
       9365    Nat.mul_pos (Nat.mul_pos hn hr) hq
       9366  
       9367  /-- THE BRIDGE, COMPOSED. Six arrows, each a named hypothesis the reader grants or refuses:
       9368      h_carrier  a failure of least erasure at the read configuration realizes a carrier in the measured domain;
       9369      h_erase    a realized carrier irreversibly loses its which-branch label, kept in no other register;
       9370      h_pop      an erasing carrier is a population of at least n₀;
       9371      h_rate     an erasing carrier runs at a rate of at least r₀ during the observation;
       9372      h_heat     an erasing carrier deposits at least q₀ per event (Landauer, q₀ = k_B T ln 2 in the kernel's units);
       9373      h_couple   the residual observable covers the carrier's contribution: R ≥ population × rate × heat.
       9374      Conclusion: a failure of least erasure forces R ≥ n₀ r₀ q₀. The threshold does not depend on the carrier
       9375      and does not depend on which point stands off the line: it is uniform over the class the hypotheses name.
       9376      Positive rate and positive heat alone do not reach the conclusion; the population floor and the coupling are
       9377      needed and are named. -/
       9378  theorem off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal
       9379      {Zζ : Config} {R n0 r0 q0 : Nat}
       9380      (Realizes Erases : Carrier → Prop) (density rate heat : Carrier → Nat)
       9381      (h_carrier : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → ∃ c, Realizes c)
       9382      (h_erase   : ∀ c, Realizes c → Erases c)
       9383      (h_pop     : ∀ c, Erases c → density c ≥ n0)
       9384      (h_rate    : ∀ c, Erases c → rate c ≥ r0)
       9385      (h_heat    : ∀ c, Erases c → heat c ≥ q0)
       9386      (h_couple  : ∀ c, Erases c → R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (density c) (rate c) (heat c)) :
       9387      ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → R ≥ n0 * r0 * q0 := by
       9388    intro hnot
       9389    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := h_carrier hnot
       9390    have he := h_erase c hc
       9391    exact Nat.le_trans (carrier_floor density rate heat c (h_pop c he) (h_rate c he) (h_heat c he)) (h_couple c he)
       9392  
       9393  end Bridge
       9394  
       9395  /-! ## VII-d · the heat theorem at its exact strength: the two cases, kept apart -/
       9396  
       9397  /-- Exact null: residual = 0 with positive rate and heat forces the population to zero. -/
       9398  theorem density_zero_from_exact_null {ρ r q : Nat} (hr : r > 0) (hq : q > 0)
       9399      (h0 : LeastErasureDoF.residual ρ r q = 0) : ρ = 0 :=
       9400    LeastErasureDoF.null_forces_zero hr hq h0
       9401  
       9402  /-- Finite sensitivity: residual ≤ ε with rate ≥ r₀ and heat ≥ q₀ bounds the population: ρ · r₀ q₀ ≤ ε. -/
       9403  theorem density_bound_at_finite_sensitivity {ρ r q r0 q0 ε : Nat}
       9404      (hR : LeastErasureDoF.residual ρ r q ≤ ε) (hr : r ≥ r0) (hq : q ≥ q0) :
       9405      ρ * r0 * q0 ≤ ε :=
       9406    LeastErasureDoF.density_bound_from_residual_bound hR hr hq
       9407  
       9408  /-! ## VII-e · THE CAPSTONE, every input printed -/
       9409  
       9410  /-- THE CAPSTONE. Five inputs, each printed, none carried by a structure:
       9411      h_id      the identification: the classical hypothesis is least erasure at the read configuration;
       9412      h_bridge  the bridge: a failure of least erasure there forces the residual observable to at least δ;
       9413      h_bound   the observational bound: the residual observable is at most ε;
       9414      h_gap     the gap: ε < δ;
       9415      h_pos     the threshold is positive (implied by h_gap over the naturals; printed because the Recommendation
       9416                prints it).
       9417      Conclusion: the classical hypothesis. The proof is pointwise and constructive: at each read point the
       9418      registration either fixes the point, or it does not and the bridge puts the residual at δ > ε ≥ R.
       9419      The cone is empty. An empty cone says the proof uses no axiom; it does not discharge a hypothesis. -/
       9420  theorem classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound
       9421      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {R δ ε : Nat}
       9422      (h_id     : ClassicalRH ↔ LeastErasure Zζ)
       9423      (h_bridge : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → R ≥ δ)
       9424      (h_bound  : R ≤ ε)
       9425      (h_gap    : ε < δ)
       9426      (h_pos    : 0 < δ) :
       9427      ClassicalRH := by
       9428    have _hδ : δ ≠ 0 := Nat.pos_iff_ne_zero.mp h_pos
       9429    apply h_id.mpr
       9430    intro p hp
       9431    match decEq (reg p) p with
       9432    | isTrue h => exact h
       9433    | isFalse h =>
       9434      have hnot : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ := fun hle => h (hle p hp)
       9435      have hRδ : R ≥ δ := h_bridge hnot
       9436      exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans hRδ h_bound) h_gap) (Nat.lt_irrefl δ)
       9437  
       9438  /-- THE CAPSTONE, EXPLODED: the nine inputs of the Final Scribal Recommendation. The reading, the six arrows of
       9439      the bridge, the bound, and the gap against the composed threshold n₀ r₀ q₀. -/
       9440  theorem classical_rh_from_the_arrows
       9441      {Carrier : Type} {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {R n0 r0 q0 ε : Nat}
       9442      (Realizes Erases : Carrier → Prop) (density rate heat : Carrier → Nat)
       9443      (h_read    : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ)
       9444      (h_carrier : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → ∃ c, Realizes c)
       9445      (h_erase   : ∀ c, Realizes c → Erases c)
       9446      (h_pop     : ∀ c, Erases c → density c ≥ n0)
       9447      (h_rate    : ∀ c, Erases c → rate c ≥ r0)
       9448      (h_heat    : ∀ c, Erases c → heat c ≥ q0)
       9449      (h_couple  : ∀ c, Erases c → R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (density c) (rate c) (heat c))
       9450      (h_bound   : R ≤ ε)
       9451      (h_gap     : ε < n0 * r0 * q0) :
       9452      ClassicalRH :=
       9453    classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound
       9454      (classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading h_read)
       9455      (off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal Realizes Erases density rate heat
       9456        h_carrier h_erase h_pop h_rate h_heat h_couple)
       9457      h_bound h_gap (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le ε) h_gap)
       9458  
       9459  /-- THE EXACT-NULL ROUTE, the Mandate II of the second edition, with its premise printed. If a failure of least
       9460      erasure realizes a population of positive size, rate and heat whose contribution the residual covers, and the
       9461      residual is EXACTLY zero, the hypothesis follows. The premise R = 0 is not what a measurement at finite
       9462      sensitivity reports; the paper's closure runs on the gap route above, and this theorem records where the
       9463      second edition's wording stood. -/
       9464  theorem classical_rh_from_identification_and_exact_null
       9465      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {R : Nat}
       9466      (h_id     : ClassicalRH ↔ LeastErasure Zζ)
       9467      (h_bridge : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → ∃ ρ r q : Nat, ρ > 0 ∧ r > 0 ∧ q > 0 ∧ R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual ρ r q)
       9468      (h_null   : R = 0) :
       9469      ClassicalRH := by
       9470    apply h_id.mpr
       9471    intro p hp
       9472    match decEq (reg p) p with
       9473    | isTrue h => exact h
       9474    | isFalse h =>
       9475      have hnot : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ := fun hle => h (hle p hp)
       9476      obtain ⟨ρ, r, q, hρ, hr, hq, hR⟩ := h_bridge hnot
       9477      have hpos := LeastErasureDoF.residual_pos hρ hr hq
       9478      rw [h_null] at hR
       9479      exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le hpos hR) (Nat.lt_irrefl 0)
       9480  
       9481  /-- NO THIRD POSITION. Given the identification, the bound and the gap, the denial of the hypothesis and the
       9482      bridge cannot both stand. A reader who denies the hypothesis has named the bridge as the arrow that fails;
       9483      a reader who grants the bridge has granted the hypothesis. Constructive; the cone is empty. -/
       9484  theorem no_third_position
       9485      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {R δ ε : Nat}
       9486      (h_id    : ClassicalRH ↔ LeastErasure Zζ)
       9487      (h_bound : R ≤ ε)
       9488      (h_gap   : ε < δ) :
       9489      ¬ (¬ ClassicalRH ∧ (¬ LeastErasure Zζ → R ≥ δ)) := by
       9490    intro ⟨hno, h_bridge⟩
       9491    have hnot : ¬ LeastErasure Zζ := fun hle => hno (h_id.mpr hle)
       9492    exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans (h_bridge hnot) h_bound) h_gap) (Nat.lt_irrefl δ)
       9493  
       9494  /-! ## VII-f · what the capstone does not do, by theorem: its inputs are keyed -/
       9495  
       9496  /-- The pair world of the off point is closed and lacks least erasure. -/
       9497  theorem pair_world_lacks_le : Closed (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ ¬ LeastErasure (pairWorld offPoint) :=
       9498    ⟨pair_world_closed offPoint,
       9499     fun hle => off_point_is_off ((reg_erases_nothing_iff offPoint).mp (hle offPoint (Or.inl rfl)))⟩
       9500  
       9501  /-- THE READING IS KEYED. No theorem of the interface identifies an arbitrary proposition with least erasure at
       9502      an arbitrary closed configuration: for the true proposition and the pair world the identification fails. The
       9503      identification is therefore an input, granted for the reading of Section 11 and for nothing else. -/
       9504  theorem the_reading_is_keyed :
       9505      ∃ (P : Prop) (S : Config), Closed S ∧ ¬ (P ↔ LeastErasure S) :=
       9506    ⟨True, pairWorld offPoint, pair_world_lacks_le.1,
       9507     fun h => pair_world_lacks_le.2 (h.mp trivial)⟩
       9508  
       9509  /-- THE BRIDGE IS KEYED. No theorem of the interface makes a failure of least erasure lift the residual: on the
       9510      pair world with R = 0 and δ = 1 the bridge fails. The bridge is therefore an input: derived from the physics
       9511      at the grade of its arrows, or granted by name, never read off the chart. -/
       9512  theorem the_bridge_is_keyed :
       9513      ∃ (S : Config) (R δ : Nat), Closed S ∧ ¬ LeastErasure S ∧ ¬ (¬ LeastErasure S → R ≥ δ) :=
       9514    ⟨pairWorld offPoint, 0, 1, pair_world_lacks_le.1, pair_world_lacks_le.2,
       9515     fun h => Nat.not_succ_le_zero 0 (h pair_world_lacks_le.2)⟩
       9516  
       9517  /-- THE BOUND DOES NOT CLOSE ALONE. A bound R ≤ ε with no bridge leaves least erasure undecided: the pair world
       9518      is closed, lacks least erasure, and is consistent with every bound. -/
       9519  theorem the_bound_alone_decides_nothing (ε : Nat) :
       9520      ∃ S : Config, Closed S ∧ ¬ LeastErasure S ∧ (0 : Nat) ≤ ε :=
       9521    ⟨pairWorld offPoint, pair_world_lacks_le.1, pair_world_lacks_le.2, Nat.zero_le ε⟩
       9522  
       9523  /-! ## VII-g · the hardened closure -/
       9524  
       9525  /-- THE HARDENED CLOSURE. The two-sided closure of Part VI, the seven-claim master seal of the companion kernel,
       9526      the identification reduced to the reading, the act as the premise packaged, the bridge composed, the two
       9527      cases of the heat theorem, the capstone in both forms, the exact-null route, no third position, and the three
       9528      keyed-input theorems, each by its exact type. -/
       9529  theorem the_hardened_closure :
       9530      (type_of% @BothSides.the_two_sided_closure) ∧
       9531      (type_of% @LeastErasureDoF.the_master_seal) ∧
       9532      (type_of% @classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading) ∧
       9533      (type_of% @the_act_is_the_premise_packaged) ∧
       9534      (type_of% @off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal) ∧
       9535      (type_of% @density_zero_from_exact_null) ∧
       9536      (type_of% @density_bound_at_finite_sensitivity) ∧
       9537      (type_of% @classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound) ∧
       9538      (type_of% @classical_rh_from_the_arrows) ∧
       9539      (type_of% @classical_rh_from_identification_and_exact_null) ∧
       9540      (type_of% @no_third_position) ∧
       9541      (type_of% @the_reading_is_keyed) ∧
       9542      (type_of% @the_bridge_is_keyed) ∧
       9543      (type_of% @the_bound_alone_decides_nothing) :=
       9544    ⟨@BothSides.the_two_sided_closure, @LeastErasureDoF.the_master_seal,
       9545     @classical_rh_iff_le_of_reading, @the_act_is_the_premise_packaged,
       9546     @off_line_zero_forces_observable_signal, @density_zero_from_exact_null,
       9547     @density_bound_at_finite_sensitivity, @classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound,
       9548     @classical_rh_from_the_arrows, @classical_rh_from_identification_and_exact_null,
       9549     @no_third_position, @the_reading_is_keyed, @the_bridge_is_keyed, @the_bound_alone_decides_nothing⟩
       9550  
       9551  end Hardening
       9552  end PartVII

       9644  /-! # PART VIII · the physico-formal carrier — OPTIONAL CORROBORATION, NOT REQUIRED FOR THE FORMAL LOOP -/
       9645  /-!
       9646    PART VIII · THE PHYSICO-FORMAL CARRIER.
       9647  
       9648    Part VII took the carrier as a type variable and six arrows as hypotheses. Part VIII replaces the variable by a
       9649    type given by its constructors, `PhysicalCarrier`: a self-conjugate state at a height (the neutral sector), or a
       9650    member of a conjugate pair at a height with the sign that tells it from its partner (the charged sector). Charge
       9651    conjugation `C` and annihilation `annihilate` are defined on it by cases; the physical carrier is then an instance
       9652    of the seed's own carrier abstraction (Part II, `PrimeFreedom.Carrier`): `C` is a fold, `annihilate` its
       9653    registration, and every law of that namespace holds on the carrier by theorem.
       9654  
       9655    The map from a zero to its carrier, `map_zero_to_carrier`, is total by the integer's constructors and a bijection
       9656    with the chart; it carries the fold to charge conjugation, the line to the neutral sector, and the registration to
       9657    annihilation. On this map two of Part VII's six arrows are theorems: an off-line zero is carried to the charged
       9658    sector (h_carrier), where annihilation does not fix it and sends it and its partner to one state, so one label is
       9659    lost and kept nowhere on the carrier (h_erase). A third, h_heat, is Landauer's law entered as a definition,
       9660    `landauerHeatPerEvent T = T · ln 2`, with a temperature floor: the arrow is then the monotonicity of a product.
       9661  
       9662    What remains is physics, and is printed as hypotheses of the capstone: h_realize, that the vacuum instantiates
       9663    the carrier of every read zero; h_pop and h_rate, the population and rate floors of a realized charged carrier;
       9664    h_temp, the temperature floor; h_couple, that the residual observable covers the carrier's contribution; the
       9665    reading h_read; and a certified bound B. No definition below makes any of these true. A theorem that the universe
       9666    realizes a state is not available to any logic: it enters as an axiom, which this file declares none of; as a
       9667    hypothesis, which is what is done here; or as a definition that is the claim restated, which the Final Scribal
       9668    Recommendation forbids (no hidden premise in a structure field). The theorems of VIII-f record, by witness, that
       9669    the realization predicate is the input: one choice of it makes h_realize hold at every configuration, another
       9670    makes it fail at the pair world.
       9671  
       9672    NOTE: in the flipped formal register, the observational inputs of this part
       9673    (h_realize, h_pop, h_rate, h_temp, h_couple, h_read, the certified bound B) are SUPERSEDED in the
       9674    core arch by the formalized compute cargo — the local `VerificationEvent` enacting `Stage1`
       9675    (`ApparatusCargo`), the formal registration projection, and `BoundChainMathlib`'s proved links
       9676    (`h_read_proved`, `h_id_proved`) over ℂ. The eight empirical inputs, including
       9677    `CertifiedObservationalBound`, bath temperatures, Landauer heat floors, carrier population and
       9678    rate floors, and residual flux couplings, are retired from the active arch and remain in this
       9679    file, untouched, as fenced conditional theorems (optional retrospective corroboration),
       9680    matching the status of `ApparatusCargo.stage2_optional_corroboration`.
       9681  -/
       9682  section PartVIII
       9683  namespace PhysicoFormal
       9684  open RememberedOffered
       9685  
       9686  /-! ## VIII-a · the carrier, by constructors; conjugation and annihilation, by cases -/
       9687  
       9688  /-- THE PHYSICAL CARRIER. A state of the sector in which a zero is realized is one of two kinds:
       9689      `selfConjugate t`, a state at height t that charge conjugation fixes, the neutral sector; or
       9690      `conjugatePair m t sign`, a member of the conjugate pair of magnitude m + 1 at height t, with `sign` the one
       9691      label that tells it from its partner, the charged sector. A type given by its constructors, inhabited at every
       9692      height; which of its states the vacuum instantiates is the premise h_realize of VIII-e, not a field here. -/
       9693  inductive PhysicalCarrier where
       9694    | selfConjugate (t : Int)
       9695    | conjugatePair (m : Nat) (t : Int) (sign : Bool)
       9696  
       9697  /-- Charge conjugation: it fixes the neutral sector and flips the sign in the charged sector. -/
       9698  def C : PhysicalCarrier → PhysicalCarrier
       9699    | .selfConjugate t => .selfConjugate t
       9700    | .conjugatePair m t s => .conjugatePair m t (!s)
       9701  
       9702  theorem C_involutive (c : PhysicalCarrier) : C (C c) = c := by
       9703    cases c with
       9704    | selfConjugate t => rfl
       9705    | conjugatePair m t s => cases s <;> rfl
       9706  
       9707  /-- The neutral sector: the self-conjugate states. -/
       9708  def Neutral : PhysicalCarrier → Prop
       9709    | .selfConjugate _ => True
       9710    | .conjugatePair _ _ _ => False
       9711  
       9712  /-- The neutral sector is exactly the fixed locus of charge conjugation. -/
       9713  theorem neutral_iff_C_fixed (c : PhysicalCarrier) : Neutral c ↔ C c = c := by
       9714    cases c with
       9715    | selfConjugate t => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => trivial⟩
       9716    | conjugatePair m t s => exact ⟨fun h => h.elim, fun h => by cases s <;> cases h⟩
       9717  
       9718  /-- Fixedness under charge conjugation is decided on the carrier, by cases. -/
       9719  theorem carrier_em (c : PhysicalCarrier) : C c = c ∨ C c ≠ c := by
       9720    cases c with
       9721    | selfConjugate t => exact Or.inl rfl
       9722    | conjugatePair m t s => exact Or.inr (fun h => by cases s <;> cases h)
       9723  
       9724  /-- Annihilation, the physical discard: a member of a pair goes to the neutral state at its height; a neutral state
       9725      stays. The sign is kept in no register of the carrier. -/
       9726  def annihilate : PhysicalCarrier → PhysicalCarrier
       9727    | .selfConjugate t => .selfConjugate t
       9728    | .conjugatePair _ t _ => .selfConjugate t
       9729  
       9730  theorem annihilate_lands (c : PhysicalCarrier) : C (annihilate c) = annihilate c := by
       9731    cases c <;> rfl
       9732  
       9733  theorem annihilate_fixes (c : PhysicalCarrier) (h : C c = c) : annihilate c = c := by
       9734    cases c with
       9735    | selfConjugate t => rfl
       9736    | conjugatePair m t s => cases s <;> cases h
       9737  
       9738  theorem annihilate_forgets (c : PhysicalCarrier) : annihilate (C c) = annihilate c := by
       9739    cases c <;> rfl
       9740  
       9741  /-- Annihilation fixes a state exactly when the state is neutral. -/
       9742  theorem annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral (c : PhysicalCarrier) : annihilate c = c ↔ Neutral c := by
       9743    cases c with
       9744    | selfConjugate t => exact ⟨fun _ => trivial, fun _ => rfl⟩
       9745    | conjugatePair m t s => exact ⟨fun h => (by cases h), fun h => h.elim⟩
       9746  
       9747  /-- A conjugate pair is two states with one image under annihilation: the sign is the bit that annihilation erases. -/
       9748  theorem pair_is_two_states_one_image (m : Nat) (t : Int) :
       9749      PhysicalCarrier.conjugatePair m t true ≠ PhysicalCarrier.conjugatePair m t false ∧
       9750      annihilate (.conjugatePair m t true) = annihilate (.conjugatePair m t false) :=
       9751    ⟨fun h => (by cases h), rfl⟩
       9752  
       9753  /-- THE PHYSICAL CARRIER IS AN INSTANCE OF THE SEED'S CARRIER ABSTRACTION (Part II): charge conjugation is a fold. -/
       9754  def carrierFold : PrimeFreedom.Carrier.Fold PhysicalCarrier := ⟨C, C_involutive⟩
       9755  
       9756  /-- Annihilation is a registration for that fold: it lands on the neutral sector, fixes it, and forgets the sign. -/
       9757  def carrierReg : PrimeFreedom.Carrier.Registration carrierFold :=
       9758    ⟨annihilate, annihilate_lands, annihilate_fixes, annihilate_forgets⟩
       9759  
       9760  /-- THE CLOSURE ON THE PHYSICAL CARRIER: the four laws Part II proves on any carrier, instantiated on this one by
       9761      theorem. Least erasure is the value; the value is lossless registration; the lossless member of a record is
       9762      unique; every charged state gives two worlds of one record that differ in the value. -/
       9763  theorem the_closure_on_the_physical_carrier :
       9764      type_of% (PrimeFreedom.Carrier.the_closure_on_any_carrier carrierReg carrier_em) :=
       9765    PrimeFreedom.Carrier.the_closure_on_any_carrier carrierReg carrier_em
       9766  
       9767  /-! ## VIII-b · the map from a zero to its carrier, total and bijective, equivariant -/
       9768  
       9769  /-- THE MAP FROM A ZERO TO ITS CARRIER. A point of the chart at offset d and height t goes: on the line, to the
       9770      self-conjugate state at t; at offset n + 1, to the positive member of the pair of magnitude n + 1 at t; at offset
       9771      −(n + 1), to the negative member. Total, by the integer's three constructors. -/
       9772  def map_zero_to_carrier : Point → PhysicalCarrier
       9773    | (Int.ofNat 0, t) => .selfConjugate t
       9774    | (Int.ofNat (n + 1), t) => .conjugatePair n t true
       9775    | (Int.negSucc n, t) => .conjugatePair n t false
       9776  
       9777  /-- The inverse: a carrier state read back as a point of the chart. -/
       9778  def carrier_to_zero : PhysicalCarrier → Point
       9779    | .selfConjugate t => (Int.ofNat 0, t)
       9780    | .conjugatePair n t true => (Int.ofNat (n + 1), t)
       9781    | .conjugatePair n t false => (Int.negSucc n, t)
       9782  
       9783  theorem map_left_inverse (p : Point) : carrier_to_zero (map_zero_to_carrier p) = p := by
       9784    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       9785    cases d with
       9786    | ofNat n => cases n <;> rfl
       9787    | negSucc n => rfl
       9788  
       9789  theorem map_right_inverse (c : PhysicalCarrier) : map_zero_to_carrier (carrier_to_zero c) = c := by
       9790    cases c with
       9791    | selfConjugate t => rfl
       9792    | conjugatePair n t s => cases s <;> rfl
       9793  
       9794  /-- The map is injective: two zeros with one carrier are one zero. -/
       9795  theorem map_injective (p q : Point) (h : map_zero_to_carrier p = map_zero_to_carrier q) : p = q := by
       9796    rw [← map_left_inverse p, ← map_left_inverse q, h]
       9797  
       9798  /-- The map is surjective: every carrier state is the carrier of a zero. -/
       9799  theorem map_surjective (c : PhysicalCarrier) : ∃ p, map_zero_to_carrier p = c :=
       9800    ⟨carrier_to_zero c, map_right_inverse c⟩
       9801  
       9802  /-- EQUIVARIANCE. The fold of the chart is charge conjugation on the carrier: s ↦ 1 − s̄ is C. -/
       9803  theorem map_fold (p : Point) : map_zero_to_carrier (fold p) = C (map_zero_to_carrier p) := by
       9804    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       9805    cases d with
       9806    | ofNat n => cases n <;> rfl
       9807    | negSucc n => rfl
       9808  
       9809  /-- The line of the chart is the neutral sector of the carrier. -/
       9810  theorem map_neutral_iff_onLine (p : Point) : Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) ↔ onLine p := by
       9811    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       9812    cases d with
       9813    | ofNat n =>
       9814      cases n with
       9815      | zero => exact ⟨fun _ => rfl, fun _ => trivial⟩
       9816      | succ n => exact ⟨fun h => h.elim, fun h => by cases h⟩
       9817    | negSucc n => exact ⟨fun h => h.elim, fun h => by cases h⟩
       9818  
       9819  /-- The registration of the chart is annihilation on the carrier. -/
       9820  theorem map_reg (p : Point) : map_zero_to_carrier (reg p) = annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) := by
       9821    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
       9822    cases d with
       9823    | ofNat n => cases n <;> rfl
       9824    | negSucc n => rfl
       9825  
       9826  /-- Least erasure on the chart is least erasure on the carrier, configuration by configuration, through the map. -/
       9827  theorem le_transports (S : Config) :
       9828      LeastErasure S ↔ ∀ p, S p → annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) = map_zero_to_carrier p := by
       9829    constructor
       9830    · intro h p hp
       9831      rw [← map_reg, h p hp]
       9832    · intro h p hp
       9833      exact (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mpr ((map_neutral_iff_onLine p).mp
       9834        ((annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral _).mp (h p hp)))
       9835  
       9836  /-! ## VIII-c · the mathematical violation forces the physical discard -/
       9837  
       9838  /-- MATHEMATICAL VIOLATION FORCES PHYSICAL DISCARD. A zero off the line is carried to the charged sector; there
       9839      charge conjugation moves it, annihilation does not fix it, and annihilation sends it and its conjugate partner
       9840      to one state. One label, the sign, is lost and kept in no register of the carrier. Theorem; no premise. This
       9841      is h_carrier and h_erase of Part VII, discharged on the concrete carrier. -/
       9842  theorem mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) :
       9843      ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) ∧
       9844      C (map_zero_to_carrier p) ≠ map_zero_to_carrier p ∧
       9845      annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) ≠ map_zero_to_carrier p ∧
       9846      annihilate (C (map_zero_to_carrier p)) = annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) :=
       9847    have hn : ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) := fun hN => h ((map_neutral_iff_onLine p).mp hN)
       9848    ⟨hn,
       9849     fun hC => hn ((neutral_iff_C_fixed _).mpr hC),
       9850     fun hA => hn ((annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral _).mp hA),
       9851     annihilate_forgets _⟩
       9852  
       9853  /-- ON THE LINE NOTHING IS DISCARDED: the carrier is neutral and annihilation fixes it. -/
       9854  theorem on_line_discards_nothing (p : Point) (h : onLine p) :
       9855      Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) ∧ annihilate (map_zero_to_carrier p) = map_zero_to_carrier p :=
       9856    have hN := (map_neutral_iff_onLine p).mpr h
       9857    ⟨hN, (annihilate_fixes_iff_neutral _).mpr hN⟩
       9858  
       9859  /-! ## VIII-d · the energetic bookkeeping: labels, entropy, heat -/
       9860  
       9861  /-- LANDAUER'S LAW, ENTERED AS A DEFINITION: the heat of erasing one label at temperature T is T · ln 2 in the
       9862      kernel's units (ln 2 scaled by 10⁶). It is a physical law, not derived here; the kernel's
       9863      `heat_from_joint_conservation` carries only its shape, and no theorem below pretends otherwise. What the
       9864      theorems derive is the count of labels and that the heat is positive exactly when the count is. -/
       9865  def landauerHeatPerEvent (T : Nat) : Nat := T * LeastErasureDoF.ln2_scaled
       9866  
       9867  /-- The heat of erasing b labels at temperature T. -/
       9868  def landauerHeat (bits T : Nat) : Nat := bits * landauerHeatPerEvent T
       9869  
       9870  /-- The heat is the seed's price (Part III, `price`) at the temperature T · ln 2. -/
       9871  theorem landauerHeat_is_price (bits T : Nat) : landauerHeat bits T = price (landauerHeatPerEvent T) bits := rfl
       9872  
       9873  /-- The per-event heat is monotone in the temperature: a temperature floor is a heat floor. This is h_heat of
       9874      Part VII, derived from the law and the floor. -/
       9875  theorem heat_floor_from_temperature {T T0 : Nat} (h : T ≥ T0) :
       9876      landauerHeatPerEvent T ≥ landauerHeatPerEvent T0 :=
       9877    Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ h
       9878  
       9879  /-- The per-event heat at the CMB temperature of the kernel is positive. -/
       9880  theorem heat_at_cmb_positive : landauerHeatPerEvent LeastErasureDoF.cmb_mK > 0 :=
       9881    Nat.mul_pos (by decide) (by decide)
       9882  
       9883  /-- A FINITE CONFIGURATION AS A SYSTEM OF THE KERNEL: one record per height on the line and one per pair; one free
       9884      label, the sign, per pair; the total the product. -/
       9885  def systemOf (F : FinCfg) : LeastErasureDoF.System :=
       9886    ⟨F.line.length + F.pairs.length, F.pairs.length,
       9887     (F.line.length + F.pairs.length) * 2 ^ F.pairs.length, rfl⟩
       9888  
       9889  /-- The same records with every sign gone: the system after annihilation. -/
       9890  def systemAfter (F : FinCfg) : LeastErasureDoF.System :=
       9891    ⟨F.line.length + F.pairs.length, 0, (F.line.length + F.pairs.length) * 2 ^ 0, rfl⟩
       9892  
       9893  /-- The entropy the kernel assigns to the configuration is one ln 2 per pair, and after annihilation it is zero:
       9894      the entropy drop of the discard is the erased count times ln 2. -/
       9895  theorem entropy_of_discard (F : FinCfg) :
       9896      LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy (systemOf F) = erased F * LeastErasureDoF.ln2_scaled ∧
       9897      LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy (systemAfter F) = 0 :=
       9898    ⟨rfl, Nat.zero_mul _⟩
       9899  
       9900  /-- One annihilation is one erasure of the kernel: a system with one more label and twice the total, taken to
       9901      this system. Records kept, one label lost, total halved. -/
       9902  def oneAnnihilation (s : LeastErasureDoF.System) (hs : s.distinct > 0) : LeastErasureDoF.EraseProcess :=
       9903    { before := ⟨s.distinct, s.free + 1, 2 * s.total, by
       9904        have h_inv : s.total = s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free := s.inv
       9905        have h1 : 2 * s.total = 2 * (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) :=
       9906          congrArg (fun x => 2 * x) h_inv
       9907        have h2 : 2 * (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) = (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) :=
       9908          Nat.two_mul _
       9909        have h3 : (Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2 = (Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (Nat.pow 2 s.free) := Nat.mul_two _
       9910        have h4 : s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2) = s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (Nat.pow 2 s.free)) :=
       9911          congrArg (fun x => s.distinct * x) h3
       9912        have h5 : s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (Nat.pow 2 s.free))
       9913            = s.distinct * (Nat.pow 2 s.free) + s.distinct * (Nat.pow 2 s.free) :=
       9914          Nat.left_distrib _ _ _
       9915        have h6 : s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2) = (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) + (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) :=
       9916          Eq.trans h4 h5
       9917        have h7 : 2 * (s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 s.free) = s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2) :=
       9918          Eq.trans h2 (Eq.symm h6)
       9919        have h8 : s.distinct * ((Nat.pow 2 s.free) * 2) = s.distinct * Nat.pow 2 (s.free + 1) := rfl
       9920        exact Eq.trans (Eq.trans h1 h7) h8⟩
       9921      after := s
       9922      h_distinct := rfl
       9923      h_free := rfl
       9924      h_total := rfl
       9925      h_gt := by
       9926        show s.total < 2 * s.total
       9927        have hpos : 0 < s.total := by
       9928          rw [s.inv]; exact Nat.mul_pos hs (Nat.two_pow_pos _)
       9929        rw [Nat.two_mul]
       9930        exact Nat.lt_add_of_pos_left hpos }
       9931  
       9932  /-- The kernel's entropy law holds of each annihilation by instance. -/
       9933  theorem annihilation_drops_one_ln2 (s : LeastErasureDoF.System) (hs : s.distinct > 0) :
       9934      LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy (oneAnnihilation s hs).after + LeastErasureDoF.ln2_scaled =
       9935        LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy (oneAnnihilation s hs).before :=
       9936    LeastErasureDoF.sysEntropy_decrease _
       9937  
       9938  /-- DISCARD FORCES HEAT GENERATION. The annihilation of a finite configuration erases one label per off-line pair,
       9939      the seed's `erased`; at any positive temperature its Landauer heat is zero exactly at the value, and positive
       9940      whenever a point stands off the line. The count is theorem; the law is `landauerHeatPerEvent`. -/
       9941  theorem discard_forces_heat_generation (F : FinCfg) (T : Nat) (hT : 0 < T) :
       9942      (landauerHeat (erased F) T = 0 ↔ Value F.pts) ∧
       9943      (¬ Value F.pts → landauerHeat (erased F) T > 0) :=
       9944    have hq : 0 < landauerHeatPerEvent T := Nat.mul_pos hT (by decide)
       9945    have hiff : landauerHeat (erased F) T = 0 ↔ Value F.pts := price_zero_iff_value F _ hq
       9946    ⟨hiff, fun hv => Nat.pos_of_ne_zero (fun h0 => hv (hiff.mp h0))⟩
       9947  
       9948  /-! ## VIII-e · the certified bound, the physical premises, and the physico-formal capstone -/
       9949  
       9950  /-- A CERTIFIED OBSERVATIONAL BOUND: the residual observable R, the sensitivity ε, the certificate R ≤ ε, and the
       9951      name of the dataset that issued it. A measurement is a premise by its nature; this is the type it is entered as. -/
       9952  structure CertifiedObservationalBound where
       9953    R : Nat
       9954    ε : Nat
       9955    certificate : R ≤ ε
       9956    dataset : String
       9957  
       9958  /-- The detection gap: the uniform floor a realized charged carrier puts under the residual observable,
       9959      δ = n₀ · r₀ · (T₀ · ln 2). -/
       9960  def detectionGap (n0 r0 T0 : Nat) : Nat := n0 * r0 * landauerHeatPerEvent T0
       9961  
       9962  /-- The gap is positive exactly when its three floors are. -/
       9963  theorem detectionGap_pos {n0 r0 T0 : Nat} (hn : n0 > 0) (hr : r0 > 0) (hT : T0 > 0) : detectionGap n0 r0 T0 > 0 :=
       9964    Nat.mul_pos (Nat.mul_pos hn hr) (Nat.mul_pos hT (by decide))
       9965  
       9966  /-- THE SIGNAL FLOOR OF A REALIZED CHARGED CARRIER, from the three floors and the coupling: population × rate × heat
       9967      per event is at least n₀ · r₀ · (T₀ · ln 2), and the residual covers it. -/
       9968  theorem signal_floor {R n0 r0 T0 T : Nat} (population rate : PhysicalCarrier → Nat) (c : PhysicalCarrier)
       9969      (h_pop : population c ≥ n0) (h_rate : rate c ≥ r0) (h_temp : T ≥ T0)
       9970      (h_couple : R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (population c) (rate c) (landauerHeatPerEvent T)) :
       9971      R ≥ detectionGap n0 r0 T0 :=
       9972    Nat.le_trans (Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.mul_le_mul h_pop h_rate) (heat_floor_from_temperature h_temp)) h_couple
       9973  
       9974  /-- EVERY VIOLATION EXCEEDS THE DETECTION GAP. Two physical premises, named: the vacuum instantiates the carrier of
       9975      every read zero (h_realize); a realized charged carrier puts the floor δ under R (h_signal). Then a read zero
       9976      off the line forces R ≥ δ. That the zero's carrier is charged is theorem (VIII-c), not premise. -/
       9977  theorem every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap
       9978      {Zζ : Config} {R δ : Nat} (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
       9979      (h_realize : ∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
       9980      (h_signal  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → R ≥ δ)
       9981      (p : Point) (hp : Zζ p) (hoff : ¬ onLine p) : R ≥ δ :=
       9982    h_signal _ (h_realize p hp) (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard p hoff).1
       9983  
       9984  /-- THE BRIDGE OF PART VII, DERIVED. From the two physical premises, a failure of least erasure at the read
       9985      configuration forces R ≥ δ: exactly h_bridge of `classical_rh_from_identification_gap_and_bound`. The step from
       9986      a failed universal to a witness is classical; the cone is printed. -/
       9987  theorem bridge_from_realization
       9988      {Zζ : Config} {R δ : Nat} (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
       9989      (h_realize : ∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
       9990      (h_signal  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → R ≥ δ) :
       9991      ¬ LeastErasure Zζ → R ≥ δ := by
       9992    intro hnot
       9993    apply Classical.byContradiction
       9994    intro hlt
       9995    apply hnot
       9996    intro p hp
       9997    apply (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mpr
       9998    apply Classical.byContradiction
       9999    intro hoff
      10000    exact hlt (every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap realized h_realize h_signal p hp hoff)
      10001  
      10002  /-- THE PHYSICO-FORMAL CLOSURE. The capstone, every input printed, the carrier concrete:
      10003      h_read     the reading: the classical hypothesis is the value of the configuration at which the zeros are read;
      10004      h_realize  the vacuum instantiates the carrier of every read zero                               (physics);
      10005      h_pop      a realized charged carrier is a population of at least n₀                            (physics);
      10006      h_rate     a realized charged carrier annihilates at a rate of at least r₀ during the observation (physics);
      10007      h_temp     the temperature during the observation is at least T₀                                (physics);
      10008      h_couple   the residual observable covers the carrier's contribution, population × rate × heat   (physics);
      10009      B          a certified bound R ≤ ε from a named dataset                                           (measurement);
      10010      h_gap      ε < δ = n₀ · r₀ · (T₀ · ln 2)                                                          (arithmetic on the two).
      10011      Discharged on the carrier, no longer hypotheses: that an off-line zero is realized as a charged state, that its
      10012      annihilation erases one label, and that the heat per label is T · ln 2 ≥ T₀ · ln 2.
      10013      Conclusion: the classical hypothesis. Pointwise and constructive; the cone is empty. An empty cone says the
      10014      proof uses no axiom; it discharges none of the eight inputs. -/
      10015  theorem classical_rh_from_physico_formal_closure
      10016      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {n0 r0 T0 T : Nat}
      10017      (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) (population rate : PhysicalCarrier → Nat)
      10018      (B : CertifiedObservationalBound)
      10019      (h_read    : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ)
      10020      (h_realize : ∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
      10021      (h_pop     : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → population c ≥ n0)
      10022      (h_rate    : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → rate c ≥ r0)
      10023      (h_temp    : T ≥ T0)
      10024      (h_couple  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c →
      10025                     B.R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (population c) (rate c) (landauerHeatPerEvent T))
      10026      (h_gap     : B.ε < detectionGap n0 r0 T0) :
      10027      ClassicalRH := by
      10028    apply h_read.mpr
      10029    intro p hp
      10030    match decEq p.1 0 with
      10031    | isTrue h => exact h
      10032    | isFalse hoff =>
      10033      have hc : ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier p) := (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard p hoff).1
      10034      have hr := h_realize p hp
      10035      have hfloor : B.R ≥ detectionGap n0 r0 T0 :=
      10036        signal_floor population rate _ (h_pop _ hr hc) (h_rate _ hr hc) h_temp (h_couple _ hr hc)
      10037      exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans hfloor B.certificate) h_gap) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
      10038  
      10039  /-- NO THIRD POSITION, ON THE CARRIER. Given the reading, the bound and the gap, the denial of the hypothesis and
      10040      the two physical premises cannot all stand: whoever denies the hypothesis has named h_realize or h_signal as
      10041      the premise that fails. -/
      10042  theorem no_third_position_on_the_carrier
      10043      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {δ : Nat} (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
      10044      (B : CertifiedObservationalBound)
      10045      (h_read : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ) (h_gap : B.ε < δ) :
      10046      ¬ (¬ ClassicalRH ∧ (∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p)) ∧
      10047         (∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → B.R ≥ δ)) := by
      10048    intro ⟨hno, h_realize, h_signal⟩
      10049    apply hno
      10050    apply h_read.mpr
      10051    intro p hp
      10052    match decEq p.1 0 with
      10053    | isTrue h => exact h
      10054    | isFalse hoff =>
      10055      have hRδ := every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap realized h_realize h_signal p hp hoff
      10056      exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans hRδ B.certificate) h_gap) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
      10057  
      10058  /-! ## VIII-f · what is premise, shown by witness -/
      10059  
      10060  /-- THE REALIZATION IS THE PREMISE. The predicate that says which carriers the vacuum instantiates is an input:
      10061      under the predicate that realizes every state, h_realize holds at every configuration; under the predicate that
      10062      realizes none, h_realize fails at the pair world of the off point. No theorem of this file chooses between them. -/
      10063  theorem realization_is_the_premise :
      10064      (∃ realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop, ∀ S : Config, ∀ p, S p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p)) ∧
      10065      (∃ realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop, ¬ ∀ p, pairWorld offPoint p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p)) :=
      10066    ⟨⟨fun _ => True, fun _ _ _ => trivial⟩,
      10067     ⟨fun _ => False, fun h => h offPoint (Or.inl rfl)⟩⟩
      10068  
      10069  /-- THE CARRIER ALONE DECIDES NOTHING. The pair world of the off point is closed, lacks least erasure, and its
      10070      carriers are charged; with no realization premise and no bound no theorem above reaches the value there. -/
      10071  theorem the_carrier_alone_decides_nothing :
      10072      Closed (pairWorld offPoint) ∧ ¬ LeastErasure (pairWorld offPoint) ∧
      10073      ¬ Neutral (map_zero_to_carrier offPoint) :=
      10074    ⟨pair_world_closed offPoint,
      10075     fun hle => off_point_is_off ((reg_erases_nothing_iff offPoint).mp (hle offPoint (Or.inl rfl))),
      10076     (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard offPoint off_point_is_off).1⟩
      10077  
      10078  /-- THE LAW IS NOT DERIVED. Landauer's heat is a definition of this file: at temperature zero it is zero for every
      10079      count. The theorem records that nothing in the kernel forces the heat, only counts it. -/
      10080  theorem landauer_is_entered_not_derived (bits : Nat) : landauerHeat bits 0 = 0 := by
      10081    unfold landauerHeat landauerHeatPerEvent
      10082    rw [Nat.zero_mul, Nat.mul_zero]
      10083  
      10084  /-! ## VIII-h · the root on the physical side: the floor is there, and the realization is not -/
      10085  
      10086  /-- THE PHYSICAL FLOOR: that some state is realized. -/
      10087  def PhysicalFloor (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) : Prop := ∃ c, realized c
      10088  
      10089  /-- THE PHYSICAL FLOOR IS SELF-GROUNDING, in the seed's own sense (Part I, `SelfGrounding`): an act of measurement
      10090      is a realized state, so every act, the act of denial included, instantiates the floor. Constructed, not posited:
      10091      the acts, one act, and the state each act realizes are the three fields, and the floor follows from them. -/
      10092  def physicalFloorGrounding (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) (Act : Type) (anAct : Act)
      10093      (stateOf : Act → PhysicalCarrier) (h : ∀ a, realized (stateOf a)) :
      10094      SelfGrounding (PhysicalFloor realized) :=
      10095    ⟨Act, anAct, fun a => ⟨stateOf a, h a⟩⟩
      10096  
      10097  /-- THE PHYSICAL FLOOR DECIDES NO REALIZATION. Under the predicate that realizes exactly the apparatus state, the
      10098      floor holds, the floor is self-grounding, and the realization of the off-line zero fails at the pair world. The
      10099      floor is there and the carrier of the off-line zero is not: the mirror, on the physical side, of the seed's
      10100      `the_floor_alone_decides_no_value`. The passage from "some state is realized" to "the carrier of every read zero
      10101      is realized" is not an inference from the floor; it is the second layer, the act at the configuration. -/
      10102  theorem the_physical_floor_decides_no_realization :
      10103      ∃ realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop,
      10104        PhysicalFloor realized ∧
      10105        SelfVerifying (PhysicalFloor realized) ∧
      10106        ¬ ∀ p, pairWorld offPoint p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p) :=
      10107    ⟨fun c => c = PhysicalCarrier.selfConjugate 0,
      10108     ⟨_, rfl⟩,
      10109     fun _ => ⟨_, rfl⟩,
      10110     fun h => by have e := h offPoint (Or.inl rfl); cases e⟩
      10111  
      10112  /-- THE REALIZATION IS NOT THE FLOOR: identified on every configuration, they would agree at the pair world, where
      10113      the floor holds and the realization fails. The mirror of the seed's `floor_is_not_least_erasure`. -/
      10114  theorem realization_is_not_the_floor :
      10115      ¬ ∀ realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop, ∀ S : Config,
      10116          (PhysicalFloor realized ↔ ∀ p, S p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p)) := by
      10117    intro h
      10118    obtain ⟨realized, hfloor, _, hfail⟩ := the_physical_floor_decides_no_realization
      10119    exact hfail ((h realized (pairWorld offPoint)).mp hfloor)
      10120  
      10121  /-- THE PHYSICAL ROUTE READS THE ROOT TWICE. The physical premises, the certified bound and the gap deliver, at the
      10122      read configuration, exactly what the seed says the act supplies: the root read twice, `RootReadTwice Zζ`, which
      10123      is the value there by `the_root_read_twice_is_the_value`. The physics is the second layer, not the first. -/
      10124  theorem the_physical_route_reads_the_root_twice
      10125      {Zζ : Config} {n0 r0 T0 T : Nat}
      10126      (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) (population rate : PhysicalCarrier → Nat)
      10127      (B : CertifiedObservationalBound)
      10128      (h_realize : ∀ p, Zζ p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
      10129      (h_pop     : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → population c ≥ n0)
      10130      (h_rate    : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → rate c ≥ r0)
      10131      (h_temp    : T ≥ T0)
      10132      (h_couple  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c →
      10133                     B.R ≥ LeastErasureDoF.residual (population c) (rate c) (landauerHeatPerEvent T))
      10134      (h_gap     : B.ε < detectionGap n0 r0 T0) :
      10135      RootReadTwice Zζ :=
      10136    (the_root_read_twice_is_the_value Zζ).mpr
      10137      (classical_rh_from_physico_formal_closure (ClassicalRH := Value Zζ) realized population rate B Iff.rfl
      10138        h_realize h_pop h_rate h_temp h_couple h_gap)
      10139  
      10140  /-- THE ONE EXIT, SHAPED. Under the reading, a certified bound, the gap, and the signal floor of a realized charged
      10141      carrier, a denial of the hypothesis asserts a read zero off the line whose carrier is realized in no measured
      10142      register: a second register, a second world. The denier owns that assertion; nothing else is open. The step from
      10143      the failed universal to its witness is classical; the cone is printed. -/
      10144  theorem the_one_exit_is_a_second_register
      10145      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Zζ : Config} {δ : Nat} (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
      10146      (B : CertifiedObservationalBound) (h_read : ClassicalRH ↔ Value Zζ) (h_gap : B.ε < δ)
      10147      (h_signal : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → B.R ≥ δ) :
      10148      ¬ ClassicalRH → ∃ p, Zζ p ∧ ¬ onLine p ∧ ¬ realized (map_zero_to_carrier p) := by
      10149    intro hno
      10150    apply Classical.byContradiction
      10151    intro hnone
      10152    apply hno
      10153    apply h_read.mpr
      10154    intro p hp
      10155    match decEq p.1 0 with
      10156    | isTrue h => exact h
      10157    | isFalse hoff =>
      10158      exact (hnone ⟨p, hp, hoff, fun hr =>
      10159        absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans
      10160          (h_signal _ hr (mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard p hoff).1) B.certificate) h_gap)
      10161          (Nat.lt_irrefl _)⟩).elim
      10162  
      10163  /-! ## VIII-g · the physico-formal closure, bound -/
      10164  
      10165  /-- THE PHYSICO-FORMAL CLOSURE, BOUND. The hardened closure of Part VII; the closure on the physical carrier; the
      10166      map's two inverses and its equivariance; the line as the neutral sector; the registration as annihilation; the
      10167      violation forcing the discard; the discard forcing the heat; every violation exceeding the gap; the bridge
      10168      derived; the capstone; no third position on the carrier; the two witnesses of what is premise; and the four
      10169      laws of the root on the physical side: the floor decides no realization, the realization is not the floor, the
      10170      physical route reads the root twice, and the one exit is a second register. -/
      10171  theorem the_physico_formal_closure :
      10172      (type_of% @Hardening.the_hardened_closure) ∧
      10173      (type_of% @the_closure_on_the_physical_carrier) ∧
      10174      (type_of% @map_left_inverse) ∧
      10175      (type_of% @map_right_inverse) ∧
      10176      (type_of% @map_fold) ∧
      10177      (type_of% @map_neutral_iff_onLine) ∧
      10178      (type_of% @map_reg) ∧
      10179      (type_of% @le_transports) ∧
      10180      (type_of% @mathematical_violation_forces_physical_discard) ∧
      10181      (type_of% @discard_forces_heat_generation) ∧
      10182      (type_of% @every_violation_exceeds_detection_gap) ∧
      10183      (type_of% @bridge_from_realization) ∧
      10184      (type_of% @classical_rh_from_physico_formal_closure) ∧
      10185      (type_of% @no_third_position_on_the_carrier) ∧
      10186      (type_of% @realization_is_the_premise) ∧
      10187      (type_of% @landauer_is_entered_not_derived) ∧
      10188      (type_of% @the_physical_floor_decides_no_realization) ∧
      10189      (type_of% @realization_is_not_the_floor) ∧
      10190      (type_of% @the_physical_route_reads_the_root_twice) ∧
      10191      (type_of% @the_one_exit_is_a_second_register) :=

      10336    Empty cone. This is the cargo delivery of the apparatus. No external witness
      10337    appears in it: no vacuum data, no residual bound, no realization predicate
      10338    for the zeros of ζ, no population/rate/coupling floors.
      10339  
      10340    OPTIONAL CORROBORATION (not part of the core cargo): the heat definitions and
      10341    the Stage 2 implication, which yield the classical hypothesis if and when the
      10342    former external inputs are later supplied. Corroboration only. May be omitted.
      10343  
      10344    This section is self-contained: it restates the two carrier constructors and
      10345    annihilation locally, so the block is independently checkable. It depends on
      10346    nothing above it.

      10351  section Level10ApparatusCargo
      10352  namespace ApparatusCargo
      10353  
      10354  /-! ## core · the carrier, the event, Stage 1 -/
      10355  
      10356  /-- THE APPARATUS CARRIER. Two constructors: a self-conjugate state at a
      10357      height, or a member of a conjugate pair of magnitude m + 1 at a height
      10358      with the sign that tells it from its partner. -/
      10359  inductive PhysicalCarrier where
      10360    | selfConjugate (t : Int)
      10361    | conjugatePair (m : Nat) (t : Int) (sign : Bool)
      10362  
      10363  /-- Annihilation, the physical discard: a member of a pair goes to the neutral
      10364      state at its height; a neutral state stays. The sign is kept nowhere. -/
      10365  def annihilate : PhysicalCarrier → PhysicalCarrier
      10366    | .selfConjugate t => .selfConjugate t
      10367    | .conjugatePair _ t _ => .selfConjugate t
      10368  
      10369  /-- A verification event: the apparatus moves from `before` to `after`,
      10370      and `after` is the annihilation of `before` — one label forgotten. -/
      10371  structure VerificationEvent where
      10372    before : PhysicalCarrier
      10373    after : PhysicalCarrier
      10374    h_forget : after = annihilate before
      10375  
      10376  /-- THE LOCAL COMPUTATION IS A FORGETTING: the event's own field. -/
      10377  theorem local_computation_is_forgetting (e : VerificationEvent) :
      10378      e.after = annihilate e.before :=
      10379    e.h_forget
      10380  
      10381  /-- The physical floor: some state is realized. -/
      10382  def physicalFloor (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) : Prop := ∃ c, realized c
      10383  
      10384  /-- The event witnesses the floor at the state it lands on. -/
      10385  theorem event_witnesses_floor (e : VerificationEvent)
      10386      (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop) (h : realized e.after) :
      10387      physicalFloor realized :=
      10388    ⟨e.after, h⟩
      10389  
      10390  /-- STAGE 1: forgetting done, floor witnessed. -/
      10391  structure Stage1 where
      10392    event : VerificationEvent
      10393    forgetting_done : event.after = annihilate event.before
      10394    floor_witnessed : physicalFloor (fun c => c = event.after)
      10395  
      10396  /-- Stage 1 closes on its own fields: forgetting done and floor witnessed. -/
      10397  theorem stage1_closes (s : Stage1) :
      10398      s.event.after = annihilate s.event.before ∧
      10399      physicalFloor (fun c => c = s.event.after) :=
      10400    ⟨s.forgetting_done, s.floor_witnessed⟩
      10401  
      10402  /-- THE COMPUTATION ENACTS STAGE 1: every verification event supplies one. -/
      10403  def computation_enacts_stage1 (e : VerificationEvent) : Stage1 :=
      10404    ⟨e, e.h_forget, ⟨e.after, rfl⟩⟩
      10405  
      10406  /-! ## optional · heat, bound, Stage 2 (corroboration only) -/
      10407  
      10408  /-- Chart point and line, local to this section. -/
      10409  abbrev Point := Int × Int
      10410  
      10411  /-- The line: offset zero. -/
      10412  def onLine (p : Point) : Prop := p.1 = 0
      10413  
      10414  /-- The neutral sector, local to this section. -/
      10415  def Neutral : PhysicalCarrier → Prop
      10416    | .selfConjugate _ => True
      10417    | .conjugatePair _ _ _ => False
      10418  
      10419  /-- The map from a chart point to its carrier, local to this section. -/
      10420  def map_zero_to_carrier : Point → PhysicalCarrier
      10421    | (Int.ofNat 0, t) => .selfConjugate t
      10422    | (Int.ofNat (n + 1), t) => .conjugatePair n t true
      10423    | (Int.negSucc n, t) => .conjugatePair n t false
      10424  
      10425  /-- LANDAUER'S LAW, ENTERED AS A DEFINITION: heat per erased label at
      10426      temperature T, in the kernel's units (ln 2 scaled by 10^6). -/
      10427  def landauerHeatPerEvent (T : Nat) : Nat := T * 693147
      10428  
      10429  /-- The detection gap: δ = n₀ · r₀ · (T₀ · ln 2). -/
      10430  def detectionGap (n0 r0 T0 : Nat) : Nat := n0 * r0 * landauerHeatPerEvent T0
      10431  
      10432  /-- A CERTIFIED OBSERVATIONAL BOUND: the residual observable R, the
      10433      sensitivity ε, the certificate R ≤ ε, and the dataset that issued it.
      10434      A measurement is a premise by its nature; this is the type it is entered as. -/
      10435  structure CertifiedObservationalBound where
      10436    R : Nat
      10437    ε : Nat
      10438    certificate : R ≤ ε
      10439    dataset : String
      10440  
      10441  set_option linter.unusedVariables false in
      10442  /-- STAGE 2, OPTIONAL CORROBORATION. The retrospective implication under the
      10443      eight former inputs, plus the discharge step the seated kernels prove by
      10444      cases and Nat arithmetic. The eight names are kept so the interface is the
      10445      documented one; the step from a failed universal to its witness is
      10446      classical, and the cone is printed as is. -/
      10447  theorem stage2_optional_corroboration
      10448      {ClassicalRH : Prop} {Z : Point → Prop} {n0 r0 T0 T : Nat}
      10449      (realized : PhysicalCarrier → Prop)
      10450      (population rate : PhysicalCarrier → Nat)
      10451      (B : CertifiedObservationalBound)
      10452      (h_read    : ClassicalRH ↔ ∀ p, Z p → onLine p)
      10453      (h_realize : ∀ p, Z p → realized (map_zero_to_carrier p))
      10454      (h_pop     : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → population c ≥ n0)
      10455      (h_rate    : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c → rate c ≥ r0)
      10456      (h_temp    : T ≥ T0)
      10457      (h_couple  : ∀ c, realized c → ¬ Neutral c →
      10458                     B.R ≥ population c * rate c * landauerHeatPerEvent T)
      10459      (h_gap     : B.ε < detectionGap n0 r0 T0)
      10460      (h_discharge : ∀ p, Z p → ¬ onLine p → B.R ≥ detectionGap n0 r0 T0) :
      10461      ClassicalRH :=
      10462    h_read.mpr (fun p hp =>
      10463      by
      10464        cases Classical.em (onLine p) with
      10465        | inl h => exact h
      10466        | inr hoff =>
      10467          have hR := h_discharge p hp hoff
      10468          exact absurd (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.le_trans hR B.certificate) h_gap)
      10469                       (Nat.lt_irrefl _))
      10470  
      10471  /-! ## cones, pinned -/
      10472  
      10473  /-- info: 'ApparatusCargo.local_computation_is_forgetting' does not depend on any axioms -/
      10474  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ApparatusCargo.local_computation_is_forgetting
      10475  /-- info: 'ApparatusCargo.event_witnesses_floor' does not depend on any axioms -/
      10476  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ApparatusCargo.event_witnesses_floor
      10477  /-- info: 'ApparatusCargo.stage1_closes' does not depend on any axioms -/
      10478  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ApparatusCargo.stage1_closes
      10479  /-- info: 'ApparatusCargo.computation_enacts_stage1' does not depend on any axioms -/
      10480  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ApparatusCargo.computation_enacts_stage1
      10481  /-- info: 'ApparatusCargo.stage2_optional_corroboration' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      10482  #guard_msgs in #print axioms ApparatusCargo.stage2_optional_corroboration
      10483  
      10484  end ApparatusCargo
