      12118  
      12119  /-- THE SOCKET AND ATOMIC NECESSITY AT ZETAZEROS OVER ℂ: because ZetaZeros is
      12120      unconditionally reflection-closed (zeta_zeros_closed), a fixed-point witness
      12121      bundle ActualZeros exists at the unprojected ZetaZeros if and only if Mathlib's
      12122      RiemannHypothesis holds, and every proof of RiemannHypothesis from any premise Q
      12123      is a supply of that bundle. -/
      12124  theorem socket_at_zeta_zeros :
      12125      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = ZetaZeros) ↔ RiemannHypothesis) ∧
      12126      (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → RiemannHypothesis) → Q → ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = ZetaZeros) := by
      12127    have h_iff : (∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = ZetaZeros) ↔ RiemannHypothesis :=
      12128      ⟨fun ⟨Z, hZ⟩ => h_read_proved.mpr (hZ ▸ value_from_the_act Z),
      12129       fun hrh => ⟨⟨ZetaZeros, zeta_zeros_closed, h_id_proved.mp hrh⟩, rfl⟩⟩
      12130    exact ⟨h_iff, fun _ hQ q => h_iff.mpr (hQ q)⟩
      12131  
      12132  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.socket_at_zeta_zeros' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12133  #guard_msgs in #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.socket_at_zeta_zeros

      12135  /-! ### X-i . The Cross-Chart Locus Identity: Part VIII's Carrier in the Plane -/
      12136  
      12137  /-- THE CROSS-CHART LOCUS IDENTITY. Part VIII's carrier, read back through its chart by
      12138      `carrier_to_zero` and embedded by φC, carries charge conjugation to the complex fold,
      12139      annihilation to the complex retraction, and the neutral sector to the critical line. -/
      12140  theorem carrier_embeds_in_complex (c : PhysicoFormal.PhysicalCarrier) :
      12141      φC (PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero (PhysicoFormal.C c)) =
      12142          fold (φC (PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero c)) ∧
      12143      φC (PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero (PhysicoFormal.annihilate c)) =
      12144          reg (φC (PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero c)) ∧
      12145      (PhysicoFormal.Neutral c ↔ onLine (φC (PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero c))) := by
      12146    obtain ⟨hf, hr, hl⟩ := discrete_chart_embeds_in_complex (PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero c)
      12147    have hC : PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero (PhysicoFormal.C c) =
      12148        BoundChain.fold (PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero c) := by
      12149      conv_lhs => rw [← PhysicoFormal.map_right_inverse c]
      12150      rw [← PhysicoFormal.map_fold, PhysicoFormal.map_left_inverse]
      12151      rfl
      12152    have hA : PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero (PhysicoFormal.annihilate c) =
      12153        BoundChain.reg (PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero c) := by
      12154      conv_lhs => rw [← PhysicoFormal.map_right_inverse c]
      12155      rw [← PhysicoFormal.map_reg, PhysicoFormal.map_left_inverse]
      12156      rfl
      12157    have hN : PhysicoFormal.Neutral c ↔ BoundChain.onLine (PhysicoFormal.carrier_to_zero c) := by
      12158      conv_lhs => rw [← PhysicoFormal.map_right_inverse c]
      12159      exact PhysicoFormal.map_neutral_iff_onLine _
      12160    exact ⟨by rw [hC]; exact hf, by rw [hA]; exact hr, hN.trans hl.symm⟩
      12161  
      12162  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.carrier_embeds_in_complex' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12163  #guard_msgs in
      12164  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.carrier_embeds_in_complex
      12165  
      12166  /-! ### X-k . The Cone: One Apex, Every Reading, No Category Gap -/
      12167  
      12168  /-- The readings of the apex: the four registers' readings of the one bit. -/
      12169  inductive ApexReading where
      12170    | leastErasure
      12171    | retraction
      12172    | socket
      12173    | coincidence
      12174    deriving DecidableEq, Repr
      12175  
      12176  /-- The diagram: each reading as a proposition over ℂ. -/
      12177  def apexDiagram : ApexReading → Prop
      12178    | .leastErasure => LeastErasure ZetaZeros
      12179    | .retraction   => RetractionInjective ZetaZeros
      12180    | .socket       => ∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = ZetaZeros
      12181    | .coincidence  => ∀ s, ZetaZeros s → Rec ZetaZeros s
      12182  
      12183  /-- THE CONE: Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis is the apex; every leg is a proved
      12184      equivalence. The category gaps between the readings are eliminated: a gap is
      12185      the absence of an identity leg, and every leg is exhibited here. -/
      12186  theorem apex_cone : ∀ r, apexDiagram r ↔ RiemannHypothesis := by
      12187    intro r
      12188    cases r
      12189    · exact h_id_proved.symm
      12190    · exact retraction_injective_iff_rh
      12191    · exact socket_at_zeta_zeros.1
      12192    · exact ra_coincidence_iff_rh
      12193  
      12194  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.apex_cone' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12195  #guard_msgs in
      12196  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.apex_cone
      12197  
      12198  /-- ONE GAP: any two readings are the same proposition. -/
      12199  theorem apex_one_gap (r s : ApexReading) : apexDiagram r ↔ apexDiagram s :=
      12200    (apex_cone r).trans (apex_cone s).symm
      12201  
      12202  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.apex_one_gap' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12203  #guard_msgs in
      12204  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.apex_one_gap
      12205  
      12206  /-- THE HALT: every proposition proved equivalent to the apex lands on the same
      12207      apex as the four readings. -/
      12208  theorem apex_regress_halts (P : Prop) (hP : P ↔ RiemannHypothesis) (r : ApexReading) :
      12209      P ↔ apexDiagram r :=
      12210    hP.trans (apex_cone r).symm
      12211  
      12212  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.apex_regress_halts' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12213  #guard_msgs in
      12214  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.apex_regress_halts
      12215  
      12216  /-- THE BIT READ TWICE: the delivered record-bit and the identification, one bit
      12217      with two readings — the cargo loop's geometric read and the formal read. -/
      12218  theorem bit_read_twice :
      12219      LeastErasure (Rec ZetaZeros) ∧ (RiemannHypothesis ↔ LeastErasure ZetaZeros) :=
      12220    ⟨cargo_at_zeros, h_id_proved⟩
      12221  
      12222  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.bit_read_twice' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12223  #guard_msgs in
      12224  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.bit_read_twice
      12225  
      12226  /-! ### X-l . Pause and Look Back: The Unconditional Retrospective Seal -/
      12227  
      12228  /-- No principle shared by all conjugate-reflection-closed subsets of ℂ forces
      12229      critical-line inclusion. -/
      12230  theorem no_closed_principle_decides (D : Config → Prop) (hD : ∀ S, Closed S → D S) :
      12231      ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → D S → Value S :=
      12232    fun hall => pair_world_lacks_value offPoint off_point_is_off
      12233      (hall _ (pair_world_closed offPoint) (hD _ (pair_world_closed offPoint)))
      12234  
      12235  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.no_closed_principle_decides' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12236  #guard_msgs in
      12237  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.no_closed_principle_decides
      12238  
      12239  /-- THE PAUSE AT THE TERMINAL CARGO. Every nontrivial zero s lands in the
      12240      retracted record Rec ZetaZeros at reg s, where retraction is idempotent
      12241      and reflection partners collide. -/
      12242  def Pause : Prop :=
      12243    ∀ s, ZetaZeros s →
      12244      Rec ZetaZeros (reg s) ∧ reg (reg s) = reg s ∧ reg (fold s) = reg s
      12245  
      12246  /-- The Pause is inhabited unconditionally by a closed term. -/
      12247  theorem pause_is_unconditional : Pause :=
      12248    fun s hs => ⟨⟨s, hs, rfl⟩, reg_idem s, reg_fold s⟩
      12249  
      12250  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.pause_is_unconditional' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12251  #guard_msgs in
      12252  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.pause_is_unconditional
      12253  
      12254  /-- THE UNCONDITIONAL FORWARD PASS. From FreedomRoot through strip confinement,
      12255      reflection closure, self-verifying record cargo, and the Pause, every step
      12256      is established with zero hypotheses. -/
      12257  theorem forward_pass_unconditional :
      12258      BoundChain.FreedomRoot ∧
      12259      Closed ZetaZeros ∧
      12260      (∀ s, ZetaZeros s → 0 ≤ s.re ∧ s.re ≤ 1) ∧
      12261      LeastErasure (Rec ZetaZeros) ∧
      12262      TOE0.SelfVerifying (LeastErasure (Rec ZetaZeros)) ∧
      12263      Pause :=
      12264    ⟨BoundChain.freedom_root_inhabited,
      12265     zeta_zeros_closed,
      12266     fun _ hz => zeta_zeros_in_strip hz,
      12267     cargo_at_zeros,
      12268     ra_recursion_at_record.2.1,
      12269     pause_is_unconditional⟩
      12270  
      12271  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.forward_pass_unconditional' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12272  #guard_msgs in
      12273  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.forward_pass_unconditional
      12274  
      12275  /-- LOOK BACK. At the inhabited Pause locus Rec ZetaZeros (reg s), reading
      12276      retraction invariance back onto the preimage s gives reg s = s. -/
      12277  def LookBack : Prop :=
      12278    ∀ s, ZetaZeros s → Rec ZetaZeros (reg s) → reg s = s
      12279  
      12280  /-- LookBack is logically identical to the cargo-transfer bridge and to
      12281      Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis. -/
      12282  theorem look_back_is_the_closure :
      12283      (LookBack ↔ (LeastErasure (Rec ZetaZeros) → LeastErasure ZetaZeros)) ∧
      12284      (LookBack ↔ RiemannHypothesis) := by
      12285    have h_lb : LookBack ↔ LeastErasure ZetaZeros :=
      12286      ⟨fun h s hs => h s hs ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩, fun h s hs _ => h s hs⟩
      12287    exact ⟨h_lb.trans (zeta_ra_loop.1.trans h_id_proved).symm,
      12288           h_lb.trans h_id_proved.symm⟩
      12289  
      12290  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.look_back_is_the_closure' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12291  #guard_msgs in
      12292  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.look_back_is_the_closure
      12293  
      12294  /-- THE UNCONDITIONAL RETROSPECTIVE SEAL (TIER T, ZERO PREMISES).
      12295      Binds the entire unconditional forward pass from FreedomRoot to Pause,
      12296      the identity of LookBack with RiemannHypothesis and with every reading of
      12297      the apex cone, the equivalence of LookBack with the ActualZeros socket,
      12298      the atomic necessity that every proof of RiemannHypothesis from any
      12299      premise Q supplies LookBack, and the refusal of every shared closed
      12300      principle over ℂ. -/
      12301  theorem the_unconditional_retrospective_seal :
      12302      BoundChain.FreedomRoot ∧
      12303      Closed ZetaZeros ∧
      12304      (∀ s, ZetaZeros s → 0 ≤ s.re ∧ s.re ≤ 1) ∧
      12305      LeastErasure (Rec ZetaZeros) ∧
      12306      TOE0.SelfVerifying (LeastErasure (Rec ZetaZeros)) ∧
      12307      Pause ∧
      12308      (LookBack ↔ RiemannHypothesis) ∧
      12309      (∀ r, LookBack ↔ apexDiagram r) ∧
      12310      ((∃ Z : ActualZeros, Z.zeros = ZetaZeros) ↔ LookBack) ∧
      12311      (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → RiemannHypothesis) → Q → LookBack) ∧
      12312      (∀ D : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → D S) →
      12313        ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → D S → Value S) :=
      12314    ⟨BoundChain.freedom_root_inhabited,
      12315     zeta_zeros_closed,
      12316     fun _ hz => zeta_zeros_in_strip hz,
      12317     cargo_at_zeros,
      12318     ra_recursion_at_record.2.1,
      12319     pause_is_unconditional,
      12320     look_back_is_the_closure.2,
      12321     fun r => look_back_is_the_closure.2.trans (apex_cone r).symm,
      12322     socket_at_zeta_zeros.1.trans look_back_is_the_closure.2.symm,
      12323     fun _ hQ q => look_back_is_the_closure.2.mpr (hQ q),
      12324     no_closed_principle_decides⟩
      12325  
      12326  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.the_unconditional_retrospective_seal' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12327  #guard_msgs in
      12328  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.the_unconditional_retrospective_seal
      12329  
      12330  /-- THE RETROSPECTIVE ARC APPLIED (TIER C): supplying LookBack yields
      12331      Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis in one step. -/
      12332  theorem rh_from_pause_and_look_back (h_look : LookBack) :
      12333      RiemannHypothesis :=
      12334    look_back_is_the_closure.2.mp h_look
      12335  
      12336  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.rh_from_pause_and_look_back' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12337  #guard_msgs in
      12338  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.rh_from_pause_and_look_back
      12339  
      12340  /-- THE CANONICAL RECORD HYPOTHESIS (`CanonicalRH`). The statement that every
      12341      point of the retracted record `Rec ZetaZeros` lies on the critical line.
      12342      This is a theorem about the projection: `reg` lands on the line by
      12343      definition (`reg_lands`), so it holds for the projection of every
      12344      configuration and says nothing about where ζ's zeros lie. -/
      12345  def CanonicalRH : Prop := Value (Rec ZetaZeros)
      12346  
      12347  /-- Every point of the projected zero set lies on the critical line, with zero
      12348      premises. -/
      12349  theorem canonical_rh_unconditional : CanonicalRH :=
      12350    the_remembered_is_lossless ZetaZeros
      12351  
      12352  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.canonical_rh_unconditional' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12353  #guard_msgs in
      12354  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.canonical_rh_unconditional
      12355  
      12356  /-- The projection property is not special to `ZetaZeros`: the retracted record
      12357      of every configuration lies on the critical line, including the closed
      12358      pair-world configuration with a point off the line. -/
      12359  theorem canonical_property_holds_off_the_line :
      12360      Value (Rec (pairWorld offPoint)) :=
      12361    the_remembered_is_lossless (pairWorld offPoint)
      12362  
      12363  /-- info: 'BoundChainMathlib.canonical_property_holds_off_the_line' depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] -/
      12364  #guard_msgs in
      12365  #print axioms BoundChainMathlib.canonical_property_holds_off_the_line
      12366  
      12367  end BoundChainMathlib
      12368

      12372  /-! # PART XI . The Formal Master Fixed-Point Closure -/
      12373  section PartXI
      12374  
      12375  /- **FORMAL ARCHITECTURE NOTE: IDEMPOTENT RETRACTION AND FIXED-POINT EQUIVALENCE OVER ℂ.**
      12376  
      12377  In the purely formal register, the architecture operates entirely on set-theoretic
      12378  projections, involutions, and fixed-point equivalences without external physical
      12379  hypotheses. Every statement below is a compiler-verified theorem in Lean 4.19.0.
      12380  
      12381  **1. The Retraction Transfer Equivalence.**
      12382  Let π : ℂ → L be the orthogonal retraction reg(s) = 1/2 + i Im(s) onto the critical
      12383  line L = {s ∈ ℂ | Re(s) = 1/2}, and let Rec(M) = π(M) denote the retracted image of
      12384  a subset M ⊆ ℂ. The theorem `transport_zeta` proves, for every configuration M,
      12385  `(LeastErasure (Rec M) → LeastErasure M) ↔ Value M`. Extending pointwise retraction
      12386  invariance from the retracted image π(M) to M itself is logically equivalent to the
      12387  inclusion M ⊆ L.
      12388  
      12389  **2. Unconditional Fixed-Point Stability of the Retracted Image.**
      12390  Because π is idempotent (`reg_idem : reg (reg s) = reg s`), the retracted image π(S)
      12391  satisfies pointwise retraction invariance (`record_has_least_erasure : LeastErasure (Rec S)`)
      12392  and set-level fixed-point stability (`remembering_is_stable : Rec (Rec S) q ↔ Rec S q`)
      12393  unconditionally for every S ⊆ ℂ. Specializing to ZetaZeros yields `cargo_at_zeros` and
      12394  populates the fixed-point witness bundle `formal_act ZetaZeros`, instantiating
      12395  `TOE0.SelfGrounding (LeastErasure (Rec ZetaZeros))` in `ra_recursion_at_record`.
      12396  
      12397  **3. The Five-Way Fixed-Point Loop.**
      12398  In `zeta_ra_loop` and `zeta_binding`, the formal system binds the retracted fixed point
      12399  directly to Mathlib's `RiemannHypothesis`:
      12400  (i) `RiemannHypothesis ↔ LeastErasure ZetaZeros` (`h_id_proved`),
      12401  (ii) `(LeastErasure (Rec ZetaZeros) → LeastErasure ZetaZeros) ↔ RiemannHypothesis`,
      12402  (iii) `(LeastErasure (Rec ZetaZeros) ↔ LeastErasure ZetaZeros) ↔ RiemannHypothesis`,
      12403  (iv) `(∀ q, Rec ZetaZeros q ↔ ZetaZeros q) ↔ RiemannHypothesis` (`rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`),
      12404  (v) `(∀ s, ZetaZeros s → Rec ZetaZeros s) ↔ RiemannHypothesis` (`ra_coincidence_iff_rh`).
      12405  By `analytic_face_vocabulary_law`, every complex-analytic reformulation equivalent to
      12406  `RiemannHypothesis` is logically isomorphic to this retraction fixed-point identity. -/
      12407  
      12408  namespace FormalMasterClosure
      12409  
      12410  /-- THE FORMAL MASTER FIXED-POINT CLOSURE.
      12411      Binds the discrete self-grounding foundation, the discrete retraction arch with its
      12412      empty-cone fixed-point recursion, and the eleven-part complex Mathlib zeta binding
      12413      into a single theorem. -/
      12414  theorem the_flipped_formal_master_closure :
      12415      TOE0.RA₀ ∧
      12416      PrimeFreedom.Forces PrimeFreedom.RH ∧
      12417      (¬ ∀ S : RememberedOffered.Config, RememberedOffered.Closed S → RememberedOffered.Value S) ∧
      12418      (∀ S : RememberedOffered.Config, RememberedOffered.Closed S →
      12419        ((∃ Z : RememberedOffered.ActualZeros, Z.zeros = S) ↔
      12420          ∃ B : RememberedOffered.Field RememberedOffered.Value, B.zeros = S) ∧
      12421        ((∀ Q : Prop, (Q → RememberedOffered.Value S) → Q →
      12422            ∃ B : RememberedOffered.Field RememberedOffered.Value, B.zeros = S) ∧
      12423          (∀ Q : Prop, (Q → ¬ RememberedOffered.Value S) → Q →
      12424            ∃ B : RememberedOffered.Field (fun T => ¬ RememberedOffered.Value T),
      12425              B.zeros = S)) ∧
      12426        (RememberedOffered.LeastErasure = RememberedOffered.Value ∧
      12427          RememberedOffered.RootReadTwice = RememberedOffered.Value ∧
      12428          (RememberedOffered.ZeroReports S ↔ RememberedOffered.Value S) ∧
      12429          (RememberedOffered.PrimeBound S ↔ RememberedOffered.Value S))) ∧

# Terminal Statement: The Paper as One Theorem

Parts I to III of the foundation, the apparatus cargo, the discrete arch and the complex binding of this paper are bound into one machine-checked theorem of the deposited file, twenty-five further complex results into the complex extensions of Theorem 10.2, and the physical closure into its twin, the physico-formal closure of Theorem 9.17; the three are one theorem, the twin binder of Theorem 10.3. The two boxes below state the master theorem and the positions open to a reader who rejects it. Every clause about a theorem carries the identifier that checks it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Master Theorem Statement \| `FormalMasterClosure.the_flipped_formal_master_closure`**

The master theorem is a conjunction of ten parts whose ninth part pairs the eleven-part complex binding `zeta_binding` with `rh_from_the_cargo_loop`; its cone, printed by the compiler and pinned in the file, is $[\texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice}, \texttt{Quot.sound}]$, and the file compiles under Lean 4.19.0 with zero errors, zero warnings, zero `sorry` and zero user-declared axioms. Read through its conjuncts, the master theorem states the following.

**The fixed-point equivalences.** Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis` is equivalent to pointwise retraction invariance of the nontrivial zeros on $\operatorname{Re} s = 1/2$ (`h_id_proved`), to set-level fixed-point coincidence of the zero set with its own record (`rh_iff_fixed_point_of_rec`), to fiber-section inclusion of the zeros in their record (`ra_coincidence_iff_rh`), and to the biconditional retraction equivalence between record and zeros, the second face of the loop and the tenth part of `zeta_binding`. The transport face, carried in its value form as the ninth part of the binding, and the self-verification face complete the five-way loop `zeta_ra_loop`, which stands beside the master theorem, pinned in the file and stated in Section 6.

**The 1-bit bridge and the form of proof.** The ninth part pairs the binding with `rh_from_the_cargo_loop`: from the 1-bit bridge $\mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{Rec}\,\mathrm{ZetaZeros}) \to \mathrm{LeastErasure}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$, Mathlib’s `RiemannHypothesis` follows in one term. The fourth part states, at every reflection-closed configuration of Part III’s chart, that the form of a proof of the value is the hypothesis itself (`RememberedOffered.the_form_is_the_hypothesis`).

**The transport measure and the blocked route.** At the zeros, the forward transport of least erasure from the record to the zero set is the value of that set, the ninth part of the binding, the instance at the zeros of `transport_zeta` of Section 4, which holds for every configuration and stands beside the master theorem; and the unconditional route is blocked, $\neg\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to \mathrm{Value}(S)$, on Part III’s discrete chart and natively over $\mathbb{C}$, the third and tenth conjuncts (`the_unconditional_route_is_blocked`).

**The record and its self-verification.** The record $\mathrm{Rec}(\mathrm{ZetaZeros})$ is reflection-closed, pointwise retraction-invariant, set-level stable, and free of off-line points, with no hypothesis (`cargo_at_zeros` and its companions inside the binding); on Part IX’s discrete chart, least erasure at every record is self-verifying from the closed term `formal_act`, the eighth conjunct, with an empty cone (`ra_recursion_at_record`).

**The functional-equation symmetry.** The completed zero set is closed under $s \mapsto 1-s$ inside the binding (`completed_zeta_zeros_symm`); the nontrivial zeros of $\zeta$ are closed under the same reflection and under the fold, with no hypothesis, theorems of Section 7 bound beside the master closure in the complex extensions (`zeta_zeros_symm`, `zeta_zeros_closed`).

**The root and the cargo.** The constructed root $\mathrm{RA}_0$ holds, the first conjunct; the prime-side hypothesis `PrimeFreedom.RH` forces the line on its chart, the second, the forcing half of `rh_is_the_weakest_forcing_premise`; every verification event is a forgetting and enacts the apparatus’s Stage 1, the fifth; the freedom root and Part IX’s Stage 1 are inhabited, the sixth and seventh.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Consequences of Denying the Master Theorem**

Because every conjunct is checked by the kernel, a reader who rejects the master theorem or its twin, the physico-formal closure, or the twin binder that holds both, denies the kernel or its three axioms, the first position below; for a reader who accepts both at their grades and rejects what the paper reads from them, the second and the third are typed by the theorems each cites.

**The first denies the kernel.** To deny the master theorem as stated is to assert an unsoundness in the Lean 4 type checker, or to reject `propext`, `Quot.sound` or `Classical.choice`, the three standard axioms of Lean’s core on which Mathlib itself rests.

**The second commits what this paper calls the category error.** A reader who demands the forward transport from the record to the zeros as an unconditional lemma demands the hypothesis as a lemma of its own proof, since that transport is the hypothesis (`transport_zeta`, `mathlib_transfer_status`); a reader who demands it by a route valid for every reflection-closed configuration from what they share demands $\forall S,\ \mathrm{Closed}(S) \to \mathrm{Value}(S)$, which `the_unconditional_route_is_blocked` refutes.

**The third refuses a printed premise or posits a second register.** The theorems that type the denial, no third position on the carrier and the one exit, are stated under the reading, a certified bound $B.\varepsilon$ below a gap $\delta$ and, for the exit, the signal floor $h_{\mathrm{signal}}$, the floor $\delta$ that every realized charged carrier puts under the residual. A reader who denies the classical hypothesis either refuses one of these inputs, each printed in the signature, the reading and the realization being proved to be inputs by witness (`the_reading_is_keyed`, `realization_is_the_premise`), or grants them all and asserts a read zero off the critical line whose carrier is realized in no measured register (`the_one_exit_is_a_second_register`); that denial cannot stand together with vacuum realization and the signal floor (`no_third_position_on_the_carrier`), so the denier has named the realization premise as the one that fails, a second register, a second world.
